title: Practical Social Media Marketing: Grow an Account, Run Campaigns, Get Clients
summary: Grow a real account with measured results, run a real campaign for a local business, and finish with a portfolio, a service package and a price sheet, using free tools on an Android phone. Malayalam and English, Kerala examples, rupee numbers and copy-ready templates throughout. Part-time: 40 weeks at about 6 hours a week. Full-time: about 14 weeks.

sections.title: Start here: how this course works
sections.summary: What you will build, how long it takes, honest growth expectations, how every lesson works and the assumptions behind the course.
sections.content:
## What this course is

A free, practical course in social media marketing, built for Kerala. You learn by doing it for real: you grow your own account from zero, run a no-cost campaign for a real local business, and finish with a portfolio, a service package and a price sheet you can show to clients or employers.

It is written for a beginner near Kuttiady in Kozhikode district who is preparing for Kerala PSC exams, has an Android phone and an old laptop, and has ₹0 to spend on learning. Content is made in Malayalam and English. It works just as well for anyone in a similar situation.

Platforms change fast, so every platform fact in this course is marked with the date it was checked: **as of October 2026**. The lessons teach principles that survive algorithm changes, and they show you where to check the current rules.

## By the end you will have

- A real account grown from zero, with 40 weeks of posting logged and a 90-day growth project measured from start to finish
- Three case studies with before and after numbers: your 30-day challenge, a 4-week pilot for a real local business, and your 90-day growth project
- Three written audits of real local businesses
- A client-ready portfolio site, a service package and a price sheet
- A complete toolkit of templates, built one module at a time

## How long it takes

| Pace | Calendar time | Hours a week | Total work |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Part-time (the default) | Week 0, then 40 weeks: about 9.5 months | About 6 | About 211 hours |
| Full-time | About 14 weeks | About 17, posting every day | About 211 hours |

Pick your pace and start date on the course page; the app then shows which week you are in and what is due. The hours are honest estimates.

**Why so long?** Growth takes real days. The 30-day challenge, the 4-week pilot and the 90-day growth project can't be rushed, even on the full-time pace. The full-time schedule shows how they overlap with the later modules.

## Honest expectations about growth

- **Most new accounts grow slowly at first.** Expect weeks where a post gets a few dozen views. That is normal, not failure.
- **Growth is lumpy.** One post may do ten times better than the rest, then views drop again. Judge your progress by monthly trends, not single posts.
- **You control inputs, not outputs.** You decide how often you post, how good your hooks are and how fast you learn from your numbers. The platform decides who sees each post.
- **Followers are not the goal.** Clients pay for enquiries, bookings and sales. This course tracks those from Module 2 onwards.
- **There are no shortcuts.** Bought followers, engagement groups and fake reviews break platform rules, can break Indian consumer law and ruin your account (Module 14).

This course never invents statistics. Where a number comes from a platform or a study, the source is linked. The people, businesses and numbers in the examples are made up to show how the methods work.

## How each lesson works

Every lesson has the same parts, in this order:

1. **ID, title, outcome and time** at the top of the page, such as SMM-M01-L01
2. **Core lesson:** the idea, explained simply, with platform facts dated
3. **Local example:** the idea applied in or near Kuttiady, with rupee numbers
4. **Free resources:** exactly what to study, how long it takes and when the link was checked
5. **Action task:** real work on your account or for a real business, and the **proof to record**
6. **Template:** copy-ready calendars, scripts, formulas, checklists and reports
7. **Common mistakes** and how to avoid them
8. **Quiz:** 3 to 5 questions, with the answers at the very bottom
9. **Progress checklist:** the ticks under **Your tasks**

Each module starts with an overview page: outcomes, total time, the module project, a self-assessment rubric, a "short on time?" version and revision flashcards.

## How to use the app for this course

- Tick each task under **Your tasks** when it is done. Ticks are saved on this phone, so save a backup now and then from **Backup and courses**.
- Paste the link to your proof (a post, a Google Drive file or a screenshot) into the task's note.
- **This week**, on the course page, lists what is due, plus your next posting checkpoint.
- Exam coming? Use exam mode (in the weekly schedule) and move your start date later so the weeks match. Your ticks are kept.

## Module map

| Module | Part-time weeks | What you do | Output for your toolkit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Foundations | 1–2 | How platforms rank content, the funnel, career paths; your practice account goes live | Starter plan and baseline |
| 2. Strategy | 3–4 | Goals, audience research, personas, niche, competitors, pillars, voice | One-page social media strategy |
| 3. Platforms in depth | 5–7 | Instagram, YouTube, Facebook, WhatsApp Business, LinkedIn, X, Threads, Telegram, Indian apps | Platform plan and optimised profiles |
| 4. Content creation | 8–11 | Hooks, scripts, Malayalam and English, shooting and editing on the phone, design | Phone content pack |
| 5. Copywriting | 12–13 | Headlines, captions, calls to action, honest persuasion, writing for each platform | Caption bank |
| 6. Content systems | 14–18 | Calendars, batching, repurposing, scheduling, templates, the 30-day challenge | Content system and 30 days of posts |
| 7. Growth | 16–18 | Social SEO, hashtags, YouTube search, trends, collaborations, community, DMs | Growth experiments |
| 8. Analytics | 19–21 | Metrics, insights, Google Analytics, UTM links, A/B tests, reports | Case study 1: your 30-day challenge |
| 9. Paid ads | 22–24 | Boosting vs Ads Manager, targeting, small budgets, testing, retargeting, ROI | Ad plan and optional test ad |
| 10. Influencer and creator marketing | 25–26 | Micro-influencers, UGC, affiliate links, creator income | Influencer brief and creator money plan |
| 11. Local business and social commerce | 27–32 | Google Business Profile, selling on WhatsApp and Instagram, reviews, events, audits, a real pilot | Three audits and case study 2: the pilot |
| 12. Personal branding | 29–31 | Your authority online, portfolio and case studies | Portfolio site |
| 13. AI for social media | 33–34 | AI for ideas, scripts, captions, images, video, analytics, and its risks | AI playbook |
| 14. Ethics, law and safety | 34–36 | Disclosure rules, copyright, music, consent, honest growth, crises, security | Compliance and safety kit |
| 15. Earning |  | Packages, pricing, clients, proposals, contracts, onboarding, reports, agency | Sales kit |
| 16. Creator wellbeing |  | Burnout, comparison, trolls and harassment | Wellbeing plan |
| 17. Capstone |  | A 90-day growth project, client-ready portfolio, service package and price sheet | Case study 3, portfolio, price sheet |

## Key assumptions

These decisions were made for you when the course was written. Change them if your situation is different.

1. **Pace:** part-time, about 6 hours a week next to PSC study. The full-time pace does the same work in about 14 weeks.
2. **Money:** learning costs ₹0. The only optional spend is a tiny test ad in Module 9 (₹300–₹1,000, or a ₹0 dry run). A cheap clip-on microphone (Module 4) is optional too.
3. **Devices:** an Android phone does almost everything. The old laptop is for spreadsheets, longer writing and, if it copes, desktop-only tools such as YouTube's title and thumbnail tests.
4. **Practice account:** by default a hyperlocal page about your area, in Malayalam with English captions: local shops, food, events and useful updates. It gives you endless content nearby, grows faster with a local audience, introduces you to future clients and becomes your portfolio. Module 1 lets you choose another niche or your own brand instead.
5. **Main platforms:** Instagram and YouTube Shorts for growth, WhatsApp Business for local selling, LinkedIn for your career. Module 3 helps you confirm or change this.
6. **The pilot:** a free 4-week pilot for a real local business in Module 11, in exchange for permission to use the results as a case study.
7. **Facts and rules** were checked on 2026-10-25. Platform features, limits and policies change often. Anything marked **check current rules** links to the official source; check it before you act, and before you advise a client.
8. **Not legal or tax advice.** The course explains Indian rules simply. For contracts, GST and disputes, ask a qualified professional.
9. **Every resource is free.** A few need a free sign-up (Meta Blueprint, HubSpot Academy, Canva, Google Skillshop).

## The running examples (all made up)

- **Anu**, a PSC aspirant from Kakkattil, runs the practice page **@kuttiady.diaries** and takes this course at the part-time pace.
- **Nisha's Oven**, a home bakery in Kuttiady (you may know her from the Entrepreneurship course)
- **Malabar Mobiles**, a phone shop with a repair counter in Kuttiady town
- **Kakkayam Hills Homestay**, a three-room homestay near Kakkayam
- **Peak Fitness**, a gym in Vatakara
- **Amma's Pickles**, a Kudumbashree pickle unit in Perambra
- **Fathima's PSC Sprint**, a Malayalam YouTube channel for PSC practice
- **Arun's ShopAssist**, a freelancer who sets up WhatsApp Business and Google profiles for shops

## Other courses in this app

This course links to two others instead of repeating them:

- **Practical Entrepreneurship** for positioning (ENT-M06-L01), pricing (ENT-M05-L03), sales conversations (Module 7), GST and tax (ENT-M08-L03) and contracts (ENT-M09-L03)
- **Free AI Generalist Course** for prompting (Level 1), AI images, video and voice (Level 3) and automation (Level 4)

| 14 | 37–40 | — | Pilot results report, capstone report, portfolio and price sheet. Your growth project now covers about 78 days. |

## A weekly rhythm that fits around PSC study

- **Weekdays:** 40–50 minutes after your PSC study block, not before it, so the exam keeps your best hours. Reply to comments for 10 minutes, then do the lesson.
- **Saturday:** a 2-hour batch session: script, shoot and edit the coming week's posts.
- **Sunday:** 30 minutes to fill in Weekly Stats and decide one thing to change next week.
- **Full-time:** mornings for creating and client work, afternoons for lessons, 15 minutes at the end of the day for numbers.

## When you fall behind

- **This week** shows earlier open tasks as overdue. Do the action tasks and your posts first; readings can wait.
- More than two weeks behind? Set a new start date on the course page so the weeks match your real progress. Your ticks are kept.
- Use each module's "short on time?" version when you need it.

## Exam mode

In the four weeks before a PSC exam: post twice a week from posts you batched earlier, reply to comments, and pause the lessons. Move your start date later by the same number of weeks. Your account keeps its rhythm, and the course waits for you.

sections.title: Week 0: free toolkit, practice account and rules from day 1
sections.summary: Free tools, one Drive folder, one workbook, a practice account with two-step verification, and the rules that apply from your first post.
sections.content:
Week 0 takes about 4 hours, including the baseline self-assessment on the next page. You set up free tools once, so every lesson has a place to save its work, and your practice account goes live.

## 1. An SMM Toolkit folder in Google Drive

Make a folder called **SMM Toolkit** with these subfolders: 00 Baseline, 01 Foundations, 02 Strategy, 03 Platforms, 04 Content, 05 Copy, 06 Systems, 07 Growth, 08 Analytics, 09 Ads, 10 Influencers, 11 Local business, 12 Portfolio, 13 AI, 14 Compliance, 15 Sales, 16 Wellbeing, 17 Capstone. Every lesson's proof goes into one of them. When a task asks for proof, copy the file's or post's link and paste it into the task's note in this app.

## 2. The SMM Workbook

Make one Google Sheets file called **SMM Workbook** with nine tabs: Posting Log, Weekly Stats, Ideas, Calendar, Hooks and Captions, Competitors, Experiments, Leads and Clients, and Pilot. Put each tab's header row (below) in row 1.

- **On the laptop:** copy a header line, paste it into cell A1, then choose Data → Split text to columns.
- **On the phone:** type the headings into row 1, or do this step once on the laptop.

```csv
Posting Log:
Date,Platform,Format,Pillar,Topic,Hook (first line),Language (ML/EN/both),Link,Views after 24 h,Views after 7 days,Accounts reached,Likes,Comments,Shares,Saves,Follows,Profile visits,Link clicks or DMs,Average watch % or time,Notes

Weekly Stats:
Week,Start date,Followers at start,Followers at end,Posts,Total views,Accounts reached,Interactions,Profile visits,Link clicks,Enquiries (DMs/calls),What I will change

Ideas:
Date,Idea,Pillar,Format,Hook idea,Source (comment/search/trend/own),Score 1-5,Used on (date)

Calendar:
Date,Day,Platform,Format,Pillar,Topic,Hook,Call to action,Status (idea/scripted/shot/edited/scheduled/posted),Link

Hooks and Captions:
Type,English,Malayalam,Used on,Result

Competitors:
Account,Platform,Followers,Posts a week,Best format,Top 3 posts (topic and views),What they do well,Gap I can fill

Experiments:
Start date,Hypothesis,Change tested,Metric,Before,After,Result,Decision

Leads and Clients:
Business,Contact person,Phone (with consent),Area,Source,Stage,Last contact,Next step,Next date,Offer,Value (Rs),Notes

Pilot:
Week,Posts,Views,Accounts reached,Profile visits,Calls,WhatsApp chats,Direction requests or visits,Orders or bookings,Revenue (Rs) if shared,Notes
```

The Posting Log is the heart of the course. Every post you publish gets a row, with its numbers after 24 hours and after 7 days.

## 3. Get your phone ready

- **Free up space:** at least 5 GB free, so videos don't fail to save. Move old photos to Google Photos or the laptop.
- **Install now:** [Canva](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.canva.editor), [Snapseed](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.niksoftware.snapseed), [YouTube Studio](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.apps.youtube.creator), Google Sheets and Google Drive. You'll add a video editor in Module 4 and WhatsApp Business and Meta Business Suite in Module 3.
- **Malayalam typing:** add Malayalam to Gboard ([how to](https://support.google.com/gboard/answer/7068494)), or install the free, open-source [Indic Keyboard](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.smc.inputmethod.indic), which can turn Manglish typing into Malayalam script.

## 4. Your practice account

Choose a provisional niche now; you'll test and refine it in Module 2. The default is a **hyperlocal page about your area**: "Kuttiady diaries: local food, shops, events and useful updates, in Malayalam". Other good options: a hobby you know well, Kerala PSC study tips, or your own brand as a social media marketer.

1. Pick a handle that is short, easy to spell in English and free on Instagram and YouTube (search for it on both).
2. Create a **new** Instagram account for the page (not your personal one) and switch it to a professional account, choosing **Creator** ([Instagram Help: professional accounts](https://help.instagram.com/502981923235522)). Professional accounts get insights and are public, which the recommendation system needs.
3. Create a YouTube channel with the same name and handle from the YouTube app or YouTube Studio.
4. Add a profile photo (a simple logo or a clear local photo you took) and a one-line bio. You will improve it in Module 3.

## 5. Turn on two-step verification

Do this before your first post. Use Google's [2-Step Verification](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/185839) for the Google account behind YouTube (Google recommends its prompts, or a passkey, over SMS codes), and turn on two-factor authentication in Instagram's Accounts Centre security settings. Save the backup codes in a safe place offline. Module 14 covers account security in depth.

## 6. Rules from day 1

These protect you, the people you post about, and your future clients. Each one is explained fully in Module 14, but they apply from your first post:

- **Only post what you have the right to post.** Your own photos and videos, or music from the app's own library. Never download photos from Google or film songs from YouTube to use in your posts.
- **Ask before you film or photograph people,** and before you post a shop, its staff or its customers. For children, ask a parent, and when in doubt leave them out.
- **Say when something is paid or free.** If a shop gives you a free meal, a discount or money to post about it, the post must say so clearly, for example "Ad" or "Free gift" (Module 14 explains the Indian rules).
- **No fake engagement.** Never buy followers, likes, views or reviews, and don't join "engagement groups". It breaks platform rules and can get your account restricted.
- **Check before you share local news.** A wrong post about an accident, a strike or a shop closing can hurt real people. When unsure, don't post.
- **Stay away from politics, religion and communal topics** on your practice page. Arguments there can bring trolls, reports and real-life trouble.
- **Keep your accounts safe:** two-step verification on, a password you use nowhere else, and never share login codes with anyone, even "Meta support".

## 7. An AI assistant as your coach

The free plans of [Gemini](https://gemini.google/subscriptions/), [ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/pricing) and [Claude](https://claude.com/pricing) are enough for this course (limits change; check current rules). Save this prompt and paste it at the start of a session:

```
You are my social media marketing coach. I live near
Kuttiady, Kozhikode, Kerala. I am a beginner taking a
practical course, about 6 hours a week, next to Kerala
PSC exam prep. I make content in Malayalam and English.
Rules for you:
1. Ask me one question at a time.
2. Push me to post, test and look at real numbers
   instead of guessing.
3. Use rupee examples and Kerala context.
4. If you are not sure about a platform feature, rule or
   number, say so and tell me to check the official help
   page. Platform rules change often.
5. Never suggest fake followers, fake reviews, copied
   content or hidden paid promotions.
6. Don't write everything for me; improve what I write.
Today I am working on: [lesson ID and task].
```

Never paste a client's private details, customers' phone numbers or your passwords into an AI tool. Module 13 covers AI properly.

## 8. Your calendar and a buddy

Block your weekly slots in Google Calendar, including the Saturday batch session and the Sunday review. Choose an accountability buddy: a friend who will ask you every Sunday, "How many posts this week, and what did you learn from the numbers?"

Every link on this page was checked on 2026-10-25. The **Sources and verification log** at the end of the course lists each one with its status.

sections.title: Baseline self-assessment (you repeat it at the end)
sections.summary: Rate 20 skills, record your account's starting numbers and write why you are doing this. You take the same assessment in week 40.
sections.content:
Before you start, record where you are. You'll take exactly the same self-assessment in week 40 and compare. Be honest: low scores now make your progress visible later. It takes about 30 minutes.

## Part 1: rate 20 skills from 1 to 5

| Score | Means |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Never heard of it, or can't do it |
| 2 | Understand it, but haven't done it |
| 3 | Can do it with help or a guide open |
| 4 | Can do it alone, reliably |
| 5 | Can teach it and do it for a client |

Copy this table into a new tab called **Baseline** in your SMM Workbook. Fill in the **Start** column now; leave **End** for week 40.

| No | Skill | Start (week 0) | End (week 40) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Explain how recommendation systems decide what people see |  |  |
| 2 | Turn a business goal into a social media objective and a KPI |  |  |
| 3 | Describe a target audience from real research, not guesses |  |  |
| 4 | Choose the right platform and format for a goal |  |  |
| 5 | Write a hook that stops the scroll, in Malayalam and English |  |  |
| 6 | Shoot a clear, well-lit video with clean sound on a phone |  |  |
| 7 | Edit a short video on a phone, with captions and licensed music |  |  |
| 8 | Design a readable carousel or YouTube thumbnail |  |  |
| 9 | Write a caption with a clear call to action and no hype |  |  |
| 10 | Plan and batch a week of content |  |  |
| 11 | Use keywords and hashtags so people can find your posts |  |  |
| 12 | Read Instagram and YouTube insights and decide what to change |  |  |
| 13 | Make a UTM link and read the result in Google Analytics |  |  |
| 14 | Plan and run a small, measured paid ad test |  |  |
| 15 | Work with a creator and disclose the partnership correctly |  |  |
| 16 | Audit a local business's social media and recommend fixes |  |  |
| 17 | Follow Indian disclosure, copyright and consent rules |  |  |
| 18 | Handle negative comments and secure an account |  |  |
| 19 | Price, propose and report on a social media service |  |  |
| 20 | Protect your energy and deal with trolls |  |  |

## Part 2: your account's starting numbers

Write these in the same tab. For a brand-new account most will be 0, and that's fine: a zero baseline makes the clearest before and after.

```
ACCOUNT BASELINE (date: ____)
Handle and platforms: ____
Followers: Instagram ____  YouTube ____  other ____
Posts so far: ____
Average views of your last 9 posts: ____ (0 if none)
Accounts reached in the last 30 days: ____
Profile visits in the last 30 days: ____
Enquiries or DMs about anything you promote: ____
```

## Part 3: three sentences

1. Why I am doing this course: ____
2. What I want to be able to do by week 40: ____
3. What usually stops me finishing things, and my plan for it: ____

Save a screenshot of the Baseline tab in **00 Baseline**.

sections.title: Posting track: post on a schedule all course
sections.summary: Post on a schedule from week 1 to week 39, log every post and review your numbers weekly. Ten checkpoints keep you on track.
sections.content:
Your account is the course's main practice ground. You post on a schedule from week 1 to week 39, log every post, and look at the numbers every Sunday. **This week** on the course page shows one checkpoint at a time.

## How often to post

| Weeks | Part-time rhythm | What it is for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1–4 | 2 posts a week, at least one short video | Build the habit; your early posts are your "before" |
| 5–13 | 3 posts a week | Use each new skill from Modules 3–5 in a real post |
| 14–18 | Every day: the 30-day challenge (SMM-M06-L04) | Volume, speed and lots of data |
| 19–26 | 3 posts a week | Apply what the challenge numbers taught you |
| 27–39 | Your 90-day sprint plan, usually 4 a week (SMM-M17-L01) | A focused, measured growth project |

**Full-time:** post every day from week 1. **Exam weeks:** two batched posts a week (see the weekly schedule).

Stories, Status updates and replies don't count as posts here, but do them too; they keep your existing audience close.

## What counts as a post

A Reel, a Short, a carousel, a photo post, a LinkedIn post or a YouTube video that is public on your practice account, that you made yourself and that follows the rules from day 1. Re-posting other people's content doesn't count, and platforms rank it lower anyway ([Instagram says](https://creators.instagram.com/blog/instagram-recommendations-eligibility-tips-creators) it recommends original content).

## Log every post

Fill in a Posting Log row when you publish, then add the views after 24 hours and after 7 days. Every Sunday, add a Weekly Stats row and write one thing you'll change. This takes 10–15 minutes a week and is the most valuable habit in the course: it turns posting into learning.

## Checkpoints

| Due by week | Checkpoint | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3 | at least 5 posts published and logged | Links to the posts and the Posting Log rows |
| 6 | 6 more posts, two of them after your profile was optimised | Posting Log rows for weeks 4–6 |
| 9 | 9 more posts, including your first phone-shot Reel or Short | Posting Log rows and the Reel or Short link |
| 13 | 12 more posts and four Weekly Stats rows | Posting Log and Weekly Stats rows |
| 21 | 9 more posts after the challenge, still on schedule | Posting Log rows for weeks 19–21 |
| 24 | 9 more posts; one used as an ad or ad test | Posting Log rows for weeks 22–24 |
| 27 | 9 more posts; your 90-day sprint has started | Posting Log rows and your sprint plan |
| 30 | posts on plan, first sprint experiment logged | Posting Log, Weekly Stats and Experiments rows |
| 33 | posts on plan, second experiment logged | Posting Log, Weekly Stats and Experiments rows |
| 36 | posts on plan, third experiment logged | Posting Log, Weekly Stats and Experiments rows |

The 30-day challenge (weeks 14–18) and the end of the 90-day sprint (week 39) are tracked in their lessons, SMM-M06-L04 and SMM-M17-L01.

## When a checkpoint is missed

Missing one is information, not failure. Ask why: too ambitious a format, no batch session, exam pressure, or a topic you dislike? Fix that one thing, then catch up by batching two weeks of simple posts on one Saturday.

sections.title: Module 1: Foundations
sections.summary: Learn how platforms decide what people see, how social media fits the path from stranger to customer, and what careers it can lead to. Your practice account starts posting this week.
sections.content:
## Overview

Most beginners start by copying what's trending. This module starts one step earlier: understanding why some posts spread and others don't, so you can make good decisions when the platforms change. You'll study the platforms' own explanations, watch your own feed like a researcher, map real customer journeys, and research real jobs and client requests in your area.

By the end of week 2 your practice account is live with its first posts, and you have a one-page starter plan and the baseline numbers your growth will be measured against.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Explain how recommendation systems use signals such as watch time, shares and satisfaction
- Map a customer's journey through the funnel and pick the right number for each stage
- Describe six career paths and the skills real listings ask for
- Choose and justify a practice niche
- Publish and log your first posts

## Time

About 9 hours in total: 7 hours 30 minutes of lessons and 1 hour 30 minutes for the module project. Part-time: weeks 1–2.

## Lessons

1. SMM-M01-L01: How social platforms and recommendation systems work (about 3 hours)
2. SMM-M01-L02: The marketing funnel and the customer journey (about 2 hours)
3. SMM-M01-L03: Career paths, your goal and your practice account (about 2 hours 30 minutes)

## Module project: Your starter plan and baseline snapshot

1. Write a one-page starter plan: your path, your goals for weeks 13, 26 and 40, your practice niche and why, your main platforms for now (default: Instagram and YouTube Shorts), and your weekly time slots.
2. Add your account baseline from Week 0 and today's numbers after your first posts.
3. Plan your next 5 posts: topic, format and hook for each.
4. Publish at least 3 posts in weeks 1–2 and log them in the Posting Log.
5. Send your plan to your accountability buddy and agree when they will check on you.

**Proof to record:** Your one-page starter plan and the links to at least 3 published, logged posts.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3. If a row is a 1, redo that part first.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Algorithm understanding | Can't explain why a post spreads | Can name some signals | Can explain signals and five lasting principles in own words |
| Funnel thinking | Judges every post by likes | Knows the stages | Gives each post a job and the right number to watch |
| Career clarity | No path or goals | A path but vague goals | A path, dated goals and skills from 10 real listings |
| Practice account | Not set up | Set up, unclear niche | Live, clear one-line bio, niche scored and chosen |
| Posting habit | No posts | 1–2 posts | 3 or more posts, all logged |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, when PSC prep or work leaves little time:

- Read the YouTube and Instagram pages from SMM-M01-L01 (about 25 minutes).
- Keep the feed diary for one day instead of three.
- Map one customer journey instead of two.
- Publish 2 posts and log them. Skip the niche scorecard if your niche is already clear.

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, read the front, say the answer, then check. Repeat the ones you missed the next day.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| Where do most of a new account's views come from? | Recommendations to people who don't follow it yet. |
| Name four signals YouTube uses for recommendations. | Watch history, search history, likes and dislikes, satisfaction surveys (also subscriptions and "Not interested"). |
| What does Instagram's Account Status show a professional account? | Whether its content and account can be recommended to non-followers. |
| Why do reposts of other people's videos get less reach? | Platforms recommend the original and can stop recommending accounts that keep reposting. |
| The five funnel stages? | Awareness, consideration, conversion, loyalty, advocacy. |
| Owned, earned or paid: a customer's Google review? | Earned. |
| What do businesses pay a social media marketer for? | Results (enquiries, bookings, sales) and saved time. |
| Four tests of a good practice niche? | Content supply, audience demand, your interest, career link. |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Skipping the "why".** Without understanding signals, you can only copy trends. With it, you can design posts that work on any platform.
- **Not logging posts from day 1.** Your first posts are your baseline. Without the numbers you can't show growth later.
- **Comparing your week 2 with someone's year 5.** Compare yourself only with your own numbers from last month.

sections.title: SMM-M01-L01: How social platforms and recommendation systems work
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Explain in your own words how Instagram, YouTube and Facebook decide what to show people, name the signals that matter most, and write five posting rules that will still work when the algorithms change. **Time:** about 3 hours (1 hour study, 2 hours action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### "The algorithm" is many systems, not one

People say "the algorithm" as if one machine decides everything. Meta says plainly that there isn't a single AI system deciding what people see on Facebook and Instagram. Many systems each predict how likely you are to be interested in a post, or to interact with it, using thousands of signals, and those predictions decide the order of your feed (as of October 2026). YouTube works the same way. The details change every month; the purpose doesn't: **show each person what they are most likely to value.**

### Two ways people see your posts

| Who sees it | Where | What it depends on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **People who follow you** | Feed, Stories, subscriptions, WhatsApp Status | Your relationship with them: how often they watch, like, reply to or message you |
| **People who don't follow you** | Instagram Reels tab and Explore, YouTube home and Shorts feed, Facebook feed recommendations, search | How well your post matches their interests and how earlier viewers reacted to it |

A new account has almost no followers, so nearly all its early views come from the second row: **recommendations**. That's good news. Instagram says its reels are now shown first to a small audience, and the ones that perform best go to wider and wider groups, "based on its engagement, not just the creator's follower count" (as of October 2026). A page with 50 followers can reach thousands of people with one good Reel.

### The signals that matter most

Platforms don't publish their exact formulas, but they do explain the main signals.

- **YouTube** names watch history, search history, subscriptions, likes, dislikes, "Not interested" and "Don't recommend channel" clicks, and satisfaction surveys. It uses surveys to understand "satisfaction, not just watch time" (as of October 2026).
- **Instagram's** explanation of Reels ranking lists your activity (which reels you liked, saved, shared or commented on), your history with the account, information about the reel (its audio, visuals and popularity) and information about the creator.
- **Meta** says engagement (likes, comments, views), how long and how often you watch, and your past interactions with the author all count, and that choosing "Not interested" or "Show less" lowers similar posts for a while.

Put simply, the system watches what real people **do** after seeing your post. Do they stop scrolling? Watch to the end? Watch again? Share it with a friend, save it, comment, follow, visit your profile? Or do they skip it in one second?

### What gets less reach

- **Copies.** Instagram recommends the original when it finds identical or near-identical content, and since 2024 it has removed accounts that repeatedly repost other people's content from recommendations. Facebook announced a similar crackdown on unoriginal content in July 2025.
- **Low quality.** Instagram's tips for creators: avoid watermarks from other apps and low-quality footage, use vertical video, hook viewers in the first 3 seconds.
- **Content that breaks the Recommendation Guidelines.** Instagram holds recommended content to "a higher standard" than what your followers may see. A professional account can check **Account Status** (Settings → Account → Account Status) to see whether its content can be recommended (as of October 2026).

### Principles that survive algorithm changes

Features and formulas change; these ideas have held for years on every platform:

1. **Make each post for one specific kind of person.** The system finds the right people more easily when the post is clearly for someone.
2. **Earn the first seconds.** Show the result, ask a sharp question or start with movement.
3. **Deliver what the hook promised.** Satisfied viewers watch longer, return and share; disappointed ones skip, and the system notices.
4. **Give people a reason to share or save it:** something useful, surprising, funny or local that they want to send to someone.
5. **Be original.** Your own photos, your own words, your own local knowledge.
6. **Be consistent and learn from your numbers.** Each post is a small experiment.
7. **Stay eligible.** Follow the rules, or nothing else matters.

### Common myths

- **"Post at the perfect time and you'll go viral."** Timing helps a little; content decides.
- **"30 hashtags = more reach."** Instagram began limiting captions to five hashtags in December 2025, and says fewer, more targeted hashtags work better than many generic ones (as of October 2026).
- **"I've been shadowbanned."** Usually the post just didn't interest people. Check Account Status first; if it shows no problem, look at your hook and watch time.
- **"Delete and repost it."** Reposting the same content doesn't fix it and may count as a duplicate. Make a better version instead.

## Local example

Anu set up **@kuttiady.diaries** in Week 0. Her first post was a photo of a tea shop with a 12-line caption and 25 hashtags: 41 views, all from her friends.

Her second post was a 15-second vertical video: steam rising from glasses of chaya in the evening rush, with the text "₹12 chaya, since 1987: Kuttiady's oldest tea shop?" on screen in the first second, and the owner's permission. It got 1,300 views, and 82% of them came from accounts that didn't follow her. Seventeen people shared it, mostly to WhatsApp, and 23 followed the page.

Why? The first second showed movement and asked a local question. Local people watched to the end, then sent it to friends. Those shares told the system that this was worth showing to more people nearby. The photo post gave the system almost nothing to work with.

(Anu and her numbers are made up to illustrate the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [YouTube Help: How YouTube recommendations work](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/16089387) | Read the whole page: the signals and where recommendations appear | 15 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Meta AI blog: How AI powers experiences on Facebook and Instagram](https://ai.meta.com/blog/how-ai-powers-experiences-facebook-instagram-system-cards/) | Read the first half: how ranking works and how people control their feeds | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Instagram for Creators: Helping creators of all sizes break through](https://creators.instagram.com/blog/helping-creators-of-all-sizes-break-through) | Read how reels are tested with small audiences first | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Instagram for Creators: What creators need to know about recommendations](https://creators.instagram.com/blog/instagram-recommendations-eligibility-tips-creators) | Read the recommendation rules and the tips for creators | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Search Engine Land: How Instagram ranks content (2023)](https://searchengineland.com/how-instagram-ranks-content-feed-stories-explore-reels-search-427774) | Skim the signals for Feed, Stories, Explore, Reels and Search | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the five resources above (about 50 minutes). Note any signal that surprises you.
2. Keep a feed diary for 3 days. On your personal Instagram and YouTube, for 10 recommended posts a day (from accounts you don't follow), write one row each: what it was, why you think it was shown to you, whether you watched to the end, and what you did (skipped, liked, shared, saved, followed).
3. On day 2, tap "Not interested" on 5 posts you dislike. On day 3, note whether your recommendations changed.
4. Write your **5 rules that survive algorithm changes**, in your own words, using what you saw in your diary.
5. Publish your first post on your practice account: a 15–30 second vertical video introducing the page ("What this page is about, in 15 seconds"). Log it in the Posting Log.

**Proof to record:** Your 30-row feed diary, your 5 rules, and the link to your first post with its Posting Log row.

## Template: feed diary (paste into a new sheet)

```csv
Day,Platform,What the post was,Why I think I was shown it,Watched to the end? (Y/N),What I did (skip/like/share/save/follow/comment),Notes
```

## Template: my 5 rules that survive algorithm changes

```
MY 5 RULES (write them in your own words)
1. Who every post is for: ____________________
2. How I will earn the first 3 seconds: ________
3. How I will keep the promise of the hook: ____
4. Why someone would share or save my posts: ___
5. What I will never do (copy, buy, spam): _____

CHECK BEFORE EVERY POST
[ ] Is it original (my photo, my video, my words)?
[ ] Is the first second interesting without sound?
[ ] Is it clearly for one kind of person?
[ ] Would I send this to a friend?
[ ] Does it follow the rules from day 1?
```

## Common mistakes

- **Chasing hacks.** Tricks that "beat the algorithm" stop working within months and can break the rules. Learn the principles instead.
- **Judging a post in the first hour.** Recommended posts can keep getting views for days. Record views after 24 hours and after 7 days.
- **Blaming a "shadowban".** Check Account Status first. If it shows no problem, improve the hook and the first 3 seconds.
- **Reposting viral videos from other accounts.** Platforms recommend the original, label reposts and can stop recommending accounts that keep doing it.
- **Writing for everyone.** A post for "everyone in Kerala" is for no one. Picture one viewer and make it for them.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. According to YouTube Help, why does YouTube use viewer surveys in recommendations?
    - A) To understand satisfaction, not just watch time
    - B) To count subscribers
    - C) To check copyright
    - D) To decide video prices
2. A new account with 30 followers posts a Reel that gets 2,000 views. Where did most of those views probably come from?
    - A) Paid ads
    - B) Hashtags alone
    - C) Its followers watching many times
    - D) Recommendations to people who don't follow it
3. Which of these is most likely to reduce a Reel's chance of being recommended on Instagram?
    - A) Posting regularly
    - B) Adding audio
    - C) Using vertical 9:16 video
    - D) Reposting someone else's video with another app's watermark
4. Your views drop for two weeks. What should you do first?
    - A) Add 30 hashtags
    - B) Check Account Status, then compare your hooks and watch time with your best posts
    - C) Delete all your posts
    - D) Buy followers to restart growth

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** YouTube's, Meta's and Instagram's own explanations of ranking (about 50 minutes)
- **Action:** keep a 3-day feed diary, write your 5 rules and publish your first post. It is done when your proof is saved: your 30-row feed diary, your 5 rules, and the link to your first post with its Posting Log row.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **A.** YouTube says surveys help the system understand satisfaction, not just watch time.
2. **D.** New accounts grow mostly through recommendations, where a reel is tested on small groups first.
3. **D.** Instagram recommends originals and advises avoiding watermarks and low-quality reposts.
4. **B.** Rule out a policy problem, then look at the signals you control.

sections.title: SMM-M01-L02: The marketing funnel and the customer journey
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Map how a real customer moves from first seeing a business on social media to buying and recommending it, and choose the right content and the right number to watch at each stage. **Time:** about 2 hours (1 hour 20 minutes study, 40 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Why most posts don't sell (and why that's fine)

A person who sees a shop's Reel for the first time is rarely ready to buy. They need to notice the shop, trust it, and have a reason to act now. Marketers describe this path as a **funnel**: many people at the top, fewer at each step down.

| Stage | What the person thinks | Content that helps | Number to watch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Awareness** | "Oh, I didn't know this place existed." | Short, entertaining or useful Reels and Shorts, local trends, collaborations | Views, accounts reached, share of non-followers |
| **Consideration** | "Is it good? Is it for me? How much?" | Proof: reviews, behind the scenes, prices, comparisons, FAQs, carousels | Profile visits, saves, follows, replies |
| **Conversion** | "I'll message, call, visit or order." | Clear offers, catalogue, "how to order", limited-time reasons | DMs and WhatsApp chats, calls, direction requests, orders |
| **Loyalty** | "I'll come back." | Updates for existing customers, Status, Channel posts, thank-yous | Repeat orders, Channel or broadcast replies |
| **Advocacy** | "You must try this." | Asking for reviews, sharing customers' posts with permission, referral offers | Reviews, tags, referrals |

Real people don't move in a straight line. Someone may see one post and order at once, or follow for months before buying. The funnel is still useful because it reminds you that **each post has a job**, and that you should judge it by the right number. A funny awareness Reel shouldn't be judged by orders, and a price-list post shouldn't be judged by views.

### The Kerala journey runs through WhatsApp

For most small businesses near Kuttiady, the conversion step isn't a website: it's a WhatsApp chat, a phone call or a visit. So a good social media plan always makes the next step easy: a WhatsApp button or link in the profile, the phone number in the bio, the location tagged, and opening hours that are correct.

### Owned, earned and paid

- **Owned:** channels you control: your Instagram page, YouTube channel, WhatsApp Business catalogue, Google Business Profile, website.
- **Earned:** what others say and share: shares, mentions, reviews, a local news page reposting you.
- **Paid:** ads and paid promotions (Module 9) and paid creator posts (Module 10).

Organic (unpaid) posting builds the owned and earned parts. Paid ads speed things up, but they work far better when the organic content is already good. This course starts with organic and adds paid later.

### One message everywhere

Your posts, profile, WhatsApp replies and shop counter should tell the same story. Marketers call this **integrated marketing communications**: every channel gives the customer the same message, so trust builds faster.

## Local example

Riyas runs **Malabar Mobiles**, a phone shop with a repair counter in Kuttiady town. This is the path one customer, Shabna, took:

| Stage | What happened | Number Riyas could track |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Awareness | Saw a 20-second Reel, "3 signs your phone battery needs replacing", that a friend shared on WhatsApp | 4,200 views; 70% non-followers |
| Consideration | Visited the profile, saw the repair price list carousel and two customer reviews | 180 profile visits that week |
| Conversion | Tapped the WhatsApp button: "Battery for Redmi Note? How much?" Got a quick reply with a price and visited the next day | 26 WhatsApp chats; 9 repairs |
| Loyalty | Joined the shop's WhatsApp Channel for offers | 310 Channel followers |
| Advocacy | Left a Google review and told her sister | 1 review, 1 referral |

The Reel never "sold" anything, yet without it Shabna would never have heard of the shop. Riyas now judges his tip Reels by views and shares, and his price posts by WhatsApp chats.

(Malabar Mobiles and these numbers are made up to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [OpenStax Principles of Marketing 13.3: Integrated Marketing Communications](https://openstax.org/books/principles-marketing/pages/13-3-integrated-marketing-communications) | Read 13.3 to see why every channel should carry the same message | 30 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [OpenStax Principles of Marketing 16.2: Social Media and Mobile Marketing](https://openstax.org/books/principles-marketing/pages/16-2-social-media-and-mobile-marketing) | Read the social media marketing part of 16.2 (you can skip mobile marketing) | 40 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Meta Blueprint: Start marketing with Meta technologies](https://www.facebookblueprint.com/student/path/211554-meta-marketing) | Free sign-up. Do the two short lessons on how businesses use Meta apps | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the three resources (about 1 hour 20 minutes).
2. Map your own journey: think of something you bought in the last year after seeing it on social media. Fill in the five stages with what actually happened.
3. Ask a friend or relative the same questions and map their journey. Note where WhatsApp, calls or visits came in.
4. Pick one real local business you know. Fill in the funnel template for it: one content idea and one number for each stage.

**Proof to record:** Two real customer journeys and one funnel map for a local business, saved in 01 Foundations.

## Template: funnel map

```
FUNNEL MAP: [business name]
Who the customer is: ____________________

AWARENESS
  Content idea: ____________________
  Number to watch: views / reach / % non-followers
CONSIDERATION
  Content idea: ____________________
  Number to watch: profile visits / saves / follows
CONVERSION
  How they act: WhatsApp / call / visit / order link
  Is it one tap away? Y / N
  Number to watch: chats / calls / orders
LOYALTY
  Content idea: ____________________
  Number to watch: repeat orders / Channel replies
ADVOCACY
  How I ask for reviews or referrals: __________
  Number to watch: reviews / referrals
```

## Template: customer journey interview (5 questions)

```
1. What did you buy, and when?
2. Where did you first see it? (Reel, Status, friend, search...)
3. What made you trust it enough to ask or buy?
4. How did you contact them or buy? (WhatsApp, call, visit, app)
5. Did you tell anyone else about it, or leave a review?
```

## Common mistakes

- **Expecting every post to sell.** Most posts build awareness and trust. Give each post one job and judge it by that job's number.
- **Only posting offers.** Offers work for people at the bottom of the funnel. Without awareness and trust posts, there is no one left to buy.
- **A hard-to-find next step.** If people can't message or call in one tap, they leave. Put the WhatsApp link and number where they can't miss them.
- **Different details everywhere.** One name, one number, one address and the same message on every channel.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. A carousel showing a bakery's prices and three customer reviews mainly helps which stage?
    - A) Awareness
    - B) None
    - C) Loyalty
    - D) Consideration
2. Which number best shows whether a "how to order" post worked?
    - A) WhatsApp chats and orders that came from it
    - B) Likes
    - C) Followers of the page
    - D) Hashtags used
3. A customer's Google review that mentions the shop is an example of:
    - A) Earned media
    - B) Owned media
    - C) A boosted post
    - D) Paid media
4. For most small shops near Kuttiady, what is the usual conversion step?
    - A) A podcast
    - B) A WhatsApp chat, a call or a visit
    - C) A long website form
    - D) An email newsletter

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** OpenStax 13.3 and 16.2 and a short Meta Blueprint course (about 1 hour 20 minutes)
- **Action:** map two real customer journeys and a funnel for one local business. It is done when your proof is saved: two real customer journeys and one funnel map for a local business, saved in 01 Foundations.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **D.** Prices and proof help people who already know the bakery decide.
2. **A.** Conversion posts are judged by actions such as chats, calls and orders.
3. **A.** Earned media is what other people say and share about you.
4. **B.** That's why the WhatsApp link, phone number and location must be easy to find.

sections.title: SMM-M01-L03: Career paths, your goal and your practice account
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Choose the career path you are aiming for, list the skills real employers and clients ask for, set your goals for the course, and confirm the niche of your practice account. **Time:** about 2 hours 30 minutes (45 minutes study, 1 hour 45 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### What people pay social media marketers for

Businesses don't pay for posts. They pay for **results** (more enquiries, bookings, visits and sales) and for **time** (someone else handling it well). Keep that in mind and every skill in this course makes sense.

### Six paths

| Path | What you do day to day | How you usually start |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Freelancer for local businesses** | Plan and make content, run WhatsApp and Google profiles, report results for 2–5 clients | A pilot for a business you know (Module 11), then monthly packages (Module 15) |
| **In-house job** | Social media executive or content creator for one company, institution or brand | Apply with a portfolio of real results; many roles ask for video and copy skills |
| **Agency job** | Work for many brands inside a team: content, ads, reports | Apply as a content creator, designer or social media executive |
| **Creator** | Grow your own channel or page and earn from it | Long-term; income usually comes later (Module 10) |
| **Specialist** | Video editor, ads specialist, community manager, analytics | Go deep in one skill after this course |
| **Your own business** | Market a business you run | Pair this course with the Entrepreneurship course |

You don't have to decide forever. Pick the path that excites you most now; the course works for all of them.

### The skills that get hired

Read real job ads and client requests and you'll see the same skills again and again: making short videos, writing captions, planning content, knowing the main platforms, reading insights, basic ads, and communicating with clients. **Proof beats certificates.** A portfolio with three real case studies and numbers persuades a shop owner or an employer more than any certificate. That's why this course makes you build one.

### Honest timelines

- Learning the skills well enough to help a small business: about 4–6 months at the part-time pace.
- First paid client: usually after a pilot or two, often with someone you already know.
- A steady income from several clients or a job: usually takes most of a year, sometimes longer.
- Growing your own account: slow for the first months for almost everyone.

These are not promises. They depend on how much you practise, your area and your luck. What you control is the work: posting, learning from numbers and talking to businesses.

### Researching your local market

Don't trust anyone's salary or price figures, including in this course, without checking. Instead, look at 10 real listings: job sites (search "social media executive Kozhikode", "content creator Kochi"), LinkedIn jobs, and the "we're hiring" posts of local businesses and agencies. Note the skills asked for and the pay, if it is stated. This also shows you what to put in your portfolio.

### Your practice account

In Week 0 you set up a practice account. Now confirm its niche with a quick scorecard. A good practice niche has:

- **Content supply:** you can make 3 posts a week for a year without running out
- **Audience demand:** people search for it and share it
- **Interest:** you enjoy it enough to keep going
- **Career link:** it helps you meet clients or shows skills employers want

The default, a **hyperlocal page about your area**, scores well on all four: there is always something new nearby, local people love sharing local posts, and every shop you feature is a future client who has already seen your work.

## Local example

Anu scored three niche ideas from 1 to 5 on each point:

| Niche | Content supply | Demand | Interest | Career link | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hyperlocal page, @kuttiady.diaries | 5 | 4 | 4 | 5 | 18 |
| Kerala PSC tips in Malayalam | 4 | 5 | 3 | 2 | 14 |
| Kozhikode food reviews | 4 | 4 | 5 | 3 | 16 |

She kept the hyperlocal page. Her research of 10 real listings (six job ads, four "need someone to handle our Instagram" posts) showed that 8 of 10 asked for short-video editing, 7 for Canva design and 5 for basic Meta ads. She set her goal: "By week 40, three case studies with numbers, two paying local clients, and a page of my own with steady weekly growth."

(Anu's scores and research are made up to illustrate the method; do your own.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [YouTube Creators (free official guides)](https://www.youtube.com/creators/) | Open "Get started" and the "Grow" overview to see what creators learn first | 20 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Instagram for Creators: Best practices hub](https://creators.instagram.com/best-practices) | Browse the best practices hub: Reels, Profile, Grow and Monetize sections | 15 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [HubSpot: what the Social Media Certification covers](https://blog.hubspot.com/customers/introducing-hubspot-academy-social-media-certification) | Read what a full social media certification covers, as a map of the skills | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the three resources (about 45 minutes).
2. Find 10 real listings: job ads and businesses asking for social media help. Copy the skills and pay (if stated) into the skills table below.
3. Choose your path for now and write your goals for week 13, week 26 and week 40.
4. Score your practice niche (and up to two alternatives) with the scorecard. Keep or change it.
5. Update your practice account's bio to say clearly what the page is about, in one line, in Malayalam or English.

**Proof to record:** Your skills table from 10 real listings, your goals, your niche scorecard and a screenshot of your updated bio.

## Template: skills table from real listings

```csv
Source (site or business),Role or request,Location,Skills asked for,Tools named,Pay (if stated),Link,Date seen
```

## Template: career plan and niche scorecard

```
MY PATH (for now): ______________________

MY GOALS
By week 13: ___ posts published, ________________
By week 26: first case study done, ______________
By week 40: ___ case studies, ___ paying clients
            or job applications, _______________

SKILLS I SAW MOST OFTEN (top 5)
1. ________ 2. ________ 3. ________
4. ________ 5. ________

NICHE SCORECARD (1-5 each)
Niche | Supply | Demand | Interest | Career | Total
1. ___________ |   |   |   |   |
2. ___________ |   |   |   |   |
3. ___________ |   |   |   |   |
My choice: _______________
One-line bio: _______________________________
```

## Common mistakes

- **Collecting certificates instead of results.** Certificates help a little; a portfolio with real numbers gets clients and jobs. Do both, but results first.
- **Believing "₹1 lakh a month in 30 days" videos.** Income takes months of practice and client work. Check real listings for real figures.
- **A niche you'll be bored of by week 6.** Score your interest honestly. You will post about this for 40 weeks.
- **Waiting to feel ready before posting.** Your early posts are supposed to be weak. They become the "before" in your first case study.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. What do small businesses mainly pay a social media marketer for?
    - A) Pretty posts
    - B) Hashtags
    - C) More enquiries, bookings or sales, and saved time
    - D) Followers from anywhere
2. What persuades a local shop owner most that you can help them?
    - A) A business card
    - B) A case study with real before and after numbers
    - C) A large personal follower count
    - D) A long list of certificates
3. Why does a hyperlocal page score well as a practice niche?
    - A) It never needs posting
    - B) Platforms pay hyperlocal pages
    - C) There is always local content, local people share it, and featured shops become future clients
    - D) It needs no permissions
4. Where should you get salary and price figures for your area?
    - A) From viral videos
    - B) From 10 or more real, current job ads and client requests
    - C) From one friend
    - D) From guessing

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** YouTube Creators, Instagram's best practices hub and HubSpot's skills overview (about 45 minutes)
- **Action:** research 10 real listings, set your goals, score your niche and update your bio. It is done when your proof is saved: your skills table from 10 real listings, your goals, your niche scorecard and a screenshot of your updated bio.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **C.** Businesses pay for results and for someone to handle it well.
2. **B.** Proof of results is what clients and employers look for.
3. **C.** It does well on content supply, demand and career link.
4. **B.** Real listings show current local demand, skills and pay.

sections.title: Module 2: Strategy
sections.summary: Decide what your account is for, who it serves, how it is different and what it talks about, using real research instead of guesses.
sections.content:
## Overview

A strategy is a short set of decisions that make every later decision easier. In two weeks you'll set goals and KPIs from your own baseline, talk to real people in your audience, mine comments and search data, study your competitors, write a positioning statement, and choose your content pillars and brand voice.

You keep posting while you do it: two posts a week, and from now on each post should fit a pillar.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Turn a business goal into a social objective, a KPI and a dated target
- Research an audience with conversations, comment mining and Google Trends
- Write an evidence-based persona
- Analyse competitors and find gaps
- Write a positioning statement, content pillars and a brand voice chart

## Time

About 10 hours in total: 9 hours of lessons and 1 hour for the module project. Part-time: weeks 3–4.

## Lessons

1. SMM-M02-L01: Goals, objectives and KPIs (about 2 hours)
2. SMM-M02-L02: Audience research and personas (about 3 hours)
3. SMM-M02-L03: Niche, positioning and competitor analysis (about 2 hours 30 minutes)
4. SMM-M02-L04: Content pillars and brand voice (about 1 hour 30 minutes)

## Module project: A one-page social media strategy

1. Put your work from this module on one page (Google Docs): goal ladder, persona, positioning statement, top 3 competitor lessons and gaps, pillars and series, voice chart and language rules.
2. Add the platforms you plan to use (you will confirm them in Module 3) and your posting rhythm.
3. Add the KPIs you will report every month.
4. Ask one person from your research to read it and tell you what is unclear. Fix it.

**Proof to record:** Your one-page strategy (link) with a note of the feedback you got and what you changed.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3. If a row is a 1, redo that part first.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Goals | No targets | Targets without baseline or date | Input and output goals from a baseline, with dates |
| Audience research | Guesses only | Some research | 5 conversations, 50 comments and Trends behind the persona |
| Positioning | Unclear what the page is | A statement others can't repeat | A statement two people repeated correctly |
| Competitors | None studied | One or two, no gaps | 3–5 studied with clear gaps |
| Pillars and voice | Random posting | Pillars but no voice | Pillars, series, 20 ideas and a written voice chart |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, when PSC prep or work leaves little time:

- Write one goal ladder (your account) with one input goal.
- Have 3 conversations instead of 5, and mine 30 comments.
- Study 3 competitors.
- Choose 3 pillars and write 12 ideas.

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, read the front, say the answer, then check. Repeat the ones you missed the next day.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| The four layers of a goal ladder? | Business goal, social objective, KPI, target. |
| What does SMART stand for (OpenStax)? | Specific, measurable, actionable, realistic, time-bound. |
| Inputs, outputs, outcomes: which is "WhatsApp orders"? | An outcome. |
| Engagement rate formula? | Interactions ÷ accounts reached × 100 (say which formula you used). |
| Four free audience research sources? | Conversations, comment mining, search data (Google Trends, search suggestions), your own insights. |
| What does 100 mean in Google Trends? | Peak relative interest for that term in the chosen time and place. |
| A niche is topic + audience + ...? | Angle. |
| Head-to-head or differentiation for a small account? | Differentiation. |
| What is a content series? | A repeating format inside a pillar, like "₹100 Friday". |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Skipping research because "I know my audience".** Everyone is surprised by what five honest conversations reveal.
- **A strategy nobody reads.** Keep it to one page and check new post ideas against it.
- **Changing strategy every week.** Give a strategy at least a month of posts before you judge it.

sections.title: SMM-M02-L01: Goals, objectives and KPIs
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Turn a business goal into a social media objective, a KPI and a dated target, for your own account and for a local business, starting from your own baseline numbers. **Time:** about 2 hours (40 minutes study, 1 hour 20 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### From "be on Instagram" to a goal you can measure

Most small businesses say "we should be on Instagram". That's not a goal. A useful plan has four layers, each one serving the one above it:

| Layer | Question | Example for Nisha's Oven |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Business goal** | What does the business need? | More weekday cake orders |
| **Social media objective** | What must social media do for that? | Get people within 5 km to message on WhatsApp |
| **KPI** | Which number shows it is working? | WhatsApp chats that start from Instagram |
| **Target** | How much, by when? | 30 chats a month by the end of March, from about 8 now |

Write targets the SMART way: **specific, measurable, actionable, realistic and time-bound**. "Grow the page" fails every test. "Reach 1,000 local followers by week 26, with at least 15% of views coming from shares" passes them all.

### Inputs, outputs and outcomes

- **Inputs** are what you control: posts a week, hooks tested, comments answered within an hour.
- **Outputs** are what the platform reports: views, reach, followers, shares.
- **Outcomes** are what the business feels: enquiries, bookings, sales, repeat customers.

Beginners set only output goals ("10,000 followers") and feel helpless when the numbers don't move. Set at least one input goal you fully control, such as "3 posts a week, every week", and judge yourself first on that.

### Which KPI for which objective

| Objective | KPIs that fit | Watch out for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Awareness | Views, accounts reached, share of views from non-followers | Big reach outside your area is worth little to a local shop |
| Engagement | Shares, saves and comments per 1,000 views; engagement rate | Likes alone are the weakest signal |
| Leads | DMs, WhatsApp chats, calls, form fills, link clicks | Count them where they arrive: label chats "from Instagram" |
| Sales | Orders or bookings you can trace (ask "how did you hear about us?", use a code word) | Don't claim sales you can't trace |
| Loyalty | Repeat orders, WhatsApp Channel or broadcast replies | Needs a simple customer list |

**Engagement rate** = (likes + comments + shares + saves) ÷ accounts reached × 100. Platforms count slightly differently, so always say which formula you used, and compare a page only with its own past numbers. There is no universal "good" engagement rate.

### Vanity metrics

A vanity metric looks impressive but doesn't change decisions: total followers, total likes, "impressions" with no context. Use them as background, never as the headline of a report.

### Start from your baseline

Targets come from your own numbers, not from someone else's success story. If your first five posts averaged 120 views, a target of 300 views a post by week 13 is a stretch but believable; 50,000 is a wish.

## Local example

Anu's goal ladder for **@kuttiady.diaries**:

- **Learning goal (input):** 3 posts a week, every week, and one experiment a month.
- **Growth objective:** become the page people in and around Kuttiady share for local news and food.
- **KPIs:** average views per post; shares per 1,000 views; followers within 25 km (Insights shows top towns once the page is bigger).
- **Baseline (first 5 posts):** 260 average views, 6 shares per 1,000 views, 48 followers.
- **Targets:** by week 13, 500 average views and 10 shares per 1,000; by week 26, 1,500 average views and 1,000 followers, mostly local.

For **Nisha's Oven** she wrote: business goal, more weekday orders; objective, WhatsApp chats from nearby parents; KPI, chats labelled "Instagram" in WhatsApp Business; target, from 8 to 30 a month by March; input, two process Reels and one price post a week.

(Made-up numbers to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [OpenStax Principles of Marketing 2.3: Purpose and Structure of the Marketing Plan](https://openstax.org/books/principles-marketing/pages/2-3-purpose-and-structure-of-the-marketing-plan) | Read the "Objectives and Issues" part on SMART objectives | 15 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [HubSpot Academy: Social Media Certification Course (free)](https://academy.hubspot.com/courses/social-media) | Free sign-up. Watch the first lesson, on social media strategy (lesson names may change) | 25 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the two resources (about 40 minutes).
2. Work out your account's baseline from your posts so far: average views, shares per 1,000 views and followers.
3. Write your own goal ladder: one input goal, one growth objective, two KPIs and targets for weeks 13 and 26.
4. Write a goal ladder for one real local business you know, from business goal to target.
5. For both, mark each number as an input, an output or an outcome.

**Proof to record:** Your two goal ladders with baselines and dated targets, saved in 02 Strategy.

## Template: goal ladder

```
GOAL LADDER: [account or business]
Business goal: ____________________________
Social media objective: ___________________
KPI 1: ______________ (input / output / outcome)
KPI 2: ______________ (input / output / outcome)
Baseline today: ___________ (date: ____)
Target by week 13: ________
Target by week 26: ________
Input goal I fully control: ___ posts a week,
  plus ________________________________
How I will measure it: Posting Log / Insights /
  WhatsApp labels / "how did you hear about us?"
```

## Template: KPI formulas

```
Engagement rate (%) = (likes + comments + shares + saves)
                      / accounts reached x 100
Shares per 1,000 views = shares / views x 1000
Non-follower share (%) = views from non-followers
                         / total views x 100
Follower growth (%) = (followers end - followers start)
                      / followers start x 100
Cost per enquiry (Rs) = money spent / enquiries
```

## Common mistakes

- **Only output goals.** You can't control views directly. Add an input goal you can meet every week.
- **Copying someone else's targets.** Start from your own baseline and stretch it.
- **Reporting likes as success.** Lead with the KPI that matches the objective, such as chats or shares.
- **No date.** A target without a date never fails, so it never teaches you anything.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Which is a SMART target?
    - A) Get more engagement soon
    - B) Become famous in Kerala
    - C) 30 WhatsApp chats a month from Instagram by 31 March
    - D) Grow the page
2. "3 posts every week" is an example of:
    - A) An outcome
    - B) A vanity metric
    - C) An input you control
    - D) A KPI for sales
3. For a lead-generation objective, which KPI fits best?
    - A) WhatsApp chats and calls that came from social media
    - B) Number of hashtags
    - C) Total likes
    - D) Follower count
4. Where should your first targets come from?
    - A) Your own baseline, stretched
    - B) A random number
    - C) The highest number you can imagine
    - D) A famous creator's numbers

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** OpenStax 2.3 on SMART objectives and HubSpot's first strategy lesson (about 40 minutes)
- **Action:** write goal ladders with baselines and dated targets for your account and one local business. It is done when your proof is saved: your two goal ladders with baselines and dated targets, saved in 02 Strategy.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **C.** It is specific, measurable, realistic for a small shop and time-bound.
2. **C.** Inputs are the actions fully in your control.
3. **A.** Leads are people who start a conversation about buying.
4. **A.** Targets based on your own numbers are believable and useful.
