sections.title: SMM-M02-L02: Audience research and personas
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Find out what your audience really wants by talking to five people, mining comments and using Google Trends, then turn it into one or two evidence-based personas. **Time:** about 3 hours (1 hour study, 2 hours action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Research beats guessing

Most accounts fail because they post what the creator likes, not what the audience needs. You don't need surveys or money to find out. You need four free sources.

**1. Short conversations.** Talk to five people in your target audience, in person or on a call, for about 10 minutes each. Ask about their real behaviour, not their opinions about your idea:

- "When did you last look for [a good bakery / a phone repair / a place to eat] nearby? How did you search?"
- "Which pages or channels do you actually watch? Why those?"
- "What was the last post you sent to someone? Why?"
- "What do you wish someone explained better about [topic]?"

**2. Comment mining.** Open 3 to 5 popular accounts in your niche and read 50 comments on their best posts. Copy the questions, complaints and praise into a sheet. Comments are your audience telling you, for free, what they care about.

**3. Search data.** Google Trends shows how search interest in a topic changes over time and by region, on a 0–100 scale. A 100 means the peak for that topic in your chosen time and place, not a number of searches, and very low interest shows as 0 ({ASOF}). Set the region to Kerala, compare two or three terms, and switch to **YouTube Search** to see video interest. Also type your topic into YouTube and Instagram search and note the suggestions that appear.

**4. Your own numbers.** Once your page has more followers, its insights show top towns, age ranges and when followers are online. Until then, use the first three sources.

### Segment before you write

OpenStax describes four common ways to divide a market. For a social account:

- **Geographic:** Kuttiady and nearby panchayats; people from the area working in the Gulf
- **Demographic:** age, gender, family stage, income band
- **Psychographic:** values, interests, lifestyle ("loves trying new food spots", "careful with money")
- **Behavioural:** how they use the platform ("watches Reels at night", "searches on YouTube before buying")

### A persona built from evidence

A persona is a one-page profile of a typical person in your audience. Give it a name, but fill it only with things your research showed: quotes, real habits, real questions. A persona made from guesses is fiction; one made from five conversations and fifty comments is a tool.

### Malayalam, English or both?

Your research will tell you. Many audiences in Malabar are comfortable with Malayalam speech, English or Manglish text, and a mix. Gulf-based followers from the area often want local news and food nostalgia. Note what language your interviewees actually use in their own posts and messages (more in SMM-M04-L02).

## Local example

Anu talked to five people: two college students, a shop owner, a mother of two and her cousin in Dubai. Comment mining on three Kozhikode food and news pages gave her 50 comments. The most common themes:

| Theme | How often (of 55 notes) | Example quote |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "Where is this? Send location" | 14 | "Ithu evideya? Location idu" |
| Prices | 11 | "Rate ethra?" |
| Nostalgia for home (Gulf followers) | 9 | "Missing naadu food" |
| Timings and parking | 7 | "Sunday open aano?" |
| Complaints about outdated posts | 5 | "Ithu ippo illa" |

Google Trends for Kerala showed that interest in "biryani" and "Onam sadya" rises before the festivals, so she noted them for her calendar. Her persona, "Shahana, 24, Kuttiady, college student", came straight from these notes: watches Reels at night, sends food spots to friends, always asks for location and price.

Her first change: every food post now shows the price and has the location tagged. Saves on food posts doubled the next week.

(Made-up research results to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [OpenStax Principles of Marketing 5.1: Market Segmentation and Consumer Markets](https://openstax.org/books/principles-marketing/pages/5-1-market-segmentation-and-consumer-markets) | Read the four ways of segmenting consumer markets | 35 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Trends Help: Get started with Google Trends](https://support.google.com/trends/answer/6248105) | Read how to compare terms, explore by region and refine by category | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Trends Help: FAQ about Google Trends data](https://support.google.com/trends/answer/4365533) | Read what the 0–100 numbers mean (and don't mean) | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Creators (free official guides)](https://www.youtube.com/creators/) | In "Grow", read "Understand your audience" | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 1 hour).
2. Talk to 5 people in your target audience, about 10 minutes each, using the questions in the template. Take notes in their own words.
3. Mine 50 comments from 3–5 popular accounts in your niche into the comment sheet. Tag each one with a theme.
4. Run 3 Google Trends comparisons for Kerala (one on YouTube Search). Screenshot each and write one sentence on what it shows.
5. Write one persona (two if your audience has two clear groups) using only what your research showed.

**Proof to record:** Notes from 5 conversations, the 50-comment sheet with themes, 3 Trends screenshots and your persona, saved in 02 Strategy.

## Template: conversation questions (English and Malayalam)

```
1. When did you last look for [topic] nearby? How?
   [topic] അവസാനമായി എപ്പോഴാണ് അന്വേഷിച്ചത്? എങ്ങനെ?
2. Which pages or channels do you actually watch? Why?
   ഏതൊക്കെ പേജുകൾ/ചാനലുകൾ ശരിക്കും കാണാറുണ്ട്? എന്തുകൊണ്ട്?
3. What was the last post you sent to someone? Why?
   അവസാനം ആർക്കെങ്കിലും അയച്ച പോസ്റ്റ് ഏതാണ്? എന്തിന്?
4. What do you wish someone explained better?
   ആരെങ്കിലും നന്നായി വിശദീകരിച്ചിരുന്നെങ്കിൽ എന്ന് തോന്നുന്നത് എന്താണ്?
5. Malayalam, English or both: what do you prefer to read?
   വായിക്കാൻ ഇഷ്ടം മലയാളമോ ഇംഗ്ലീഷോ രണ്ടുമോ?
```

## Template: comment mining sheet

```csv
Account,Post (topic),Comment (copy exactly),Type (question/complaint/praise/request),Theme,Language
```

## Template: persona card

```
PERSONA: [name], [age], [place]
Evidence: [5 conversations, 50 comments, Trends]
Language: Malayalam / English / Manglish / mix
Phone and data: ______________________
Platforms used and when: ______________
Wants: _______________________________
Problems and frustrations: ____________
Questions they ask (real quotes):
  1. "____________"  2. "____________"
What makes them trust a page: _________
What makes them share or save: ________
What makes them act (message, visit, buy): ____
What I must never do (turn-offs): _____
```

## Common mistakes

- **Asking "would you follow a page like this?"** People say yes to be polite. Ask about what they actually did last time.
- **Inventing the persona.** If a detail didn't come from research, delete it or mark it as a guess to test.
- **Reading Trends as search counts.** The 0–100 scale is relative interest in that place and time, not a number of searches.
- **Only talking to friends who love you.** Include at least two people who don't know your page.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Which question gives the most reliable information in an audience conversation?
    - A) "Will you follow me?"
    - B) "What was the last post you sent to someone, and why?"
    - C) "Is my idea good?"
    - D) "Would you like my page?"
2. In Google Trends, a value of 100 means:
    - A) The peak of relative interest for that term in your chosen time and place
    - B) 100 searches
    - C) A trending hashtag
    - D) 100% of people searched it
3. "Watches Reels at night and searches YouTube before buying" is which kind of segmentation?
    - A) None
    - B) Behavioural
    - C) Demographic
    - D) Geographic
4. What should a persona be built from?
    - A) A competitor's bio
    - B) Real conversations, comments and search data
    - C) A stock photo
    - D) Your imagination

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** OpenStax 5.1, Google Trends help and YouTube's audience guide (about 1 hour)
- **Action:** talk to 5 people, mine 50 comments, run 3 Trends comparisons and write your persona. It is done when your proof is saved: notes from 5 conversations, the 50-comment sheet with themes, 3 Trends screenshots and your persona, saved in 02 Strategy.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **B.** Questions about real past behaviour are more honest than opinions about the future.
2. **A.** Trends shows relative interest on a 0–100 scale.
3. **B.** It describes how people behave on the platforms.
4. **B.** Evidence-based personas are tools; invented ones are fiction.

sections.title: SMM-M02-L03: Niche, positioning and competitor analysis
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Study 3 to 5 competing accounts, find the gap you can fill, and write a positioning statement for your account that makes it different and easy to remember. **Time:** about 2 hours 30 minutes (50 minutes study, 1 hour 40 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### A niche is topic + audience + angle

"Food" is a topic. "Food in Kozhikode" adds a place. "Honest, under-₹200 food spots around Kuttiady, with price and location in every post" adds an angle. The narrower and clearer your niche, the easier it is for people (and recommendation systems) to understand who your posts are for. You can widen it later.

### Competitor analysis in five steps

1. **Choose 3–5 accounts:** two **direct** competitors (same topic, same area), one **indirect** (same audience, different topic) and one or two **aspirational** (bigger accounts you'd like to be like).
2. **Record the basics:** followers, posts a week, main formats, language, how they write bios and captions.
3. **Find their best posts.** On YouTube, open the channel and sort videos by **Popular**. On Instagram, scroll their Reels tab and note the ones with the highest view counts. Write down the topic, the hook and the format of the top 3.
4. **Read the comments** on those posts: what do people ask that isn't answered?
5. **Check if they run ads:** Meta's Ad Library lets anyone search the ads a Page is running on Facebook and Instagram. If a competitor has run the same ad for months, it's probably working.

Then look for **gaps**: questions nobody answers, formats nobody uses well, a language gap (no good Malayalam explanations), a place gap (no one covers your panchayat), or a quality gap (everyone posts blurry photos).

### Positioning: the place you want in people's minds

OpenStax describes positioning as deciding and communicating how you want your market to think and feel about you, either **head-to-head** (better at the same thing) or by **differentiation** (different in a way that matters). Small accounts almost always win by differentiation.

Write it as one statement:

**For [audience] who [want or need], [@handle] is the [kind of account] that [main benefit], unlike [alternatives], because [proof or angle].**

If you are positioning a business rather than an account, the Entrepreneurship course covers business positioning and naming in ENT-M06-L01.

### Don't copy, learn

Study competitors for patterns (formats, hooks, posting rhythm), never to copy their words, photos or videos. Copying breaks platform rules and the law, and it makes you a weaker version of them.

## Local example

Anu analysed four accounts:

| Account (made up) | Type | Followers | Posts a week | Best format | What they do well | Gap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| @kozhikode.eats | Direct, bigger city | 85,000 | 6 | Reels with price on screen | Fast cuts, clear prices | Almost nothing from Kuttiady side |
| @vatakara.news | Direct, local news | 22,000 | 10 | Photo posts with long text | Quick news | Often no source; no food or shops |
| A Malayalam vlogger | Aspirational | 400,000 | 2 | 10-minute YouTube videos | Storytelling | Never covers small towns |
| A local college page | Indirect | 6,000 | 3 | Event Stories | Students share everything | Only campus |

Gap: nobody gives honest, current, price-and-location posts for the Kuttiady area, in Malayalam, with checked facts. Her positioning:

"For people in and around Kuttiady (and those missing home in the Gulf) who want to know what's good nearby, @kuttiady.diaries is the local page that shows real places with price and location in every post, unlike big city pages and unchecked forwards, because Anu visits every place herself and checks before she posts."

(Made-up accounts and numbers.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [OpenStax Principles of Marketing 5.6: Product Positioning](https://openstax.org/books/principles-marketing/pages/5-6-product-positioning) | Read positioning statements and perceptual maps | 30 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Meta Transparency Center: Meta Ad Library tools](https://transparency.meta.com/researchtools/ad-library-tools/) | Open the Ad Library from this page and search for two local businesses or competitors | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 (page title checked) |
| [Instagram for Creators: Best practices hub](https://creators.instagram.com/best-practices) | In "Get started", read the Profile and Reels pages | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 50 minutes).
2. Choose 3–5 accounts: two direct, one indirect, one or two aspirational.
3. Fill in the competitor sheet for each, including their top 3 posts and the questions people ask in comments.
4. Write down at least three gaps you could fill.
5. Write your positioning statement and test it on two people from your research: can they repeat what your page is about after hearing it once?

**Proof to record:** Your competitor sheet for 3–5 accounts, your list of gaps and your positioning statement, saved in 02 Strategy.

## Template: competitor sheet (the Competitors tab)

```csv
Account,Platform,Type (direct/indirect/aspirational),Followers,Posts a week,Main formats,Language,Top 3 posts (topic and views),Hooks they use,Questions in comments,Runs ads? (Ad Library),What they do well,Gap I can fill
```

## Template: positioning statement

```
For ______________________ (audience)
who ______________________ (want or need),
@________ is the ______________ (kind of account)
that ______________________ (main benefit),
unlike ____________________ (alternatives),
because ___________________ (proof or angle).

Test: two people repeat it back in their own words?
Person 1: ______________  Person 2: ______________
```

## Common mistakes

- **Only studying huge accounts.** Include direct local competitors; their audience is your audience.
- **Copying a competitor's posts.** Learn the pattern, never take the content.
- **A niche too wide to remember.** If you need two sentences to explain the page, narrow it.
- **Competing head-to-head with a much bigger page.** Differentiate: a different place, language, angle or quality.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Which is the clearest niche?
    - A) Food
    - B) Everything local
    - C) Kerala
    - D) Honest under-₹200 food spots around Kuttiady, with price and location in every post
2. What does Meta's Ad Library let you do?
    - A) Buy followers
    - B) See a page's private messages
    - C) Download competitors' videos
    - D) Search the ads that Pages are running on Facebook and Instagram
3. How do small accounts usually win against much bigger ones?
    - A) By posting at midnight
    - B) By differentiation: a place, language, angle or quality the big ones don't serve
    - C) By copying them
    - D) Head-to-head on the same posts
4. An "aspirational" competitor is:
    - A) A fake account
    - B) A bigger account you learn patterns from
    - C) An account you copy
    - D) A client

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** OpenStax 5.6 on positioning, Meta's Ad Library and Instagram's profile guidance (about 50 minutes)
- **Action:** analyse 3–5 competitors, list the gaps and write a tested positioning statement. It is done when your proof is saved: your competitor sheet for 3–5 accounts, your list of gaps and your positioning statement, saved in 02 Strategy.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **D.** It combines a topic, an audience and an angle.
2. **D.** It's a public transparency tool for ads.
3. **B.** Differentiation gives people a reason to follow you as well.
4. **B.** You study it for patterns in formats, hooks and rhythm.

sections.title: SMM-M02-L04: Content pillars and brand voice
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Choose 3 to 5 content pillars that serve your persona, fill your Ideas tab with 20 ideas, and write a brand voice chart for Malayalam and English. **Time:** about 1 hour 30 minutes (25 minutes study, 1 hour 5 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Pillars: the few things you always talk about

A content pillar is one of the 3 to 5 big themes your page covers. Pillars keep you consistent (people know what to expect) and stop you running out of ideas (each pillar has endless posts in it). Build them from your research: each pillar should answer a real need of your persona.

For a hyperlocal page, for example:

1. **Eat:** honest food spots with price and location
2. **Know:** useful local updates: timings, new shops, events, roadworks (checked)
3. **People:** short stories of local shop owners, craftspeople and helpers (with consent)
4. **Nostalgia and places:** old photos (your own or with permission), rivers, hills, festivals

A rough rule: most posts should help, entertain or inform; only a few should sell. For a business, pillars might be **show** (product and process), **teach** (useful tips), **prove** (results and reviews with permission), **personal** (the story behind it) and **offer**. The Entrepreneurship course uses these for business content in ENT-M06-L02.

### Series: pillars on autopilot

A **series** is a repeating format inside a pillar: "₹100 Friday" (a food spot under ₹100 every Friday), "Shop of the week", "Then and now". Series are easier to make, easier for followers to recognise and easier to batch.

### Brand voice: how you sound

Your voice is your page's personality in words. Write it down so it stays the same whether you're tired, happy or writing at midnight. A **voice chart** lists three to four traits, each with what it means and what it doesn't:

| We are | That means | We are not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Friendly | Talk like a helpful neighbour; use "നമ്മുടെ" | Over-familiar or slangy with strangers |
| Honest | Say the price, say when something was average | Paid hype or fake "best ever" |
| Local | Use place names, local words and humour | Cliquey or mocking other areas |
| Careful | Check facts; say "as of today" | Rumours, forwards, politics |

### Language rules

Decide, and write down, how you'll mix languages: for example "Malayalam in speech and on-screen text, English in the first line of the caption for search, Manglish never in the on-screen text". SMM-M04-L02 goes deeper.

### A light visual identity

Two colours, one or two fonts (one that supports Malayalam well, such as Manjari or Noto Sans Malayalam), and one photo style (daylight, real places, no stock photos). Use them on every cover and thumbnail.

## Local example

Anu's pillars and series for @kuttiady.diaries:

| Pillar | Share of posts | Series | Funnel job |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Eat | 40% | "₹100 Friday" | Awareness, shares |
| Know | 25% | "This week near you" (Sunday) | Follows, saves |
| People | 20% | "Shop story" (owner speaks, 45 seconds) | Trust, shares |
| Places and nostalgia | 15% | "Then and now" (her own old family photos) | Shares from the Gulf |

Her voice: friendly, honest, local, careful. Her rule: "If I can't check it, I don't post it." Her language rule: Malayalam speech and on-screen text, an English first line for search.

She filled her Ideas tab with 24 ideas in 40 minutes, six per pillar.

(Made up to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Instagram for Creators: Best practices hub](https://creators.instagram.com/best-practices) | In "Creation", read the pages on creating engaging and original content | 15 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Canva Design School: Marketing with Canva](https://www.canva.com/en/design-school/courses/marketing-with-canva) | Free sign-up. Watch the lesson "Optimizing brand presence" | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the two resources (about 25 minutes).
2. Choose 3–5 pillars from your research, each linked to a need of your persona.
3. Create 2 series ideas you could repeat every week.
4. Fill your Ideas tab with at least 20 ideas: at least 4 per pillar, each with a format and a hook idea.
5. Write your voice chart and language rules, and pick your two colours and fonts.

**Proof to record:** Your pillars and series, 20 or more ideas in the Ideas tab, and your voice chart with language rules, saved in 02 Strategy.

## Template: content pillars

```
PILLAR 1: ________  (share of posts: __%)
  Persona need it serves: ______________
  Funnel job: awareness / trust / action
  Series: "__________" every ________
  Ideas: 1. ______ 2. ______ 3. ______ 4. ______
PILLAR 2: ________  (repeat)
PILLAR 3: ________
PILLAR 4: ________ (optional)
PILLAR 5: ________ (optional)
```

## Template: voice chart and language rules

```
WE ARE      | THAT MEANS            | WE ARE NOT
____________ | _____________________ | __________
____________ | _____________________ | __________
____________ | _____________________ | __________

WORDS WE USE: ________________________
WORDS WE NEVER USE: __________________
LANGUAGE RULES
  Speech in videos: Malayalam / English / mix
  On-screen text: ______________________
  Caption first line: __________________
  Hashtags: ____________________________
VISUALS
  Colours: ______ (hex) and ______ (hex)
  Fonts: ______ (Malayalam) ______ (English)
  Photo style: _________________________
```

## Common mistakes

- **Too many pillars.** Eight themes means none of them is clear. Start with 3 or 4.
- **Pillars about you, not them.** Each pillar must answer a need from your research.
- **Voice that changes with your mood.** Write the chart and check every caption against it.
- **Mixing scripts randomly.** Decide where Malayalam, English and Manglish go, and stick to it.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. What is a content pillar?
    - A) One of 3–5 main themes your page always covers
    - B) A paid ad
    - C) A hashtag
    - D) One viral post
2. Why are series useful?
    - A) They are easier to make, batch and recognise
    - B) Platforms pay for them
    - C) They avoid all rules
    - D) They replace pillars
3. A voice chart line "Honest, not paid hype" helps you:
    - A) Write captions that sound the same and stay trustworthy
    - B) Avoid using Malayalam
    - C) Post less
    - D) Get more hashtags

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** Instagram's guidance on engaging, original content and Canva's brand presence lesson (about 25 minutes)
- **Action:** choose your pillars and series, add 20 ideas and write your voice chart. It is done when your proof is saved: your pillars and series, 20 or more ideas in the Ideas tab, and your voice chart with language rules, saved in 02 Strategy.
- **Quiz:** at least 2 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **A.** Pillars give a page consistency and an endless source of ideas.
2. **A.** A repeating format saves time and builds habits in your audience.
3. **A.** A written voice keeps your tone consistent across every post.

sections.title: Module 3: Platforms in depth
sections.summary: Learn what each platform is for and its current rules, optimise every profile you'll use, and choose a platform mix you can keep up.
sections.content:
## Overview

Platforms differ in who uses them, what formats they reward and how people find content. In three weeks you'll go deep on Instagram, YouTube, Facebook and WhatsApp Business, then look at LinkedIn, X, Threads, Telegram and Indian apps, and choose one main and one support platform for your page. Every platform fact is dated, because they change.

From week 5 you post three times a week. By the end of week 7 your profiles are optimised and your platform plan is written.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Use Instagram Reels, trial reels, carousels and Stories for the right jobs
- Set up a YouTube channel and plan Shorts and long videos
- Run WhatsApp Business with a catalogue, quick replies, labels, Status and Channels
- Use Facebook Pages and local Groups within their rules
- Choose a platform mix with a scored matrix and set up a LinkedIn career profile

## Time

About 14 hours in total: 12 hours of lessons and 2 hours for the module project. Part-time: weeks 5–7.

**Full-time track:** When you finish this module, your growth project starts: every day of posting from now on counts towards it. Read SMM-M17-L01 now and set your growth target, then carry on with Module 4.

## Lessons

1. SMM-M03-L01: Instagram: Reels, Stories, carousels and your profile (about 3 hours 30 minutes)
2. SMM-M03-L02: YouTube: Shorts, long-form and your channel (about 3 hours)
3. SMM-M03-L03: Facebook Pages and Groups, and WhatsApp Business (about 3 hours)
4. SMM-M03-L04: LinkedIn, X, Threads, Telegram and Indian platforms: choosing your mix (about 2 hours 30 minutes)

## Module project: Your platform plan and optimised profiles

1. Put before and after screenshots of every profile you optimised (Instagram, YouTube, WhatsApp Business, Facebook if used, LinkedIn) in 03 Platforms.
2. Write a one-page platform plan: main and support platforms and why, posts a week on each, which formats, and how one post becomes several (you'll refine this in Module 6).
3. Add your rules for each platform: hashtag count, music source, caption language, posting days.
4. Check every bio, link and phone number works by opening them from another phone.

**Proof to record:** Before and after screenshots of each profile and your one-page platform plan.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3. If a row is a 1, redo that part first.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Instagram | Profile unclear | Some fields optimised | Every checklist item done; Reel, carousel and Stories posted |
| YouTube | No channel | Channel without description or verification | Verified, described, first Short live, long video planned |
| WhatsApp Business | Not installed | Profile only | Profile, catalogue, quick replies, labels and Status working |
| Platform choice | Posting everywhere at random | A choice without reasons | A scored matrix with one main and one support platform |
| Rules and accuracy | Unaware of current limits | Knows some | Knows and follows current limits, with dates, and checks them |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, when PSC prep or work leaves little time:

- Optimise only your Instagram profile and post one Reel.
- Set up the YouTube channel basics and post one Short; skip the long-video plan.
- Set up the WhatsApp Business profile and two quick replies.
- Fill in the platform matrix for your own account only.

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, read the front, say the answer, then check. Repeat the ones you missed the next day.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| Longest Instagram Reel that can be recommended to non-followers? | 3 minutes (as of October 2026). |
| Maximum items in an Instagram carousel? | 20 photos or videos. |
| Hashtag limit in an Instagram caption since December 2025? | Five. |
| What does a trial reel do? | Shows a reel to non-followers first so you can test it, with results after about 24 hours. |
| YouTube Shorts: maximum length and shape? | Up to 3 minutes, square or vertical (uploads since 15 October 2024). |
| What happens to a Short over 1 minute with an active Content ID claim? | It is blocked worldwide until the claim is resolved. |
| YouTube first Partner Program level in India? | 500 subscribers, 3 uploads in 90 days, and 3,000 watch hours in 12 months or 3 million Shorts views in 90 days. |
| Can WhatsApp Channel followers reply? | No: they can react with emoji or vote in polls. |
| A beginner's platform mix? | One main, one support, plus WhatsApp for conversations. |
| TikTok in India? | Blocked since June 2020. |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Optimising once and forgetting.** Check your profiles every month; links break and hours change.
- **Using one video file everywhere without adjusting.** Same idea, but check shape, length, music and captions for each platform.
- **Ignoring WhatsApp because it isn't "social media".** For local business it is where most sales happen.

tasks.detail: **Proof to record:** Before and after screenshots of each profile and your one-page platform plan.

sections.title: SMM-M03-L01: Instagram: Reels, Stories, carousels and your profile
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Know what each Instagram format is for and its current limits, optimise your profile so the right people understand and find it in seconds, and publish a Reel, a carousel and Stories. **Time:** about 3 hours 30 minutes (1 hour study, 2 hours 30 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### The formats and what each is for (as of October 2026)

| Format | What it is | Best for | Current limits and tips |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Reels** | Vertical video, shown to followers and non-followers | Reaching new people | Reels up to 3 minutes can be recommended to non-followers in the Reels tab and Explore. Use 9:16, hook in the first 3 seconds, no other app's watermark. |
| **Trial reels** | A reel shown first only to non-followers | Testing an idea without risking your followers' feed | Results after about 24 hours; then share it to your profile or leave it. For professional accounts. |
| **Carousels** | Up to 20 photos or videos in one post | Saving and sharing: guides, lists, before and after, price lists | The profile grid shows rectangles since January 2025, so keep key text in the middle of the cover. Adding audio can help photos and carousels show in the Reels tab. |
| **Stories** | Photos or videos that disappear after 24 hours | Talking to people who already follow you | Polls, questions and link stickers start conversations. Save the best in **Highlights** on your profile. |
| **Live** | Real-time video | Q&A, events, launches | Announce it in Stories first. |
| **Broadcast channels** | One-to-many messages to followers who join | Updates for your keenest followers | Listed among Instagram's creator tools. |
| **DMs** | Private messages | Turning interest into enquiries | Reply fast; set up saved replies. |

### Professional account: creator or business

A professional account is public, gets **Insights** and can check **Account Status** (whether its content can be recommended). Choose **Creator** for a page or a personal brand and **Business** for a shop or service. Instagram's help pages explain the difference and how to switch. One practical difference to check: Instagram's licensed music library isn't available in the same way to every account, so business accounts may see a smaller selection of music, such as Meta's royalty-free Sound Collection (as of October 2026).

### Your profile is a 3-second test

A new visitor decides in seconds whether to follow. Instagram's own tips say to put **keywords in your handle, profile name, bio and captions**, because search reads them. Optimise each part:

- **Username (handle):** short, easy to spell, the same on every platform: @kuttiady.diaries
- **Name field:** the keyword people search for, not just your name: "Kuttiady | Food, Shops, Local news"
- **Bio (who + what + proof + action):** "Real places around Kuttiady with price and location. Visited and checked by Anu. New post every Mon, Wed, Fri. Tag us or DM to suggest a spot."
- **Links:** Instagram allows up to five links in your bio (since April 2023): for example your WhatsApp Channel, YouTube and a Google Form for suggestions.
- **Contact buttons** (business accounts): call, WhatsApp, directions.
- **Highlights:** 3–5 with simple covers: "Start here", "Food", "Ask us", "Rules".
- **Pinned posts:** pin your best and most typical posts to the top of your grid.

### Hashtags and captions

Since December 2025 Instagram limits captions to **five hashtags**, and says fewer, more targeted ones work better than many generic ones such as #reels or #explore (as of October 2026). Put keywords and hashtags in the caption, not in a comment.

### Views is the main number

Since August 2024, **Views** is the main metric across Reels, photos, carousels and Stories in Insights, counting repeat views. Look at how many views came from **non-followers**: that is your growth.

## Local example

**Peak Fitness**, a gym in Vatakara, had the handle @peak_fitness_vtk_official_2019, the name field "Peak Fitness", a bio with three emojis and no location, and no Highlights. New visitors couldn't tell what it was or where.

After an hour of work: handle @peakfitness.vatakara; name field "Gym in Vatakara | Peak Fitness"; bio "Strength and weight-loss training for beginners. Women's batch 6–8 am. First session free. WhatsApp below 👇"; links to WhatsApp and the timetable; Highlights "Batches", "Fees", "Results (with permission)", "Find us".

They posted a carousel, "5 machines beginners use wrongly", and a 30-second Reel of a trainer fixing a squat. Over the next four weeks, profile visits rose from about 40 to 160 a week, and the gym started asking every new member how they'd heard about it: 6 of 19 said Instagram.

(Peak Fitness and its numbers are made up to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Instagram for Creators: Finding success on reels in 2025](https://creators.instagram.com/blog/the-latest-with-instagram) | Read the whole post: 3-minute reels, trial reels and audio on photos | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Instagram Help: Set up a professional account](https://help.instagram.com/502981923235522) | Open it and follow the steps if your account isn't professional yet | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 (page title checked) |
| [Instagram Help: About business and creator accounts](https://help.instagram.com/iphone-app/138925576505882) | Read the difference between business and creator accounts | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 (page title checked) |
| [TechCrunch: Instagram trial reels (December 2024)](https://techcrunch.com/2024/12/10/instagram-rolls-out-trial-reels-that-arent-shown-to-a-creators-followers) | Read how trial reels work | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Metricool: Instagram carousels up to 20 photos or videos (August 2024)](https://metricool.com/instagram-increases-carousel-content-limit/) | Note the 20-item carousel limit | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Social Samosa: Instagram limits hashtags to five per post (December 2025)](https://www.socialsamosa.com/news-2/instagram-hashtags-five-per-post-10923075) | Read why Instagram cut hashtags to five | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Social Samosa: Instagram makes Views its main metric (August 2024)](https://socialsamosa.com/news-2/instagram-updates-metrics-creators-prioritise-reach-6807009) | Read what changed when Views became the main metric | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [TechCrunch: Instagram allows up to five links in bio (April 2023)](https://techcrunch.com/2023/04/18/instagram-takes-on-linktree-and-others-with-support-for-up-to-5-links-in-bio/) | Read how to add up to five links | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 45 minutes).
2. Check your account is professional (Creator for a page or personal brand). Open Account Status and screenshot it.
3. Screenshot your profile as it is now ("before").
4. Optimise it with the checklist: handle, name field keyword, bio formula, links, Highlights with simple covers, pinned posts.
5. Publish one Reel (vertical, hook in the first 3 seconds) and one carousel (5–10 slides) that fit your pillars. If trial reels are available to you, publish the Reel as a trial first.
6. Post 3 Stories over the week, including one poll or question sticker, and save one to a Highlight.
7. Screenshot your profile again ("after") and log the posts.

**Proof to record:** Before and after screenshots of your profile, your Account Status screenshot, and links to the Reel and carousel with their Posting Log rows.

## Template: Instagram profile checklist

```
[ ] Professional account (Creator or Business)
[ ] Account Status checked: no issues
[ ] Handle: short, easy to spell, same everywhere
[ ] Name field includes the keyword people search
[ ] Bio: who it's for + what they get + proof + action
[ ] Links (up to 5): WhatsApp / YouTube / form / site
[ ] Contact buttons (business): call, WhatsApp, directions
[ ] 3-5 Highlights with simple covers
[ ] Best posts pinned to the top
[ ] Profile photo clear at small size
[ ] Location or service area clear
```

## Template: bio formula (English and Malayalam)

```
[Who it's for] + [what they get] + [proof] + [action]

EN: Real places around Kuttiady with price and
    location. Visited and checked. New posts Mon,
    Wed, Fri. DM us a spot to feature!
ML: കുറ്റ്യാടിയിലെ നല്ല സ്ഥലങ്ങൾ, വിലയും ലൊക്കേഷനും സഹിതം.
    നേരിട്ട് പോയി നോക്കിയവ മാത്രം.
    പുതിയ പോസ്റ്റ് തിങ്കൾ, ബുധൻ, വെള്ളി.
    നിങ്ങളുടെ ഇഷ്ട സ്ഥലം DM ചെയ്യൂ!
```

## Template: format quick card

```
REEL: 9:16 vertical, 1080 x 1920, hook in 3 s,
      up to 3 min, no other app's watermark,
      captions on screen, audio added
CAROUSEL: up to 20 slides; cover slide = hook;
      last slide = call to action; key text
      in the middle (grid shows rectangles)
STORY: 9:16; 24 hours; add a poll or question;
      save the best to a Highlight
CAPTION: first line = hook; keywords in the text;
      max 5 hashtags, specific not generic
```

## Common mistakes

- **A handle full of underscores and numbers.** If people can't remember or spell it, they can't find you. Make it short and clear.
- **A bio about you instead of the visitor.** Say who it's for and what they get, then give one action.
- **Posting horizontal videos as Reels.** Shoot vertical 9:16 from the start (SMM-M04-L03).
- **Generic hashtags.** Five specific tags (#kuttiady #kozhikodefood) beat #reels #viral #explore.
- **Ignoring Stories.** Stories are where followers talk back. Use polls and questions every week.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. How many hashtags does Instagram now allow in a caption, as reported in December 2025?
    - A) 10
    - B) Unlimited
    - C) 30
    - D) 5
2. What is a trial reel?
    - A) A reel only your followers see
    - B) A deleted reel
    - C) A reel shown first to non-followers so you can test it
    - D) A paid ad
3. Where does Instagram suggest putting keywords so people can find you in search?
    - A) In your password
    - B) Only in comments
    - C) Nowhere; search ignores text
    - D) In your handle, profile name, bio and captions
4. Which format is usually best for reaching people who don't follow you yet?
    - A) DMs
    - B) Reels
    - C) Highlights
    - D) Stories

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** Instagram's creator posts and help pages, plus dated reports on reels, carousels, hashtags and views (about 45 minutes)
- **Action:** optimise your Instagram profile and publish a Reel, a carousel and Stories. It is done when your proof is saved: before and after screenshots of your profile, your Account Status screenshot, and links to the Reel and carousel with their Posting Log rows.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **D.** Instagram limited captions to five hashtags and says fewer, targeted ones work better.
2. **C.** Trial reels go to non-followers first; you see results after about 24 hours.
3. **D.** Instagram's tips name the handle, profile name, bio and captions.
4. **B.** Reels are recommended to non-followers in the Reels tab and Explore.

sections.title: SMM-M03-L02: YouTube: Shorts, long-form and your channel
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Set up and optimise a YouTube channel, understand when to use Shorts and when to use long videos, and publish your first Short. **Time:** about 3 hours (1 hour study, 2 hours action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Two kinds of YouTube

| | **Shorts** | **Long-form videos** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shape and length | Square or vertical, up to 3 minutes (for uploads since 15 October 2024) | Usually horizontal 16:9, any length |
| How people find them | Swiping in the Shorts feed | Search, home page, suggested videos |
| What they build | Reach and discovery | Trust, depth and search traffic for months or years |
| Effort | Low to medium | Medium to high |

A good beginner plan: **Shorts for discovery, long videos for trust.** For example, a 40-second Short answers one question; a 10-minute video answers the whole topic and appears in search for years.

### Music and Shorts: a trap to avoid

YouTube's rule (as of October 2026): a Short **longer than 1 minute** with an active Content ID copyright claim is **blocked worldwide**. It can't be watched, recommended or earn money until the claim is released. So for Shorts over a minute, use music from YouTube's own libraries: most Shorts audio library songs can be used for up to 90 seconds in a 3-minute Short, and royalty-free tracks from the **YouTube Audio Library** in YouTube Studio won't get a Content ID claim. Module 14 covers copyright properly.

### How YouTube decides what to show

Recommendations use watch history, search history, subscriptions, likes, dislikes, "Not interested" clicks and satisfaction surveys. Search ranks videos by **relevance** (how well the title, description, tags and the video itself match the search), **engagement** (for example watch time for that search) and **quality** (signs of expertise and trustworthiness). YouTube says it doesn't accept payment for better placement in organic search. SMM-M07-L01 covers YouTube SEO.

### Set up your channel properly

- **Name and handle:** the same as your Instagram page.
- **Description:** the first two lines say who it's for and what they get, with your main keywords: "Kuttiady food, shops and local news in Malayalam. New Shorts every Mon, Wed and Fri."
- **Banner and profile picture:** make the banner in Canva; keep text in the centre so it isn't cut off on phones.
- **Links and contact:** WhatsApp Channel, Instagram, a business email.
- **Verify your account** with a phone number. Custom thumbnails need a verified account, and custom thumbnails for Shorts can only be added in YouTube Studio on a computer (as of October 2026).
- **Upload defaults** (in YouTube Studio settings): a default description with your links saves time on every upload.

### Thumbnails in one paragraph

For long videos, upload a 16:9 image (YouTube recommends high resolution and a minimum width of 640 pixels; 1280 × 720 is a common, light size). From the phone the file must be under 2 MB. One face or object, 3–5 big words, strong contrast (SMM-M04-L05).

### The YouTube Partner Program, honestly

YouTube's expanded Partner Program is available in India (as of October 2026). The first level (fan funding and Shopping features) needs **500 subscribers, 3 public uploads in the last 90 days, and either 3,000 watch hours in 12 months or 3 million Shorts views in 90 days**. Sharing ad revenue needs **1,000 subscribers and either 4,000 watch hours in 12 months or 10 million Shorts views in 90 days**. Most new channels take many months to get there, and many never do, so treat it as a later bonus, not the plan (Module 10). Check current rules before you rely on these numbers.

### Apps

- **YouTube Studio** (phone and computer): analytics, comments, video details.
- **YouTube Create**: Google's free phone editor with a royalty-free music library, captions and voiceover. It needs Android 8.0 or later and at least 4 GB of RAM, so it may not run on older phones (SMM-M04-L04 has alternatives).

## Local example

**Fathima's PSC Sprint** (from the Entrepreneurship course) runs a Malayalam YouTube channel for Kerala PSC learners:

- **Shorts, Monday to Saturday:** one PSC question in 30–45 seconds, answer explained in Malayalam, ending "Full weekly test every Sunday".
- **One long video every Sunday:** "This week's 20 questions explained", 12–15 minutes with chapters, a thumbnail with the week number and a clear title such as "Kerala PSC LDC 2026: 20 Kerala history questions explained (Malayalam)".
- **Music:** none in the questions; a soft track from the YouTube Audio Library in the intro of long videos.

After three months, most new subscribers came from Shorts, but most watch time came from the Sunday videos, because people searched for them. Each format did a different job.

(Made-up example to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [YouTube Help: Understand three-minute YouTube Shorts](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/15424877) | Read the whole page, especially the copyright rule for Shorts over 1 minute | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Creators (free official guides)](https://www.youtube.com/creators/) | In "Create", read the Shorts and Longform pages | 20 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Help: How YouTube search works](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/16090438) | Read how search ranks videos | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Help: Add custom thumbnails](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/72431) | Read the thumbnail requirements | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Help: Overview of the expanded YouTube Partner Program](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13429240) | Read the eligibility thresholds and what each level unlocks | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 55 minutes).
2. Set up your channel with the checklist: handle, keyword description, banner, links, contact email and upload defaults.
3. Verify your account with your phone number in YouTube Studio settings.
4. Upload your first Short: a 20–45 second vertical video that fits a pillar. Use your original video file (not one downloaded from Instagram with its watermark).
5. Write a one-paragraph plan for one long video you will make in Module 4: topic, title, 5 chapter headings.

**Proof to record:** Screenshots of your channel page and verification status, the link to your first Short with its Posting Log row, and your long-video plan.

## Template: channel setup checklist

```
[ ] Channel name and handle match your Instagram
[ ] Description: line 1 who it's for, line 2 what they
    get + main keywords; posting schedule
[ ] Banner made in Canva, text in the safe centre
[ ] Profile picture clear at small size
[ ] Links: WhatsApp Channel, Instagram, email
[ ] Account verified (phone number)
[ ] Upload defaults: description with links, category,
    language set to Malayalam or English
[ ] YouTube Studio app installed, comments notifications on
```

## Template: Shorts and long-form plan

```
SHORTS (discovery)
  Series name: ______________  How often: ______
  Length: ___ seconds  Hook style: ____________
  Music: none / Shorts library / Audio Library
  Ending line: points to the long video or Channel

LONG VIDEO (trust and search)
  Topic: ____________________________________
  Title with the search phrase: ______________
  Chapters: 00:00 Intro / ____ / ____ / ____ / ____
  Thumbnail idea (3-5 words): ________________
```

## Common mistakes

- **Copyrighted film songs in Shorts.** Over a minute, a claim blocks the Short worldwide. Use YouTube's libraries or no music.
- **Uploading Instagram downloads with the watermark.** Export your original file and upload that.
- **An empty channel description.** The first two lines help viewers and search understand the channel.
- **Chasing the Partner Program in month one.** Build useful videos first; the thresholds come later, if at all.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. What happens to a 2-minute Short with an active Content ID claim, according to YouTube Help?
    - A) It earns money for you
    - B) It becomes a long video
    - C) It is blocked worldwide until the claim is resolved
    - D) Nothing
2. Which three elements does YouTube say it prioritises in search?
    - A) Hashtags, likes and time of day
    - B) Subscribers only
    - C) Relevance, engagement and quality
    - D) Price, length and colour
3. Why is verifying your YouTube account useful early on?
    - A) It is required to watch videos
    - B) Custom thumbnails need a verified account
    - C) It removes ads
    - D) It doubles your views
4. Which is a sensible beginner plan?
    - A) Wait for 1,000 subscribers before posting long videos
    - B) Shorts for discovery and long videos for trust and search
    - C) Only reposts
    - D) Only 1-hour videos

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** YouTube's Shorts, search, thumbnail and Partner Program help pages and the Creators guides (about 55 minutes)
- **Action:** set up and verify your channel, publish your first Short and plan one long video. It is done when your proof is saved: screenshots of your channel page and verification status, the link to your first Short with its Posting Log row, and your long-video plan.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **C.** Shorts over one minute with an active claim are blocked globally.
2. **C.** YouTube lists relevance, engagement and quality.
3. **B.** You can upload your own thumbnails only if your account is verified.
4. **B.** The two formats do different jobs and support each other.

sections.title: SMM-M03-L03: Facebook Pages and Groups, and WhatsApp Business
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Set up WhatsApp Business with a catalogue, quick replies and labels, understand Status, Channels and business broadcasts and their rules, and decide how Facebook Pages and local Groups fit your plan. **Time:** about 3 hours (50 minutes study, 2 hours 10 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Facebook: older audiences, local groups and Reels

Many local customers, especially older ones, still discover and discuss businesses on Facebook, often in local Groups. A **Facebook Page** gives a business a public presence with posts, Reels, reviews and events. You can post to a Page and an Instagram account together from **Meta Business Suite**, which also lets you schedule posts and Stories for both and reply to messages and comments in one inbox.

Two rules to know (as of October 2026):

- **Original content wins.** In July 2025 Meta said Facebook accounts that repeatedly repost other people's text, photos or videos get lower distribution and can lose access to monetisation. Reactions, commentary and joining trends are fine; plain reposting is not.
- **Groups have their own rules.** Local buy-and-sell and community groups are powerful, but each admin sets rules about promotion. Read them, help first, and promote only where it's allowed.

### WhatsApp Business: the shop counter in your customer's pocket

For most small businesses in Kerala, WhatsApp is where enquiries turn into sales. The free **WhatsApp Business** app adds tools on top of normal WhatsApp (as of October 2026):

- **Business profile:** description, address or service area, hours, email, website
- **Catalogue:** products or services with photos, prices and descriptions that customers can browse and share
- **Greeting and away messages:** automatic replies when someone first messages or when you're closed
- **Quick replies:** saved answers to common questions, typed with a shortcut such as /price
- **Labels and lists:** sort chats, such as New enquiry, Order confirmed, Paid, Delivered
- **Customer notes:** remember details like "prefers eggless cakes"
- **Message statistics** and **ads that click to WhatsApp** (Module 9)

### Status, Channels and broadcasts

| Tool | Who sees it | Good for | Know this |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Status** | Your contacts who have your number saved, for 24 hours | Daily specials, behind the scenes | Feels personal; post 1–3 a day at most |
| **Channel** | Anyone who follows it | Regular updates for many people | One-way: followers can't reply, only react with emoji or vote in polls. Followers don't see the admin's name, photo or number. Creating a channel is still rolling out, so it may not be available to everyone yet. |
| **Business broadcasts** | The customers you choose, as private one-to-one messages | Offers, reminders, restock alerts | Can reach customers even if they haven't saved your number; can be scheduled; shows read and reply rates. WhatsApp has been testing monthly limits and paid tiers for broadcasts, so check current rules. |

### Message only people who agreed

Send offers only to people who gave you their number for that purpose and are happy to hear from you. Tell them how to stop ("Reply STOP"). Spamming people gets you blocked and reported, and WhatsApp has been [testing limits on messages that get no reply](https://techcrunch.com/2025/10/17/whatsapp-will-curb-the-number-of-messages-people-and-businesses-can-send-without-a-response). India's data protection rules also expect clear consent for using personal data (Module 14).

## Local example

**Amma's Pickles**, a Kudumbashree unit in Perambra, set up WhatsApp Business on a second SIM:

- **Profile:** "Home-made Malabar pickles. Orders by 6 pm, delivered next day within 10 km. Mon–Sat 9–6."
- **Catalogue:** 8 pickles with photos taken in daylight, the weight and the price (₹120 for 250 g mango, ₹180 for 250 g prawn).
- **Quick replies:** /price (catalogue link), /delivery (areas and charges), /pay (UPI ID and QR), /order (how to order in three steps), in Malayalam and English.
- **Labels:** New enquiry, Confirmed, Paid, Delivered, Repeat customer.
- **Status:** one photo a day of the day's batch.
- **Channel:** "Amma's Pickles updates": weekly new flavours and festival pre-orders.

In the local Facebook group "Perambra Market" (whose rules allow selling posts on Saturdays), they post one Reel each Saturday and answer every comment. After a month, they could see from labels that 40% of new enquiries mentioned the group.

(Made-up example to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [WhatsApp Business: the built-in business tools](https://whatsappbusiness.com/resources/resource-library/small-business-use-whatsapp-business-app/) | Read the list of built-in business tools | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [WhatsApp Business: business broadcasts](https://whatsappbusiness.com/resources/resource-library/business-broadcasts-whatsapp/) | Read how business broadcasts work | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |
| [WhatsApp Help: About creating a WhatsApp Channel](https://faq.whatsapp.com/265055289421317) | Read how channels work and who sees what | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [TechCrunch: WhatsApp to limit broadcast messages (March 2025)](https://techcrunch.com/2025/03/18/whatsapp-will-soon-limit-number-of-broadcast-messages-users-and-businesses-can-send/) | Read about broadcast limits and paid tiers being tested | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |
| [Meta Business Suite app (Google Play)](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.facebook.pages.app) | Read what Meta Business Suite does; install it if you will use a Facebook Page | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [TechCrunch: Meta cracks down on unoriginal Facebook content (July 2025)](https://techcrunch.com/2025/07/14/following-youtube-meta-announces-crackdown-on-unoriginal-facebook-content) | Read what counts as unoriginal content on Facebook | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Meta Blueprint: Browse free courses from the Blueprint catalog](https://www.facebookblueprint.com/student/page/512235-browse-free-courses-from-the-blueprint-catalog) | Watch the 1-minute videos "How to create a Facebook Page" and "How to post on a Facebook Page" | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 45 minutes).
2. Install WhatsApp Business, ideally on a separate number for your page or a future client. Fill in the business profile completely.
3. Build a catalogue with 3–5 items. For a practice page, use services such as "Feature your shop (free)" or "Local event listing".
4. Write 4 quick replies in Malayalam and English, set a greeting message and an away message, and create 4 labels.
5. Post one Status and, if Channels are available to you, create a Channel for your page and post one update.
6. Facebook: either create a Page for your practice account and connect it to Instagram in Meta Business Suite, or join 3 local Facebook Groups and write down each group's promotion rules.

**Proof to record:** Screenshots of your WhatsApp Business profile, catalogue, quick replies and labels, plus your Facebook Page link or the rules of 3 local groups.

## Template: WhatsApp Business setup checklist

```
[ ] Separate number (or decided to use mine)
[ ] Profile: description, address or area, hours,
    email, links
[ ] Catalogue: 3+ items, daylight photos, prices
[ ] Greeting message (first contact)
[ ] Away message (outside hours)
[ ] Quick replies: /price /delivery /pay /order
[ ] Labels: New enquiry, Confirmed, Paid, Delivered,
    Repeat customer
[ ] Status plan: 1-3 a day at most
[ ] Channel (if available) and its link in your bios
[ ] Broadcasts only to people who agreed, with a way
    to stop
```

## Template: quick replies (English and Malayalam)

```
/order
EN: Thanks for your message! To order: 1. Choose from
    our catalogue 2. Send the item and quantity
    3. Share your location. We confirm in 10 minutes.
ML: മെസ്സേജിന് നന്ദി! ഓർഡർ ചെയ്യാൻ: 1. കാറ്റലോഗിൽ നിന്ന്
    തിരഞ്ഞെടുക്കുക 2. ഐറ്റവും എണ്ണവും അയക്കുക
    3. ലൊക്കേഷൻ ഷെയർ ചെയ്യുക. 10 മിനിറ്റിനുള്ളിൽ ഉറപ്പിക്കാം.

/away
EN: We're closed now (open Mon-Sat, 9-6). We'll reply
    first thing tomorrow.
ML: ഇപ്പോൾ കട അടച്ചിരിക്കുന്നു (തിങ്കൾ-ശനി, 9-6).
    നാളെ രാവിലെ തന്നെ മറുപടി തരാം.
```

## Template: Facebook group etiquette

```
Before posting in a group:
[ ] Read the rules and pinned posts
[ ] Check which days or posts allow promotion
[ ] Comment helpfully on others' posts for a week first
[ ] Post useful content, not only offers
[ ] Reply to every comment within a few hours
[ ] Never tag strangers or post the same thing in 10
    groups at once
```

## Common mistakes

- **Adding people to broadcasts or groups without asking.** Message only people who agreed, and give an easy way to stop.
- **A catalogue without prices.** "Price?" is the first question. Answer it before they ask.
- **Ten Status updates a day.** People mute you. One to three good ones are enough.
- **Spamming Facebook groups.** Admins remove you. Help first, follow the rules, then promote.
- **Reposting other people's videos on a Page.** Facebook lowers their reach and can remove monetisation. Make your own.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Can followers reply to a WhatsApp Channel update?
    - A) Only on weekends
    - B) No; they can react with emoji or vote in polls
    - C) Only if they pay

2. What are WhatsApp Business quick replies?
    - A) Voice calls
    - B) Automatic ads
    - C) Saved answers to common questions, typed with a shortcut
    - D) A payment method
3. What did Meta announce in July 2025 about Facebook accounts that keep reposting others' content?
    - A) Lower distribution and possible loss of monetisation
    - B) They get a badge
    - C) More reach
    - D) Nothing
4. Who should get your business broadcast offers?

    - B) Every number you can find

It is done when your proof is saved: screenshots of your WhatsApp Business profile, catalogue, quick replies and labels, plus your Facebook Page link or the rules of 3 local groups.

## Answers

1. **B.** Channels are one-way; followers react or vote.
2. **C.** They save time and keep answers consistent.

sections.title: SMM-M03-L04: LinkedIn, X, Threads, Telegram and Indian platforms: choosing your mix
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Know what LinkedIn, X, Threads, Telegram and Indian regional apps are good for, choose one main and one support platform for your account and for a client, and set up a LinkedIn profile for your career. **Time:** about 2 hours 30 minutes (40 minutes study, 1 hour 50 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### The other platforms in one table (as of October 2026)

| Platform | What it's good for | Know this |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **LinkedIn** | Careers, B2B services, professional credibility | Your personal profile matters more than a company Page for freelancers. LinkedIn says Pages with complete information get 30% more weekly views and that weekly posting doubles engagement (its own figures). Creator mode was removed in 2024 and its tools opened to everyone. Document (PDF) posts work well for guides. |
| **X (Twitter)** | News, public conversation, journalists, tech | Its recommendation code is published on GitHub: about half of the "For You" feed comes from accounts you follow, the rest from others, ranked by a neural network. Rarely the first choice for local shops. |
| **Threads** | Text conversations linked to your Instagram account | Meta said it reached 500 million monthly users in June 2026, and that India was one of its most active countries in 2024. It has topic Communities. Easy to repurpose Instagram ideas into short text posts. |
| **Telegram** | Education, exam prep, updates and files | Channels can have unlimited subscribers and keep the full history for new subscribers; add a discussion group for comments. |
| **ShareChat and Moj** | Indian-language feeds and short video | Both support Malayalam among many Indian languages; worth testing for some audiences. |
| **Koo** | — | Shut down in July 2024. |
| **TikTok** | — | Blocked in India since June 2020, along with 58 other apps. |

### Choose your mix: go deep before wide

Every extra platform costs time every week. A beginner does better with **one main platform** (where you post your best work and try to grow), **one support platform** (where you repurpose, with little extra work) and **WhatsApp** for conversations. Add more only when you can keep up without dropping quality.

Score each candidate from 1 to 5:

- **Audience:** are your persona's people really there? (Use your research from SMM-M02-L02.)
- **Format fit:** does your content suit it (short video, photos, text, long video)?
- **Goal fit:** does it serve your objective (awareness, trust, leads, career)?
- **Effort:** can you post there every week without burning out? (5 = easy)
- **Your skill:** do you enjoy and do well in that format?

### Your career profile on LinkedIn

Whatever your main platform, set up LinkedIn for your career now; Module 12 builds it further.

- **Headline:** "Learning social media marketing | Helping local businesses in Kozhikode get more enquiries" (be honest that you are learning)
- **About:** three short paragraphs: what you're learning, what you've done so far (your page, your challenge), and what you want to do next
- **Featured:** link your practice page now; add case studies later

## Local example

Anu scored platforms for three different accounts:

| Account | Main | Support | Conversations | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| @kuttiady.diaries (her page) | Instagram Reels | YouTube Shorts | WhatsApp Channel | Local young audience on Reels; Shorts reuse the same videos |
| Kakkayam Hills Homestay | Instagram | YouTube long videos (room and trek tours) | WhatsApp Business for bookings | Travellers watch long tours before booking; Google reviews matter too |
| Fathima's PSC Sprint | YouTube | Telegram channel | WhatsApp Channel | Learners search YouTube; Telegram suits daily question files |

She also wrote her LinkedIn headline: "Learning social media marketing | Building a local page in Kuttiady | Open to helping small businesses in Kozhikode".

(Made-up example to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [LinkedIn: LinkedIn Pages best practices](https://business.linkedin.com/advertise/linkedin-pages/best-practices) | Read the best practices; note which figures are LinkedIn's own claims | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Social Media Today: LinkedIn removes Creator Mode (February 2024)](https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/linkedins-removing-its-creator-mode-option/706585/) | Read what changed when Creator mode was removed | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Meta: New Threads features at 500 million monthly users (June 2026)](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/06/meta-launching-new-features-500-million-monthly-threads-users/) | Read the Threads update: user numbers, Communities, live chats | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Telegram: Channels FAQ](https://telegram.org/faq_channels) | Read how Telegram channels and discussion groups work | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [ShareChat (Google Play)](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=in.mohalla.sharechat) | Check the languages listed | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [X: recommendation algorithm source code (GitHub)](https://github.com/twitter/the-algorithm) | Skim the first part of the README: how "For You" is built | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Business Today: Koo shuts down (July 2024)](https://businesstoday.in/technology/news/story/little-yellow-bird-says-final-goodbye-indias-twitter-rival-koo-shuts-down-435555-2024-07-03) | Read why Koo shut down | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [PIB: Government blocks 59 apps, including TikTok (June 2020)](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1635206&reg=48&lang=2) | Read the June 2020 order that blocked TikTok and other apps | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 40 minutes).
2. Fill in the platform matrix for your practice account and choose your main and support platforms.
3. Fill it in again for one real local business you might help later.
4. Set up or update your LinkedIn profile: photo, headline, About and a Featured link to your practice page.
5. If Threads suits you, make one short text post from an idea that did well on Instagram.

**Proof to record:** Your two platform matrices with decisions, and a screenshot of your LinkedIn headline and About section.

## Template: platform selection matrix

```
Score 1-5 (effort: 5 = easy)
Platform   | Audience | Format | Goal | Effort | Skill | Total
Instagram  |          |        |      |        |       |
YouTube    |          |        |      |        |       |
Facebook   |          |        |      |        |       |
WhatsApp   |          |        |      |        |       |
LinkedIn   |          |        |      |        |       |
Threads    |          |        |      |        |       |
Telegram   |          |        |      |        |       |
ShareChat  |          |        |      |        |       |

MAIN: ________  SUPPORT: ________
CONVERSATIONS: WhatsApp Business / Channel / DMs
Posts a week: main ___ support ___
Review this choice in week 21 (after Module 8).
```

## Template: LinkedIn headline and About formula

```
HEADLINE
[What you're learning or do] | [who you help] |
[proof or current project]

ABOUT (3 short paragraphs)
1. I'm learning social media marketing, focused on
   [niche or area].
2. So far I have [built @page / posted X times /
   run a 30-day challenge]. What I learned: ______
3. I'd like to help [kind of business] with
   [result]. Contact: ______
```

## Common mistakes

- **Starting on six platforms at once.** Quality drops everywhere. One main, one support, plus WhatsApp.
- **Planning around a blocked or closed app.** Check an app is available in India and still running before you plan.
- **Treating LinkedIn like Instagram.** LinkedIn rewards useful, professional posts and a complete profile.
- **Believing platform-published figures without saying so.** When you quote a platform's own numbers, say they are its claims.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. What is a sensible platform mix for a beginner?
    - A) Only X
    - B) One main, one support, plus WhatsApp for conversations
    - C) None until you have 1,000 followers
    - D) Every platform at once
2. What is true about Telegram channels?
    - A) They are banned in India
    - B) They show only the last post
    - C) They can have unlimited subscribers
    - D) They are limited to 256 members
3. Why shouldn't a Kerala business plan its marketing around TikTok?
    - A) It only works in Malayalam
    - B) It has been blocked in India since June 2020
    - C) It's too expensive
    - D) It has no videos
4. For a freelancer's career on LinkedIn, what matters most at first?
    - A) Thousands of connections
    - B) A paid subscription
    - C) A complete personal profile with an honest headline and Featured work
    - D) A company Page with no posts

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** LinkedIn, Threads, Telegram, X and Indian platform sources (about 40 minutes)
- **Action:** choose your platform mix with the matrix and set up your LinkedIn career profile. It is done when your proof is saved: your two platform matrices with decisions, and a screenshot of your LinkedIn headline and About section.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **B.** Going deep before wide protects quality and your time.
2. **C.** Telegram's FAQ says channels can have unlimited subscribers.
3. **B.** TikTok was among 59 apps blocked in June 2020.
4. **C.** Clients and employers look at your personal profile and proof.

sections.title: Module 4: Content creation
sections.summary: Make content people stop for: strong hooks, simple scripts, Malayalam and English that read well, and videos and designs made entirely on your phone.
sections.content:
## Overview

This is the craft module. In four weeks you'll write hooks and scripts, set language rules, learn to shoot with good light and sound using what you already have at home, edit on the phone with corrected captions and licensed sound, and design carousels, covers and thumbnails that are readable at phone size.

Every lesson ends with a real post. By week 11 you will have a phone content pack and a production kit of checklists and templates you'll use for the rest of the course.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Write hooks and short scripts using proven story structures
- Use Malayalam and English deliberately, with correct fonts and subtitles
- Shoot steady, well-lit vertical video with clean sound on an Android phone
- Edit on the phone with corrected captions, licensed sound and clean exports
- Design readable carousels, Reel covers and YouTube thumbnails within Canva's licence

## Time

About 17 hours 30 minutes in total: 15 hours of lessons and 2 hours 30 minutes for the module project. Part-time: weeks 8–11.

## Lessons

1. SMM-M04-L01: Hooks, scripts and storytelling (about 3 hours)
2. SMM-M04-L02: Malayalam and English content (about 1 hour 30 minutes)
3. SMM-M04-L03: Shooting on your phone: light, sound and framing (about 4 hours)
4. SMM-M04-L04: Editing on your phone (about 4 hours)
5. SMM-M04-L05: Design basics, carousels and thumbnails (about 2 hours 30 minutes)

## Module project: Your phone content pack

1. Make, entirely on your phone: 3 short videos (at least one talking to camera and one voiceover with B-roll), 2 carousels and 1 YouTube thumbnail.
2. Use the scripts, shooting, editing and design checklists for every piece, with consent notes where people appear.
3. Post them across weeks 10–12 and log each one.
4. Write a half-page production kit: your scripts template, shot list, editing steps and design template, in the order you actually use them.
5. Note your best and worst piece by 7-day views and say why you think each did as it did.

**Proof to record:** Links to the 3 videos and 2 carousels, the thumbnail image, your production kit and your best-and-worst notes.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3. If a row is a 1, redo that part first.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hooks | Starts with greetings or logos | Some hooks, inconsistent | Every piece hooks in the first second, visually and in text |
| Light and sound | Dark or noisy | Mostly clear | Clear light on faces and clean speech every time |
| Editing | Unedited clips | Trimmed but slow, or caption errors | Tight cuts, corrected captions, licensed sound, clean export |
| Design | Cluttered and hard to read | Readable but inconsistent | Readable at phone size, consistent template, within licence |
| Language | Random mixing, broken letters | Mostly consistent | Clear language rules, checked fonts, accurate subtitles |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, when PSC prep or work leaves little time:

- Write 5 hooks and 1 script; post one video.
- Do the light test only (skip the sound test) and shoot one Reel.
- Edit one video with corrected captions.
- Make one carousel from a template.

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, read the front, say the answer, then check. Repeat the ones you missed the next day.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| Three layers of a hook? | Visual, on-screen text and the first spoken sentence. |
| What must every hook do? | Tell the truth, and be delivered by the video. |
| Best free light for faces? | A window in front or to the side of the person. |
| What matters more for talking videos: picture or sound? | Sound. |
| Which free editor exports with no watermark and is made by Instagram? | Edits. |
| YouTube Create needs at least how much RAM? | 4 GB (Android 8.0 or later). |
| Where should you get music for posts? | The platform's own library or the YouTube Audio Library, never downloaded film songs. |
| What does Canva's free licence forbid for logos? | Using free library media as part of a logo, trademark or business name. |
| Three Malayalam fonts that render well? | Manjari, Chilanka, Noto Sans Malayalam. |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Buying gear before learning light and sound.** A window and a quiet room beat an expensive camera.
- **Perfectionism.** Post the good-enough version; you learn more from ten posts than from one perfect one.
- **Skipping consent because "it's just a small page".** Every person and shop deserves to be asked, and clients will expect it.
