sections.title: Module 6: Content systems
sections.summary: Build the system that lets you post consistently for months: a calendar, batching, repurposing, scheduling and templates. Then prove it with a 30-day content challenge.
sections.content:
## Overview

Good marketers aren't more inspired than others; they have systems. In week 14 you plan your month around Kerala's seasons, batch a week of content in one session, and turn single ideas into several posts. In week 15 you schedule with free official tools and build a template library.

The 30-day challenge starts in week 14 and runs until week 18, alongside Module 7. It is the heart of the course's first half: every day you post, measure and learn.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Plan a month of content around themes, pillars and series
- Batch a week of posts in one session and keep a buffer
- Repurpose one idea into several platform-ready posts
- Schedule posts with Meta Business Suite, YouTube Studio and LinkedIn
- Complete 30 days of daily posting with full measurement

## Time

About 18 hours in total: 17 hours of lessons and 1 hour for the module project. Part-time: weeks 14–18, with the module project due in week 15.

## Lessons

1. SMM-M06-L01: Content calendars and batching (about 2 hours)
2. SMM-M06-L02: Repurpose one idea across platforms (about 1 hour 30 minutes)
3. SMM-M06-L03: Scheduling tools and templates (about 1 hour 30 minutes)
4. SMM-M06-L04: The 30-day content challenge (about 12 hours)

## Module project: Your content system, version 1

1. Show your system working by the end of week 15: the 30-day Calendar tab with statuses, a "repurpose" column filled in, and at least 7 posts scheduled or posted from batches.
2. Write your batching routine (days, times, tasks) as you actually do it.
3. Organise your template library in 06 Systems with a short index.
4. Keep 3–5 buffer posts ready.
5. Write one paragraph: what in this system saves you the most time, and what still takes too long.

**Proof to record:** Screenshots of your Calendar tab and 06 Systems folder, your batching routine and your one-paragraph review.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3. If a row is a 1, redo that part first.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Calendar | No plan | A plan for a week | A month of themes and a 30-day calendar with statuses |
| Batching | One post at a time | Sometimes batched | Two regular batch sessions a week and a buffer of 3–5 posts |
| Repurposing | One platform only | Copies across platforms | Adapted versions from original files, planned in the calendar |
| Scheduling and templates | Posting live, from scratch | Some templates | Official scheduling plus a template library in use |
| 30-day challenge | Under 15 days | 15–29 days or weak logging | 30 days, all logged, 4 reviews, 3 experiments |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, when PSC prep or work leaves little time:

- Plan only the first two weeks of the challenge in detail.
- One batch session a week instead of two.
- Repurpose one post into one other format.
- If 30 days is impossible right now, do 30 posts in 45 days, keeping all the logging and reviews.

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, read the front, say the answer, then check. Repeat the ones you missed the next day.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| Three levels of a content calendar? | Month (themes), week (pillars and series), day (the exact post). |
| The six statuses of a post? | Idea, scripted, shot, edited, scheduled, posted. |
| How big should your buffer be? | Three to five finished, evergreen posts. |
| Why upload original files when cross-posting? | Watermarked reposts get less reach. |
| Free tool to schedule Facebook and Instagram posts? | Meta Business Suite. |
| Where do you find your best posting time? | Your own Insights and Analytics, plus a two-time-slot test. |
| The 30-day challenge's experiment rule? | One change a week, so you know what made the difference. |
| Missed a challenge day: what do you do? | Post the next day and carry on. |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **A system on paper only.** If you don't use it in week 15, simplify it until you do.
- **Treating the challenge as a race for followers.** It's a learning sprint. The data is the prize.
- **Forgetting Module 7 during the challenge.** Use each growth lesson as that week's experiment.

tasks.detail: **Proof to record:** Screenshots of your Calendar tab and 06 Systems folder, your batching routine and your one-paragraph review.

sections.title: SMM-M06-L01: Content calendars and batching
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Plan a month of content around Kerala's seasons and your pillars, run it through a simple status workflow, and make a week of posts in one batch session. **Time:** about 2 hours (25 minutes study, 1 hour 35 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Why a calendar beats inspiration

Posting "when inspired" leads to three posts in one day and nothing for two weeks. A calendar turns your strategy into a schedule you can keep, shows gaps before they happen, and lets you prepare for busy weeks such as exams and festivals.

Plan at three levels:

| Level | What you decide | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Month** | Themes: festivals, seasons, local events, launches | Last Sunday of the previous month |
| **Week** | Which pillar and series goes on which day | Saturday batch session |
| **Day** | The exact post, hook, caption and CTA | In the batch session, or the night before |

### A Kerala content year (check the dates every year)

- **Festivals:** Vishu (April), Onam (August or September), Eid and Ramadan (dates move each year), Christmas, Deepavali, local temple, church and mosque festivals
- **Seasons:** summer heat (March–May), monsoon (June–September), wedding seasons
- **Calendar moments:** school reopening (June), exam results, Gulf holiday travel, new academic year, salary days
- **Local:** your panchayat's events, sports, markets, new shop openings

Festival posts work when they are relevant to the business and to people's lives (an "Onam sadya pre-order" for a caterer), not a generic greeting card from every page.

### A simple status workflow

Every row in your Calendar tab moves through: **idea → scripted → shot → edited → scheduled → posted**. At a glance you can see what's ready and what's stuck. If Wednesday's post is still "idea" on Tuesday night, swap in a ready post from your buffer.

### Batching

Making one post at a time means changing tasks constantly. **Batching** groups similar work:

1. **Plan and script** all of the week's posts in one sitting (30–45 minutes).
2. **Shoot** everything at one location in one trip (45–60 minutes): one shop visit can give you a Reel, a carousel, Stories and a "shop story".
3. **Edit** all the videos in one sitting (45–60 minutes).
4. **Write and schedule** captions (20–30 minutes).

YouTube's own well-being tips for creators suggest batching similar tasks, such as replying to comments, making thumbnails or filming, on the same day.

### Keep a buffer

Always keep **three to five finished posts** ready for weeks when you're ill, travelling or close to an exam. Evergreen posts (tips, "then and now", FAQs) make the best buffer because they don't go out of date.

## Local example

Anu planned her November with three themes: "Monsoon is over: outdoor spots", "Wedding season food", and her series "₹100 Friday" and "Shop story".

Her Saturday batch, about 3 hours:

| Time | Task | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 9:00–9:40 | Script the week from the caption bank | 7 scripts |
| 9:45–11:00 | One trip to Kuttiady town: a bakery, a tailor, a juice shop (all with permission) | Clips for 4 Reels, 1 carousel, Stories |
| 2:00–3:00 | Edit 4 Reels in Edits | 4 videos exported |
| 3:00–3:30 | Captions and scheduling | 5 posts scheduled, 2 in the buffer |

During the week she spent only about 15 minutes a day: replying to comments and posting one Story.

(Made-up example to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [YouTube Help: Well-being tips for creators](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/12930055) | Read the parts on routines and batching similar tasks | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Canva Design School: Marketing with Canva](https://www.canva.com/en/design-school/courses/marketing-with-canva) | Watch "Organizing and sharing content" | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 20 minutes).
2. Write next month's themes: festivals, seasons and local events, with dates you have checked.
3. Fill the Calendar tab for the 30 days of your challenge (it starts this week): date, platform, format, pillar, topic, hook and CTA, using your caption bank from Module 5.
4. Put two batch sessions a week in your Google Calendar for the next five weeks.
5. Run your first batch session and get the first 7 days to "edited" or "scheduled". Make 2 extra posts for your buffer.

**Proof to record:** Your monthly themes, the 30-day Calendar tab and screenshots showing at least 7 posts at "edited" or "scheduled" plus 2 buffer posts.

## Template: monthly theme planner

```
MONTH: ________
Festivals and dates (checked): __________________
Season or weather: ______________________________
Local events: ___________________________________
Business moments (launch, offer, new stock): ____
THEMES (2-3): 1. ________ 2. ________ 3. ________
SERIES this month: "________" every ________
Buffer posts ready: ___ (target 3-5)
```

## Template: weekly batch routine

```
SATURDAY (about 3 hours)
[ ] 30-45 min  plan and script the week
[ ] 45-60 min  shoot at one location (consent!)
[ ] 45-60 min  edit all videos
[ ] 20-30 min  write captions, schedule, update Calendar
WEDNESDAY (about 45 minutes)
[ ] edit or design anything left; top up the buffer
DAILY (10-15 minutes)
[ ] reply to comments and messages
[ ] one Story or Status
[ ] log yesterday's post in the Posting Log
```

## Common mistakes

- **Planning more than you can make.** A calendar you can't keep is worse than none. Plan for your real hours.
- **No buffer.** One bad week breaks the habit. Keep three to five posts ready.
- **Generic festival greetings.** Make festival posts useful and relevant to the business, or skip them.
- **Shooting one post per trip.** One location visit can give you a week of content.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. What is batching?
    - A) Deleting old posts
    - B) Posting everything on one day
    - C) Buying followers in batches
    - D) Grouping similar tasks, such as all scripting, then all shooting, then all editing
2. Why keep a buffer of finished posts?
    - A) Platforms require it
    - B) So you can keep posting in weeks when you're ill, travelling or near an exam
    - C) To post ten at once
    - D) To avoid writing captions
3. What should you do before planning festival posts?
    - A) Post the same greeting as everyone
    - B) Copy last year's dates
    - C) Skip all festivals
    - D) Check this year's dates and make the post relevant to the business

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** YouTube's routine and batching tips and Canva's content organising lesson (about 20 minutes)
- **Action:** plan your 30-day challenge calendar and batch the first week plus 2 buffer posts. It is done when your proof is saved: your monthly themes, the 30-day Calendar tab and screenshots showing at least 7 posts at "edited" or "scheduled" plus 2 buffer posts.
- **Quiz:** at least 2 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **D.** It saves time and makes posting consistent.
2. **B.** Evergreen buffer posts protect your rhythm.
3. **D.** Festival dates move, and relevance beats generic greetings.

sections.title: SMM-M06-L02: Repurpose one idea across platforms
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Turn one strong idea or video into several posts for different platforms without copying, watermarks or broken rules, and keep a repurposing map so it becomes a habit. **Time:** about 1 hour 30 minutes (20 minutes study, 1 hour 10 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Create once, publish many

Making a good piece of content takes most of the effort: the idea, the visit, the filming. Publishing it in several shapes takes little extra time and reaches people where they are. This is **repurposing**: one idea, adapted for each platform.

### A content tree

| Start with | Turn it into |
| --- | --- |
| **One long YouTube video** (10 minutes) | 3–5 Shorts or Reels of the best moments; a carousel of the key points; a Threads or LinkedIn post with the main lesson; a WhatsApp Channel update linking to the video |
| **One Reel** | A YouTube Short (from the original file); a Story with a poll about it; a Facebook Reel or Page post; a WhatsApp Status |
| **One carousel** | A LinkedIn document post (export the slides as a PDF); a Story sequence; a Google Business Profile update for a business |
| **One shop visit** | A Reel, a carousel of prices, a "shop story" interview, Stories, a Google review photo for the owner (with permission) |

### Adapt, don't copy

- **Shape:** 9:16 for Reels, Shorts and Stories; 16:9 for long YouTube videos; 4:5 or square for carousels and feed photos.
- **Length:** cut a longer video into short moments; don't stretch a Short.
- **Words:** rewrite the caption for each platform's mood (SMM-M05-L03).
- **Music:** add it inside each app, or use YouTube's libraries. For YouTube Shorts longer than a minute, a copyright claim blocks the Short worldwide (as of October 2026).
- **Files:** always upload your original export. Never download your own post from one app (with its watermark) and upload it to another.

### Repurposing your own work is welcome; reposting others' isn't

Platforms reward originality. Instagram recommends originals over near-identical copies and Facebook announced reduced reach in July 2025 for accounts that repeatedly repost other people's content. Turning **your own** video into a Short, a carousel and a Story is exactly what they expect creators to do.

### Make it a habit

Add a "repurpose" column to your Calendar: for every main post, note the two or three other places it will go. Do the repurposing in your batch session, not as an afterthought.

## Local example

Fathima filmed one 12-minute YouTube video, "20 Kerala geography questions for PSC (Malayalam)". From it, in about 50 extra minutes, she made:

- 4 Shorts, each one tricky question with the answer
- a 7-slide carousel, "5 rivers questions that keep coming back", for Instagram
- a Telegram channel post with the questions as a quiz and the video link
- a WhatsApp Channel update: "New: 20 geography questions explained. Video: [link]"
- a LinkedIn post (on her personal profile) about what she learned making PSC content in Malayalam

The long video got most of its first views from the Shorts and the Telegram post. One idea filled her week.

(Made-up example to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [YouTube Help: Understand three-minute YouTube Shorts](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/15424877) | Re-read the music rule for Shorts over 1 minute | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [TechCrunch: Meta cracks down on unoriginal Facebook content (July 2025)](https://techcrunch.com/2025/07/14/following-youtube-meta-announces-crackdown-on-unoriginal-facebook-content) | Re-read what counts as unoriginal content | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [LinkedIn: LinkedIn Pages best practices](https://business.linkedin.com/advertise/linkedin-pages/best-practices) | Re-read the tip on document (PDF) posts | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 15 minutes).
2. Pick your best post so far (highest 7-day views or shares).
3. Draw its content tree: list at least 4 other formats or platforms it can become.
4. Make and publish at least 2 of them this week, each adapted (shape, length, words, music) and uploaded from your original files.
5. Add a "repurpose" column to your Calendar tab and fill it for the rest of the challenge.

**Proof to record:** Your content tree, links to the 2 repurposed posts with their Posting Log rows, and a screenshot of the new Calendar column.

## Template: repurposing map

```
MAIN PIECE: _______________ (platform, link)
1. Short/Reel moments: ____ ____ ____
2. Carousel: title ____________ slides ___
3. Story: poll or question ____________
4. Text post (Threads/LinkedIn/Facebook): ____
5. WhatsApp: Status ____ / Channel ____
6. For a business: Google Business Profile post ____
CHECK EACH ONE:
[ ] right shape  [ ] right length  [ ] rewritten words
[ ] music added in-app or from YouTube's libraries
[ ] uploaded from the original file, no watermark
```

## Common mistakes

- **Identical copies everywhere.** Adapt shape, length and words for each platform.
- **Watermarked cross-posting.** Upload your original export to each app.
- **Repurposing weak content.** Repurpose your winners; let the weak posts go.
- **Repurposing other people's videos.** That is reposting, and platforms push it down. Only repurpose your own work.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Which is good repurposing?
    - A) Cutting your own long video into Shorts and a carousel
    - B) Downloading a viral Reel from another page and posting it
    - C) Re-uploading an Instagram download to YouTube
    - D) Posting the same caption on every app
2. Before cross-posting a video, you should:
    - A) Download it from Instagram
    - B) Upload the original export to each platform
    - C) Make it horizontal for Reels
    - D) Add another app's watermark
3. A carousel can become which LinkedIn format?
    - A) A document (PDF) post
    - B) A voice note
    - C) A Short
    - D) A Story

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** YouTube's Shorts music rule, Facebook's originality crackdown and LinkedIn's document tip (about 15 minutes)
- **Action:** turn your best post into at least 2 adapted posts and add a repurpose column to your calendar. It is done when your proof is saved: your content tree, links to the 2 repurposed posts with their Posting Log rows, and a screenshot of the new Calendar column.
- **Quiz:** at least 2 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **A.** It adapts your own original work for other formats.
2. **B.** Watermarked reposts get less reach.
3. **A.** Export the slides as a PDF and post them as a document.

sections.title: SMM-M06-L03: Scheduling tools and templates
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Schedule posts with free official tools, choose posting times from your own data, and build a template library that halves the time each post takes. **Time:** about 1 hour 30 minutes (20 minutes study, 1 hour 10 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Schedule with the official tools first (as of October 2026)

| Tool | What you can schedule |
| --- | --- |
| **Meta Business Suite** (app or computer) | Posts and Stories for a Facebook Page and its connected Instagram account, plus one inbox for messages and comments |
| **YouTube Studio** | Uploads set to publish at a chosen date and time (choose "Schedule" when you upload) |
| **LinkedIn** | Posts on your profile or Page at a chosen date and time |
| **WhatsApp Business broadcasts** | Messages to the customers you choose, sent now or later |

Official tools are free, don't need your password shared with another company, and support the formats properly. Third-party schedulers can be useful for agencies later; check their free plans and permissions carefully before connecting a client's account.

### Scheduled isn't the same as forgotten

Be around for the first hour after a scheduled post goes live, to reply to early comments. Stories and Status updates usually work better posted live, because they react to the day.

### Posting times: use your own data

There is no universal "best time". Once your account has enough followers, Instagram Insights shows when your followers are most active; YouTube Analytics shows when your viewers are on YouTube. Until then, pick a time when your persona is free (evenings for many, lunch break for workers) and test two time slots for two weeks each.

### A template library saves hours

Build once, reuse forever. Keep these in Drive folder **06 Systems**:

- **Canva templates:** Reel cover, carousel (cover, content, summary, CTA), Story frame, YouTube thumbnail, price list
- **Text templates:** caption formulas, CTA bank, reply templates, hashtag sets for each pillar (max 5 each)
- **Checklists:** shooting, editing, design, caption check, honest persuasion check
- **File naming:** date_series_topic_version (2026-11-07_shopstory_tailor_v1.mp4)

A good library makes a routine post take 30–40 minutes instead of two hours.

## Local example

Anu's scheduling set-up for the challenge:

- Instagram and her new Facebook Page: scheduled in Meta Business Suite every Saturday after her batch session.
- YouTube Shorts: uploaded on Saturday and scheduled for 7:30 pm on the same days as the Reels.
- WhatsApp Channel: posted live, because it reacts to the day.

She tested two times for her Reels: 1 pm for the first two weeks, 7:30 pm for the next two. Average views were similar, but replies came faster at 7:30 pm when she was free to answer, so she kept the evening slot. Her template library cut her editing and design time roughly in half by week 3.

(Made-up example to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Meta Business Suite app (Google Play)](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.facebook.pages.app) | Read what you can schedule and manage; install it if you use a Facebook Page | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [WhatsApp Business: business broadcasts](https://whatsappbusiness.com/resources/resource-library/business-broadcasts-whatsapp/) | Re-read the scheduling part | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |
| [LinkedIn: LinkedIn Pages best practices](https://business.linkedin.com/advertise/linkedin-pages/best-practices) | Re-read the scheduling tip | 2 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Canva Design School: Marketing with Canva](https://www.canva.com/en/design-school/courses/marketing-with-canva) | Re-watch "Organizing and sharing content" if you skipped it | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 15 minutes).
2. Schedule at least 3 challenge posts in advance with official tools (Meta Business Suite, YouTube Studio, or LinkedIn).
3. Build your template library in Drive 06 Systems: at least 4 Canva templates, your text templates and your checklists.
4. Choose two posting times to test, and write the test in the Experiments tab.

**Proof to record:** Screenshots of 3 scheduled posts, a screenshot of your 06 Systems folder, and the posting-time test in the Experiments tab.

## Template: template library contents

```
06 Systems/
  Canva: reel-cover, carousel (4 slides), story-frame,
         yt-thumbnail, price-list
  Text:  caption-formulas, cta-bank, replies,
         hashtag-sets (pillar: 5 tags each)
  Checklists: shooting, editing, design, caption,
         honest-persuasion
  Naming: YYYY-MM-DD_series_topic_v1
```

## Template: posting-time test (Experiments tab row)

```csv
Start date,Hypothesis,Change tested,Metric,Before,After,Result,Decision
____,Evening posts get faster replies,1 pm vs 7:30 pm (2 weeks each),Average 24 h views and replies in first hour,,,,
```

## Common mistakes

- **Giving your password to an unknown scheduling app.** Use official tools first; connect third-party tools only through official log-in screens.
- **Scheduling and disappearing.** Reply to comments in the first hour.
- **Copying someone's "best time to post".** Test times with your own audience.
- **Templates that make every post look identical.** Keep the layout, change the photo, colour accent or headline.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Which free tool schedules posts and Stories for a Facebook Page and its Instagram account?
    - A) Snapseed
    - B) Meta Business Suite
    - C) Google Trends
    - D) Telegram
2. What is the best way to choose posting times?
    - A) Post at random
    - B) Copy a viral post's time
    - C) Always post at midnight
    - D) Use your own Insights and test two time slots
3. Why be online for the first hour after a scheduled post?
    - A) To delete it if views are low
    - B) Platforms require it
    - C) To reply to early comments and start conversations
    - D) To repost it

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** Meta Business Suite, WhatsApp broadcast scheduling, LinkedIn scheduling and Canva's organising lesson (about 15 minutes)
- **Action:** schedule 3 posts with official tools, build your template library and set up a posting-time test. It is done when your proof is saved: screenshots of 3 scheduled posts, a screenshot of your 06 Systems folder, and the posting-time test in the Experiments tab.
- **Quiz:** at least 2 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **B.** Its listing says it creates, schedules and manages posts and Stories for both.
2. **D.** Your own audience's habits are what matter.
3. **C.** Quick replies build community and keep conversations going.

sections.title: SMM-M06-L04: The 30-day content challenge
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Post every day for 30 days, log every post's numbers, review each week and run one small experiment a week, so that you finish with real data about what works for your audience. **Time:** about 12 hours (30 minutes study, about 11 hours 30 minutes of posting and reviews over 30 days).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Why 30 days in a row

Posting every day for a month does three things that three posts a week can't. You learn faster, because you get ten times more data. You get faster at making content, because you repeat the whole process daily. And you find out which formats and topics your audience actually wants, instead of guessing.

### The rules

1. **Post once a day for 30 days** on your main platform: a Reel or Short, a carousel or a photo post. Stories and Status updates don't count (do them too).
2. **At least 12 of the 30 are short videos.**
3. **Quality floor:** every post has a hook, corrected captions, licensed sound and consent from anyone in it. Don't drop your standards to hit the count.
4. **Log everything:** a Posting Log row the day you post, views after 24 hours, views and other numbers after 7 days.
5. **Sunday review:** a Weekly Stats row and one decision for the next week.
6. **One experiment a week:** change one thing (hook type, length, format, language, posting time) and compare.
7. **Missed a day?** Post the next day and carry on. Don't post three times to "catch up".

Batch twice a week (SMM-M06-L01) and keep your buffer full, so the challenge takes about 20–30 minutes a day, not two hours.

### A four-week shape

| Week | Days | Focus | Experiment idea |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 1–7 | Your usual formats, all pillars; find your baseline | None: just measure |
| 2 | 8–14 | Hooks | Question hooks vs result-first hooks |
| 3 | 15–21 | Formats and length | 15-second vs 45-second videos; carousel vs Reel on the same topic |
| 4 | 22–30 | Double down on what worked | Repeat your top 3 topics in new versions |

### Honest expectations

Some days a post will get almost no views. One or two posts may do far better than the rest. Most accounts don't "blow up" in 30 days, and that's fine: the goal is learning and a habit, and the numbers you collect become your first case study in Module 8. Judge the challenge by your averages week to week, not by one post.

### Look after yourself

Daily posting can be tiring. Sleep, PSC study and family come first. Batch so that most days are light, take screen breaks, and if a PSC exam falls inside the 30 days, move the challenge rather than squeezing it in. Module 16 covers creator burnout properly.

## Local example

Anu's challenge (days 1–30, made-up numbers to show the method):

| Week | Posts | Average views after 7 days | Shares per 1,000 views | Followers gained | Experiment and result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 7 | 640 | 8 | 41 | Baseline |
| 2 | 7 | 910 | 11 | 66 | Question hooks beat result-first hooks for food posts |
| 3 | 7 | 820 | 14 | 58 | 15-second videos got more views; carousels got more saves |
| 4 | 9 | 1,450 | 17 | 132 | Repeated top topics: "₹100 Friday" and "shop stories" |

Her best post (day 23, a 40-second story of a 31-year-old tailoring shop) reached 9,800 accounts, mostly local, and 160 people shared it. Her worst (day 5, a long text post about bus timings) got 90 views. Her decision: shop stories and food under ₹100 become her two main series; text-heavy posts move to WhatsApp Channel.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Instagram for Creators: Helping creators of all sizes break through](https://creators.instagram.com/blog/helping-creators-of-all-sizes-break-through) | Re-read why posting regularly helps each reel reach new viewers | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Help: Well-being tips for creators](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/12930055) | Read the tips on routines and taking breaks | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Help: Tips for dealing with creator burnout](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13616108) | Read the tips on avoiding burnout before you start | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 25 minutes) and set your start date, at least two weeks away from any PSC exam.
2. Days 1–30: post every day following the rules, from your Calendar and buffer. Log each post the same day, and add the 24-hour and 7-day numbers.
3. Every Sunday: fill in Weekly Stats, write what worked and what didn't, and choose next week's one experiment (log it in Experiments).
4. Day 30: screenshot your Insights overview for the 30 days and fill in the day-30 summary.

**Proof to record:** Your Posting Log with 30 daily posts (24-hour and 7-day numbers), 4 Weekly Stats rows, 3 experiments, an Insights screenshot and your day-30 summary.

**Full-time track:** The challenge runs for 30 real days, so on the full-time pace it continues while you study Modules 7 to 10. The app will show this task as overdue for a few weeks; tick it when day 30 is done.

## Template: challenge tracker (one row a day)

```csv
Day,Date,Platform,Format,Pillar,Hook type,Length (s),Language,Views 24 h,Views 7 days,Reach,Shares,Saves,Follows,Experiment?,Note
```

## Template: Sunday review

```
WEEK __ (days __-__)
Posts: ___/7   Average 7-day views: ___
Best post: ________ (why?) ______________
Worst post: _______ (why?) ______________
Experiment this week: __________________
  Result: ___________  Decision: _________
Energy check (1-5): ___  What will make next week easier?
_________________________________________
```

## Template: day-30 summary

```
30-DAY CHALLENGE SUMMARY (dates ____ to ____)
Posts: ___/30 (short videos: ___)
Followers: start ___ end ___ (+___)
Average 7-day views: week 1 ___ week 4 ___
Shares per 1,000 views: week 1 ___ week 4 ___
Top 3 posts and why they worked:
  1. ____ 2. ____ 3. ____
3 things I'll keep doing: ____ ____ ____
3 things I'll stop doing: ____ ____ ____
What surprised me: ______________________
```

## Common mistakes

- **Dropping quality to keep the streak.** A rushed post with no hook teaches you nothing. Use your buffer instead.
- **Changing five things at once.** One experiment a week, so you know what made the difference.
- **Judging by the best or worst single post.** Compare weekly averages.
- **Burning out in week 2.** Batch, keep a buffer and protect your sleep and study time.
- **Not logging.** Without the numbers, the challenge is just tiring. Log every day.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. During the challenge, you miss day 12. What should you do?
    - A) Restart from day 1
    - B) Post on day 13 and carry on; don't post three times to catch up
    - C) Give up
    - D) Buy views
2. Why run only one experiment a week?
    - A) Experiments are banned
    - B) Platforms allow one change a week
    - C) So you know which change caused the difference
    - D) It doesn't matter
3. How should you judge whether the challenge worked?
    - A) By weekly averages and what you learned
    - B) By your single best post
    - C) By likes only
    - D) By follower count on day 1
4. A PSC exam falls on day 18 of your planned challenge. What's the sensible plan?
    - A) Stop studying
    - B) Move the challenge so it doesn't overlap the exam weeks
    - C) Skip sleep to keep posting
    - D) Post low-quality filler

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** Instagram's advice on regular posting and YouTube's well-being and burnout tips (about 25 minutes)
- **Action:** complete the 30-day content challenge with every post logged, weekly reviews and a day-30 summary. It is done when your proof is saved: your Posting Log with 30 daily posts (24-hour and 7-day numbers), 4 Weekly Stats rows, 3 experiments, an Insights screenshot and your day-30 summary.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **B.** Consistency matters more than a perfect streak.
2. **C.** Changing many things at once makes results impossible to read.
3. **A.** Averages and lessons show real progress.
4. **B.** Your exam and wellbeing come first; the challenge can move.

sections.title: Module 7: Growth
sections.summary: Grow with methods that last: social search, smart use of trends, collaborations and a real community, while the 30-day challenge gives you daily posts to test them on.
sections.content:
## Overview

Growth isn't a trick; it's being findable, timely and worth talking to. In weeks 16–18 you'll research keywords and hashtags and optimise posts for Instagram and YouTube search, use trends with a local twist, collaborate with complementary accounts, and build a daily engagement routine with moderation in place.

Each lesson gives you that week's challenge experiment, so by the end you'll know which growth methods work for your audience.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Research keywords and optimise posts for Instagram and YouTube search
- Use at most five specific hashtags on Instagram and follow YouTube's hashtag rules
- Use trends that fit, with licensed audio and a local twist
- Plan and disclose collaborations correctly
- Run a daily engagement routine, moderate comments and start a community space

## Time

About 8 hours 30 minutes in total: 7 hours 30 minutes of lessons and 1 hour for the module project. Part-time: weeks 16–18.

## Lessons

1. SMM-M07-L01: Social SEO: keywords, hashtags and YouTube search (about 2 hours 30 minutes)
2. SMM-M07-L02: Trends and collaborations (about 2 hours 30 minutes)
3. SMM-M07-L03: Community, DMs and engagement (about 2 hours 30 minutes)

## Module project: Two growth experiments

1. Choose two experiments from this module, for example keyword captions versus plain captions, or a Collab Reel versus a solo Reel on the same kind of topic.
2. Write each as a hypothesis in the Experiments tab before you start.
3. Run each for at least 4 posts per version during the challenge.
4. Compare the right metric for each (search views, follows, shares, replies) and write a decision.

**Proof to record:** Two completed rows in the Experiments tab, with the post links and the decision for each.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3. If a row is a 1, redo that part first.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Social SEO | No keywords | Some keywords, guessed | Researched keywords used naturally in profiles, captions and YouTube metadata |
| Hashtags | Many generic tags | Fewer but generic | At most five specific tags from saved sets; YouTube rules followed |
| Trends | Copies trends blindly or never uses them | Some fitting trends | Fitting trends with a twist, in-app audio, checked facts |
| Collaborations | None | Pitched, not done | At least one collaboration published with correct disclosure |
| Community | Ignores comments | Replies sometimes | Daily routine, moderation set, a community space running |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, when PSC prep or work leaves little time:

- Find 10 keywords and make one hashtag set.
- Use one trend with a twist.
- Pitch one collaboration partner.
- Reply to every comment for 7 days; turn on Hidden Words.

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, read the front, say the answer, then check. Repeat the ones you missed the next day.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| What is social SEO? | Making posts easy to find in a platform's search with the words people really use. |
| Four sources of keywords? | Audience comments and DMs, search suggestions, Google Trends, spelling variants. |
| Instagram hashtag limit and style? | At most five, specific and relevant, in the caption. |
| YouTube hashtag limit? | More than 60 and YouTube ignores all of them; up to three show above the title. |
| Three questions before using a trend? | Does it fit? Can I add a twist? Is it respectful? |
| What counts as a material connection? | Money, free products, discounts, gifts, trips, or family and work ties with the brand. |
| What does Limits on Instagram do? | Temporarily hides comments and DM requests from non-followers and recent followers. |
| Is sub4sub allowed on YouTube? | No: it is fake engagement. |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Chasing virality instead of the right audience.** A thousand local viewers can be worth more than a million random ones.
- **Growth without measurement.** Log which method you used on which post, or you'll never know what worked.
- **Fake growth to "look bigger" for clients.** Clients check, and fake numbers make your case studies worthless.

sections.title: SMM-M07-L01: Social SEO: keywords, hashtags and YouTube search
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Find the words your audience types into search, and put them where Instagram, YouTube and Google look: handles, names, bios, captions, titles, descriptions, chapters, alt text and a few specific hashtags. **Time:** about 2 hours 30 minutes (40 minutes study, 1 hour 50 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### People search social apps too

Recommendations bring people who weren't looking for you. **Search** brings people who are: "biryani near Kuttiady", "phone screen guard price", "PSC Kerala history questions Malayalam". These viewers already want what you offer, and search keeps sending them to good posts for months. **Social SEO** (search engine optimisation) means making your posts easy to find in that search.

### Find the words people really use

1. **Your audience's own words:** the questions in your comment mining sheet (SMM-M02-L02) and in DMs.
2. **Search suggestions:** start typing your topic in YouTube, Instagram and Google search and note the suggestions that appear.
3. **Google Trends:** compare candidate terms for Kerala, and switch to **YouTube Search** to see video interest. Remember the numbers are relative interest, not counts.
4. **Spelling and language variants:** people search "kuttiady", "kuttiadi", "കുറ്റ്യാടി"; "biriyani" and "biryani". Note which ones appear in suggestions.

Choose one **main keyword** per post (what it's mostly about) and one or two related ones.

### Where Instagram looks (as of October 2026)

Instagram's tips for creators say to put keywords in your **handle, profile name, bio and captions**, and to put keywords and hashtags in the caption rather than in the comments. Its search matches usernames, bios, captions, hashtags and places. So:

- **Name field and bio:** your niche and place ("Kuttiady | Food, shops, local news").
- **Caption:** the main keyword in the first line, written naturally ("New juice shop near Kuttiady bus stand").
- **Location tag:** tag the real place on posts about places.
- **Alt text:** for photos, write a short description in the post's accessibility settings; it helps people who use screen readers and describes the image in words.
- **Hashtags:** at most five, specific and relevant: place (#kuttiady #kozhikode), niche (#kozhikodefood) and community (#kudumbashree). Instagram says fewer, targeted hashtags work better than generic ones such as #reels.

### Where YouTube looks

YouTube's search ranks by **relevance** (how well the title, description, tags and the video's content match the search), **engagement** (for example, watch time for that search) and **quality** (signs of expertise, authority and trust). Practical steps:

- **Title:** the search phrase near the start, in the language people search, then a reason to click.
- **Description:** first two lines say what viewers get, using the keyword naturally; then details, links and chapters.
- **Chapters** for long videos (timestamps from 00:00, at least three, each at least 10 seconds).
- **Captions and subtitles:** correct ones make your video understandable to more people (SMM-M04-L02).
- **Hashtags:** in the title or description; up to three appear above the title. YouTube ignores all hashtags on a video with more than 60, and unrelated hashtags can get a video removed from search.
- **Playlists** that group videos on one topic help viewers keep watching.

YouTube says it doesn't accept payment for better placement in organic search. The only route is relevance, engagement and quality.

### Don't stuff

Repeating a keyword ten times, or adding unrelated popular hashtags, makes posts harder to read and can break platform rules. Write for people first; keywords should appear where a human would naturally use them.

## Local example

Riyas at **Malabar Mobiles** wanted more repair customers. Anu listened to his customers and checked search suggestions: people typed "screen guard price", "mobile display change Kuttiady" and "phone battery replacement near me". In Google Trends for Kerala, "mobile display" had more interest than "phone screen".

They changed:

- Name field: "Malabar Mobiles | Phone repair Kuttiady"
- First caption lines: "Mobile display change in Kuttiady: ₹ price for common models 👇"
- Hashtags (five): #kuttiady #kuttiadymobiles #mobilerepair #kozhikode #screenguard
- A YouTube video "Mobile display change price in Kuttiady (Malayalam)" with chapters for three common models.

Within two months, their video was getting views from YouTube search every day, and the shop asked every repair customer how they found them: "YouTube search" came up about once a week.

(Made-up example to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Instagram for Creators: What creators need to know about recommendations](https://creators.instagram.com/blog/instagram-recommendations-eligibility-tips-creators) | Re-read "Optimize for Search": keywords in handle, name, bio and captions | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Search Engine Land: How Instagram ranks content (2023)](https://searchengineland.com/how-instagram-ranks-content-feed-stories-explore-reels-search-427774) | Re-read how Instagram search matches queries | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Help: How YouTube search works](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/16090438) | Re-read relevance, engagement and quality | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Help: Find playlists and videos using hashtags (hashtag rules)](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/6390658) | Read the hashtag rules, including the 60-hashtag limit | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Social Samosa: Instagram limits hashtags to five per post (December 2025)](https://www.socialsamosa.com/news-2/instagram-hashtags-five-per-post-10923075) | Re-read why Instagram moved to five hashtags | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Trends Help: Get started with Google Trends](https://support.google.com/trends/answer/6248105) | Re-read how to compare terms and switch to YouTube Search | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 30 minutes).
2. Build a list of 20 keywords for your niche from four sources: comments and DMs, search suggestions on YouTube and Instagram, Google Trends (Kerala, web and YouTube), and spelling variants.
3. Make three hashtag sets of five each (place, niche, community) and save them in your template library.
4. Optimise 5 challenge posts: keyword in the first caption line, location tag, alt text on photos, one hashtag set.
5. Publish one YouTube video or Short with an optimised title, description and (for long videos) chapters.
6. Note in the Experiments tab which posts had keywords, so you can compare their search traffic later in Module 8.

**Proof to record:** Your 20-keyword list with sources, your three hashtag sets, and links to the 5 optimised posts and the optimised YouTube upload.

## Template: keyword research sheet

```csv
Keyword or phrase,Language or spelling,Source (comments/suggestions/Trends),Trends note,Main or related,Used in (post link)
```

## Template: social SEO checklist

```
INSTAGRAM
[ ] Name field: niche + place
[ ] Bio: keywords written naturally
[ ] Caption line 1: main keyword
[ ] Location tagged (posts about places)
[ ] Alt text written for photos
[ ] Max 5 specific hashtags (one saved set)
YOUTUBE
[ ] Title: search phrase near the start
[ ] Description lines 1-2: what viewers get + keyword
[ ] Chapters (long videos): 00:00 first, 3+, 10 s+
[ ] Correct captions or subtitles
[ ] 1-3 relevant hashtags; never unrelated ones
[ ] Added to a topic playlist
```

## Common mistakes

- **Guessing keywords.** Use your audience's words and search suggestions.
- **Keyword stuffing.** Write naturally; one main keyword and one or two related ones.
- **Generic or unrelated hashtags.** They don't help and, on YouTube, can get a video removed from search.
- **Ignoring spelling variants.** Note how people actually spell place names and dishes.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Where does Instagram suggest putting keywords for search?
    - A) Only in hashtags
    - B) In your password
    - C) Handle, profile name, bio and captions
    - D) Only in comments
2. What happens on YouTube if a video has more than 60 hashtags?
    - A) YouTube ignores all of its hashtags
    - B) Nothing
    - C) It goes viral
    - D) It gets a badge
3. Which three elements does YouTube search prioritise?
    - A) Length, colour and price
    - B) Followers, likes and time
    - C) Relevance, engagement and quality
    - D) Payment, tags and emojis
4. A good Instagram hashtag set for a Kuttiady bakery is:
    - A) No text at all
    - B) #reels #viral #explore #love #instagood
    - C) #kuttiady #kuttiadycakes #kozhikodefood #homebakery #eggless
    - D) 30 random tags

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** Instagram's and YouTube's search guidance, hashtag rules and Google Trends (about 30 minutes)
- **Action:** build a 20-keyword list and hashtag sets, optimise 5 posts and publish an optimised YouTube upload. It is done when your proof is saved: your 20-keyword list with sources, your three hashtag sets, and links to the 5 optimised posts and the optimised YouTube upload.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **C.** Those are the places Instagram's own tips name.
2. **A.** YouTube Help says it will ignore each hashtag on that content.
3. **C.** YouTube also says it doesn't accept payment for organic placement.
4. **C.** Specific place, niche and community tags.

sections.title: SMM-M07-L02: Trends and collaborations
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Spot trends early and use only the ones that fit your niche, with a local twist and licensed audio, and grow faster by collaborating with complementary accounts, disclosing any material connection. **Time:** about 2 hours 30 minutes (35 minutes study, 1 hour 55 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Four kinds of trends

| Trend | Where to spot it | How to use it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Audio** | Sounds you hear repeatedly in the Reels tab and Shorts feed | Use the sound from inside the app (so it's licensed there), with your own local idea |
| **Format** | A structure everyone is copying ("POV", "things that just make sense", "day in my life") | Keep the structure, change the content to your niche |
| **Topic and news** | Local news, Google Trends "Trending now", what people talk about in groups | Only if it fits your niche, after checking facts |
| **Seasonal** | Festivals, monsoon, exams, school reopening | Plan ahead in your calendar (SMM-M06-L01) |

### Use trends that fit, with a twist

A trend helps only if the right people watch. A hyperlocal page joining a format trend with a Kuttiady twist works; a bakery jumping on a national political trend doesn't. Ask three questions:

1. Does it fit my niche and my voice chart?
2. Can I add something local or useful, not just copy?
3. Is it respectful? Never joke about accidents, deaths, disasters or communities.

Speed matters a little; accuracy and taste matter more. For news trends, check with two reliable sources before posting, or don't post.

### Collaborations: borrow trust

Collaborating with another account introduces you to an audience that already trusts them. Options:

- **Instagram Collabs:** a co-authored post that appears on both accounts. Instagram suggests using Collabs or tags when working with other creators, instead of reposting each other's content.
- **Guest appearances:** you appear in their video and they appear in yours, on YouTube or Reels.
- **Complementary local accounts:** a bakery and a florist, a gym and a juice shop, a homestay and a trekking guide.
- **Community pages and groups:** contribute a useful post or a series.
- **Story shout-outs** between friendly accounts in the same area.

The best partners share your audience but don't compete with you, and have a similar size or a little bigger.

### Disclose material connections

If a collaboration involves money, a free product, a discount, a free stay or a family or business relationship, ASCI's guidelines treat it as a **material connection**, even if nobody asked you to promote anything, and the post must carry a clear label such as "Collaboration", "Free gift" or "Ad" where viewers can't miss it. Use the platform's paid partnership label as well when it applies. Module 14 has the full rules; Module 10 covers paid creator work.

## Local example

Anu and Nisha's Oven made a Collab Reel: "Guess the cake flavour blindfolded", filmed in Nisha's kitchen with Anu's cousin as the taster (both agreed to be filmed). Nisha gave them the cakes for free, so the caption started with "Collaboration with @nishasoven (cakes given free)", and the post appeared on both accounts.

| | Anu's page | Nisha's Oven |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Followers before | 1,180 | 2,300 |
| New followers that week | 210 | 160 |
| WhatsApp enquiries mentioning the Reel | — | 14 |

The same week Anu joined an audio trend from the Reels tab with a local twist ("Kuttiady things that just make sense"): 3,900 views, mostly local, and 70 shares.

(Made-up example to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Instagram for Creators: What creators need to know about recommendations](https://creators.instagram.com/blog/instagram-recommendations-eligibility-tips-creators) | Re-read the tip on Collabs and tags instead of reposting | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Trends Help: Get started with Google Trends](https://support.google.com/trends/answer/6248105) | Read about the "Trending now" page | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Creators: Shorts (how to record, add sound, edit and upload)](https://www.youtube.com/creators/create/shorts/) | Re-read how to add sound to a Short | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [ASCI: influencer advertising FAQs](https://www.ascionline.in/social/faqs/) | Read the FAQs on free products, barters and where labels go | 15 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |
| [YouTube Creators (free official guides)](https://www.youtube.com/creators/) | In "Grow", read "Engage your community" | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 35 minutes).
2. Keep a trend log for 3 days: find 5 trends (audio, format, topic or seasonal) that could fit your niche.
3. Use 2 of them in challenge posts with a local or useful twist, using in-app audio.
4. List 5 possible collaboration partners (complementary, similar size, same audience) and send 3 of them a collaboration message.
5. Make and publish at least one collaboration post (a Collab, a guest appearance or a shout-out swap), with a correct disclosure if there is any material connection.

**Proof to record:** Your trend log, links to the 2 trend posts, screenshots of your 3 collaboration messages, and the link to your collaboration post showing the disclosure if one was needed.

## Template: trend checklist

```
TREND: ____________  Type: audio / format / topic / seasonal
Where I saw it: ____________  Date: ____
[ ] Fits my niche and voice chart
[ ] I can add a local or useful twist: ___________
[ ] Respectful (no tragedy, no community jokes)
[ ] Facts checked with 2 sources (news trends)
[ ] Audio added inside the app (not downloaded)
Decision: use / skip
```

## Template: collaboration message (English and Malayalam)

```
EN: Hi [name]! I run @[page], a local page about
[niche] in [area] (about [n] followers, mostly local).
I love your [specific post]. Would you like to make a
Collab Reel together, maybe [specific idea]? It would
appear on both our pages. Happy to do it on a day
that suits you.

ML: നമസ്കാരം [പേര്]! ഞാൻ @[page] എന്ന [ഏരിയ]യിലെ ലോക്കൽ പേജ് നടത്തുന്നു.
നിങ്ങളുടെ [പോസ്റ്റ്] വളരെ ഇഷ്ടമായി. നമുക്ക് ഒരുമിച്ച് ഒരു Collab
Reel ചെയ്താലോ? [ആശയം]. രണ്ടു പേജിലും വരും. നിങ്ങൾക്ക്
സൗകര്യമുള്ള ദിവസം ചെയ്യാം.
```

## Template: collaboration agreement checklist

```
[ ] Idea, date and place agreed
[ ] Who films, who edits, who approves the final cut
[ ] Consent from everyone in the video
[ ] Any money, free product, discount or gift?
    -> label "Collaboration" / "Free gift" / "Ad" at the
       start of the caption and on screen (Module 14)
[ ] Collab invite sent and accepted
[ ] Both share in Stories on the day
```

## Common mistakes

- **Jumping on every trend.** Use only trends that fit your niche, with a twist.
- **Downloading trending songs.** Add trending audio inside the app, where it's licensed.
- **Joking about tragedies.** Some trends hurt people. Skip them.
- **Hidden free gifts.** A free cake or stay is a material connection; label it clearly.
- **Collaborating with competitors only.** Look for complementary accounts with the same audience.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Which trend use is best for a hyperlocal page?
    - A) Reposting the original trend video
    - B) A national political argument
    - C) A format trend with a Kuttiady twist
    - D) A joke about a recent accident
2. A bakery gives you free cakes for a Collab Reel. What must the post include?
    - A) A clear label such as "Collaboration" or "Free gift" where viewers can't miss it
    - B) Only a thank-you in the comments
    - C) Your phone number
    - D) Nothing, it's a collaboration
3. Who makes the best collaboration partner?
    - A) A direct competitor
    - B) A complementary account with the same audience and similar size
    - C) Any huge celebrity
    - D) A fake account
4. How should you add trending audio to a Reel?
    - A) Use a film song file
    - B) Download it from YouTube
    - C) Record it from a speaker
    - D) Select it inside the app when posting

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** Instagram's collab tip, Google Trends, YouTube's Shorts sound guide and ASCI's disclosure FAQs (about 35 minutes)
- **Action:** log 5 trends and use 2, pitch 3 partners and publish a collaboration post with correct disclosure. It is done when your proof is saved: your trend log, links to the 2 trend posts, screenshots of your 3 collaboration messages, and the link to your collaboration post showing the disclosure if one was needed.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **C.** It fits the niche, adds something local and is respectful.
2. **A.** Free products are a material connection under ASCI's guidelines.
3. **B.** Both audiences benefit and nobody loses customers.
4. **D.** In-app audio is licensed for use in the app.

sections.title: SMM-M07-L03: Community, DMs and engagement
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Run a daily engagement routine that turns viewers into a community, handle DMs quickly and kindly, set up moderation filters, and grow without pods, sub4sub or fake engagement. **Time:** about 2 hours 30 minutes (30 minutes study, 2 hours action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Small accounts win by talking to people

A big brand can't reply to everyone. You can. Replying to comments, answering questions and remembering regular followers builds a **community**: people who come back, talk to you and each other, and defend you when someone is rude. Communities also send strong signals to platforms: replies, saves, shares and repeat viewers.

### A daily engagement routine (15–20 minutes)

1. **Reply to every comment** on your recent posts, ideally within a few hours. Answer the actual question; ask a follow-up when it's natural.
2. **Pin the most useful comment** on a post, or one that answers a common question.
3. **Comment meaningfully on 5 posts** from accounts in your niche or area: add something, don't just write "Nice 👍".
4. **One Story with a poll or question sticker**, and reply to the answers.
5. **Check DMs and WhatsApp** and move order or payment conversations to WhatsApp Business.

### Places for your community to gather

- **Instagram Stories and Broadcast channels** for your followers
- **WhatsApp Channel** (one-way updates) or a **WhatsApp group or Community** for two-way chat, only with people who chose to join
- **A Facebook Group** if your audience likes discussion
- **YouTube's Posts tab and comment replies**
- **A Telegram channel with a discussion group** for education niches

Start with one; a dead group is worse than none.

### DMs: fast, kind, useful

- Reply within the same day; set a WhatsApp away message for nights.
- Use your reply templates (SMM-M05-L03), then personalise one line.
- Never send unsolicited sales messages to strangers ("cold DMs") in bulk. They get you blocked and reported.

### Moderation tools (as of October 2026)

- **Instagram:** **Hidden Words** filters offensive words, phrases and emojis (and likely spam DM requests) into a hidden folder; **Limits** temporarily hides comments and DM requests from people who don't follow you or only recently followed.
- **YouTube Studio** (Settings → Content controls): hold comments for review, block specific words, and hold comments with links or hashtags.

Write simple **house rules** ("Be kind, no hate, no spam, no personal attacks") in a Highlight or pinned post, and apply them calmly. SMM-M14-L04 covers negative comments and crises.

### Growth tricks that break the rules

- **Engagement pods** (groups that like and comment on each other's posts) and **follow-for-follow** fill your account with people who don't care about your content.
- **Sub4sub** (subscribe to me and I'll subscribe to you) is prohibited by YouTube's fake engagement policy, and so is promoting services that inflate views, likes or subscribers.
- **Third-party "growth" apps:** Instagram removes inauthentic likes, follows and comments made by such apps and warns the accounts that use them.

Real engagement grows slower and lasts. Fake engagement can get your account restricted and makes your numbers useless for case studies.

## Local example

Anu set up a 15-minute routine at 8 pm daily and started a WhatsApp Channel, "Kuttiady Diaries updates", linked in her bio. She also began a Story series, "Ask a shop owner": followers send questions and she asks the owners on her visits.

After three weeks:

- Replies per post went from about 2 to 9, and many came from the same regulars.
- 380 people followed the Channel; her Channel posts sent 40–80 people to each new Reel.
- Two shop owners messaged her asking whether she could help them with their own pages: her first warm leads for Module 11.

She turned on Hidden Words and blocked two spam accounts that kept posting "DM for followers".

(Made-up example to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Instagram: New ways to protect our community from abuse (Limits, Hidden Words)](https://about.instagram.com/blog/announcements/introducing-new-ways-to-protect-our-community-from-abuse) | Read how Limits and Hidden Words work | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Help: Manage your channel's moderation settings](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/16622701) | Read the moderation settings in YouTube Studio | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Help: Fake engagement policy](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/3399767) | Read what YouTube counts as fake engagement, including sub4sub | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Instagram: Removing fake likes, follows and comments](https://about.instagram.com/blog/announcements/reducing-inauthentic-activity-on-instagram) | Read why Instagram removes likes and follows from third-party apps | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [WhatsApp Help: About creating a WhatsApp Channel](https://faq.whatsapp.com/265055289421317) | Re-read how channels work if you plan one | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 30 minutes).
2. Run the daily engagement routine for 7 days and log the minutes and replies each day.
3. Leave 20 meaningful comments on posts in your niche or area over the week.
4. Turn on Hidden Words on Instagram and the YouTube comment settings that suit you; write house rules in a pinned post or Highlight.
5. Start one community place (a WhatsApp Channel, a group people choose to join, or a Story series) and add its link to your bio.

**Proof to record:** Your 7-day engagement log, screenshots of your moderation settings and house rules, and the link to your new community place.

## Template: daily engagement routine log

```csv
Date,Minutes,Comments replied,Meaningful comments on others,Story poll or question (Y/N),DMs answered,Notes
```

## Template: house rules (English and Malayalam)

```
EN: Welcome! Be kind, disagree politely, no hate, no
    spam, no personal attacks, no fake news. We hide
    or remove comments that break these rules.
ML: സ്വാഗതം! മാന്യമായി പെരുമാറുക, വിയോജിപ്പ് മര്യാദയോടെ മാത്രം.
    വിദ്വേഷം, സ്പാം, വ്യക്തിപരമായ ആക്രമണം, വ്യാജ വാർത്ത
    ഇവ അനുവദനീയമല്ല. ഇത്തരം കമന്റുകൾ മറയ്ക്കുകയോ നീക്കം
    ചെയ്യുകയോ ചെയ്യും.
```

## Template: comment and DM replies that build community

```
QUESTION:   Great question! [answer]. Have you tried ___?
PRAISE:     Thank you, [name]! What should we feature next?
SUGGESTION: Love this idea, adding it to our list 🙌
REGULAR:    [Name], you're always first! 😄 [answer]
ORDER:      Thanks! Please WhatsApp us on ___ and we'll
            sort it in minutes.
```

## Common mistakes

- **Replying with only emojis.** Answer the person and, where natural, ask a question back.
- **Joining engagement pods.** They inflate numbers without real interest and break the spirit of the rules.
- **Mass cold DMs.** They get you blocked and reported. Talk to people who show interest.
- **Starting three community groups at once.** Start one and keep it alive.
- **Arguing publicly with rude commenters.** Use filters, house rules and calm replies (SMM-M14-L04).

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. What does Instagram's Hidden Words do?
    - A) Deletes your account
    - B) Filters offensive words, phrases and emojis into a hidden folder
    - C) Hides your posts
    - D) Translates comments
2. Is "sub4sub" allowed on YouTube?
    - A) Yes, it's encouraged
    - B) Only for small channels
    - C) No, YouTube's fake engagement policy prohibits it
    - D) Only on Shorts
3. What is the best daily habit for a small account?
    - A) Using a growth app
    - B) Posting ten times a day
    - C) Replying meaningfully to every comment and engaging with others in the niche
    - D) Buying likes
4. Where should order and payment conversations move to?
    - A) Nowhere
    - B) Public comments
    - C) WhatsApp Business or DMs
    - D) A Story poll

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** Instagram's and YouTube's moderation tools and fake engagement rules (about 30 minutes)
- **Action:** run a 7-day engagement routine, set moderation filters and house rules, and start one community place. It is done when your proof is saved: your 7-day engagement log, screenshots of your moderation settings and house rules, and the link to your new community place.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **B.** It keeps abusive comments and spammy DM requests out of sight.
2. **C.** Offering to subscribe back for a subscription is fake engagement.
3. **C.** Real conversations build a community and send strong signals.
4. **C.** Keep private details private and use your labels and quick replies.

Action: run a 7-day engagement routine, set moderation filters and house rules, and start one community place

sections.title: Module 8: Analytics
sections.summary: Measure what matters, find patterns in your numbers, track visits with Google Analytics and UTM links, test fairly, and report results clearly. Then turn your 30-day challenge into your first case study.
sections.content:
## Overview

Numbers are only useful when they change what you do next. In three weeks you'll learn the metrics that matter on each platform and the ratios that compare posts fairly, set up Google Analytics 4 on a simple site with UTM links, run A/B tests with YouTube's and Instagram's own tools, and write the kind of one-page report that keeps clients.

The module project is your first portfolio piece: a results report on your 30-day challenge, with real before and after numbers.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Find and explain the key metrics in Instagram, YouTube, WhatsApp, Facebook and LinkedIn
- Calculate share, save, follow and engagement rates and compare groups of posts
- Set up GA4 with UTM links and read the Traffic acquisition report
- Run fair A/B tests and judge how sure you can be
- Write a one-page monthly report and a weekly client update

## Time

About 12 hours in total: 10 hours of lessons and 2 hours for the module project. Part-time: weeks 19–21.

**Full-time track:** Your challenge may still be running. Analyse the days you have now, then finish the case study as soon as day 30 is done.

## Lessons

1. SMM-M08-L01: Key metrics and built-in insights (about 3 hours 30 minutes)
2. SMM-M08-L02: Google Analytics 4 and UTM links (about 3 hours 30 minutes)
3. SMM-M08-L03: A/B tests and client reports (about 3 hours)

## Module project: Case study 1: your 30-day challenge results report

1. Use your challenge data, your ratio analysis and your day-30 summary.
2. Write a one-to-two-page case study with the template in SMM-M12-L02 if you want to look ahead, or simply: the goal, the starting numbers (week 0 baseline and the week before the challenge), what you did, the results after 30 days, the top 3 learnings and what you'll do next.
3. Include 3–5 screenshots of Insights or Studio.
4. Use only real numbers, and say which results are directional.
5. Save it in 08 Analytics and 12 Portfolio.

**Proof to record:** Your case study document with before and after numbers and screenshots.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3. If a row is a 1, redo that part first.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Metrics | Only looks at likes | Knows the main metrics | Explains each platform's key metrics and where to find them |
| Analysis | Reads single posts | Some ratios | Ratios and group comparisons turned into decisions |
| Tracking | No tracking | GA4 or UTMs, not both | GA4 working with consistent UTM links and a tracker |
| Testing | No tests | Tests without hypotheses | Planned tests with one change, a set metric and honest confidence |
| Reporting | No report | Long or unclear report | A one-page report a busy owner understands, plus a case study |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, when PSC prep or work leaves little time:

- Calculate share rate and follow rate for your challenge posts only.
- Make one UTM link for your Instagram bio (GA4 setup can wait).
- Skip the A/B test; write the monthly report.
- Write a half-page case study.

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, read the front, say the answer, then check. Repeat the ones you missed the next day.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| Instagram's main metric since August 2024? | Views. |
| Share rate formula? | Shares ÷ views × 1,000. |
| What does YouTube impressions CTR show? | How often an impression of your thumbnail led to a view. |
| Three UTM parameters to always use? | utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign. |
| Where are UTM results in GA4? | Reports → Acquisition → Traffic acquisition. |
| How does Test & compare choose a winner? | Watch time. |
| Two YouTube Test & compare limits? | Computer only; not for Shorts (also needs advanced features). |
| First things in a monthly report? | Goal, KPI and headline numbers against last month and the target. |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Collecting numbers without decisions.** Every report ends with three actions.
- **Hiding bad months.** Clients trust honest reports; explain and show the plan.
- **Inventing or rounding up results.** Use exact, real numbers. Your reputation depends on it.
