sections.title: SMM-M08-L01: Key metrics and built-in insights
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Read Instagram Insights, YouTube Studio analytics and WhatsApp Business statistics, work out the few ratios that matter, and turn your 30-day challenge numbers into clear decisions. **Time:** about 3 hours 30 minutes (45 minutes study, 2 hours 45 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### The numbers that matter, in plain words

| Metric | What it means | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Views** | How many times a post was seen, counting repeats | Instagram's main metric across formats since August 2024 |
| **Accounts reached** | How many different accounts saw it | Real audience size |
| **Non-follower share** | Views or reach from people who don't follow you | Your growth from recommendations |
| **Interactions** | Likes, comments, shares, saves | Signals of interest |
| **Shares and saves** | Sending to others, keeping for later | The strongest signs a post was valuable |
| **Watch time and retention** | How long people watch, and where they leave | Shows whether the hook and story worked |
| **Follows** | New followers from a post | Whether people want more from you |
| **Profile visits and link clicks** | People looking for more, or going to your link | Consideration |
| **Messages and enquiries** | DMs, WhatsApp chats, calls | Leads, the number businesses care about |

### Where to find them (as of October 2026)

- **Instagram:** open a post and tap **View insights**, or open the **professional dashboard** for the account. Look at Views, the split between followers and non-followers, interactions, and for Reels the watch time. Instagram's creator advice is to watch your **View Rate** in Insights to see whether your hook keeps people watching.
- **YouTube Studio** (phone app or computer): **Impressions** count when your thumbnail was shown for more than a second with at least half of it visible on YouTube. **Impressions click-through rate** shows how often an impression led to a view. **Average view duration** and the **audience retention** graph (intro, top moments, spikes and dips) show where people leave. **Traffic sources** show whether views came from search, the Shorts feed, browse or suggested videos. Data usually takes a day or two to appear.
- **Facebook:** Page insights in Meta Business Suite.
- **WhatsApp Business:** message statistics, and read and reply rates for business broadcasts.
- **LinkedIn:** analytics for your posts and Page.

### Ratios beat raw numbers

A post with 5,000 views and 2 shares did worse than one with 800 views and 40 shares, if your goal is to be shared. Calculate a few ratios per post:

- **Share rate** = shares ÷ views × 1,000 (shares per 1,000 views)
- **Save rate** = saves ÷ views × 1,000
- **Follow rate** = follows ÷ views × 1,000
- **Engagement rate** = interactions ÷ accounts reached × 100
- **Non-follower share** = views from non-followers ÷ views × 100

### From numbers to decisions

Look for **patterns** across many posts, not single surprises. Group your 30 challenge posts by pillar, format, hook type, length and language, and compare the averages. Then write each finding as **"So what? Now what?"**:

- "Shop stories have twice the share rate of food posts → so local people love people stories → post two shop stories a week."

### Be careful with small numbers

With 30 posts, differences of a few per cent can be chance. Treat findings as **directional** and test them again. And remember platforms change how they count: compare with your own past numbers, measured the same way.

## Local example

Anu put her 30 challenge posts in a sheet and grouped them (made-up numbers to show the method):

| Group | Posts | Average views | Shares per 1,000 | Follows per 1,000 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shop stories | 6 | 3,100 | 19 | 9 |
| ₹100 food | 9 | 1,400 | 12 | 6 |
| Local updates (text-heavy) | 5 | 420 | 3 | 2 |
| Places and nostalgia | 6 | 1,050 | 15 | 4 |
| Collabs | 4 | 2,200 | 10 | 11 |
| Question hooks (all pillars) | 13 | 1,700 | 14 | 7 |
| Result-first hooks | 12 | 1,350 | 11 | 6 |

Her decisions: two shop stories a week; text-heavy updates move to the WhatsApp Channel; one collab a month, because collabs bring the most follows per view; keep testing question hooks, since the difference was small.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Social Samosa: Instagram makes Views its main metric (August 2024)](https://socialsamosa.com/news-2/instagram-updates-metrics-creators-prioritise-reach-6807009) | Re-read how Views became Instagram's main metric | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Instagram for Creators: Helping creators of all sizes break through](https://creators.instagram.com/blog/helping-creators-of-all-sizes-break-through) | Re-read the View Rate tip | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Help: Check your impressions and watch time](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/7577430) | Read what counts as an impression and how CTR works | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Help: Measure key moments for audience retention](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/9314415) | Re-read the retention key moments and how to use them | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [WhatsApp Business: business broadcasts](https://whatsappbusiness.com/resources/resource-library/business-broadcasts-whatsapp/) | Re-read the broadcast metrics (read and reply rates) | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |
| [HubSpot Academy: Social Media Certification Course (free)](https://academy.hubspot.com/courses/social-media) | Watch the lesson on measuring social media results (lesson names may change) | 15 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 45 minutes).
2. For all 30 challenge posts, make sure your Posting Log has 7-day views, reach, shares, saves, follows and (for videos) watch time or retention.
3. Add the five ratio columns and fill them with formulas.
4. Group the posts by pillar, format, hook type, length and language, and compare the averages.
5. Write 5 "So what? Now what?" findings with a decision each, and mark which ones need re-testing.

**Proof to record:** Your Posting Log with ratio columns, the grouped comparison table and your 5 findings with decisions.

## Template: ratio formulas for Google Sheets

```
(Assuming views in column J, shares in N, saves in O,
 follows in P, reach in K, interactions in Q, views from
 non-followers in R)
Share rate per 1,000:   =IFERROR(N2/J2*1000,0)
Save rate per 1,000:    =IFERROR(O2/J2*1000,0)
Follow rate per 1,000:  =IFERROR(P2/J2*1000,0)
Engagement rate %:      =IFERROR(Q2/K2*100,0)
Non-follower share %:   =IFERROR(R2/J2*100,0)
Group averages:         =AVERAGEIF(D:D,"Shop story",J:J)
```

## Template: findings: so what, now what

```
FINDING 1: ______________________ (numbers: ____)
  So what? _______________________
  Now what? ______________________
  Confidence: strong / directional (re-test)
FINDING 2: ...
(5 findings)
```

## Common mistakes

- **Reading only views.** Use ratios such as shares, saves and follows per 1,000 views.
- **Comparing with other people's accounts.** Compare with your own past numbers, measured the same way.
- **Deciding from one post.** Look at averages across groups of posts.
- **Checking too early.** Use 7-day numbers; recommended posts keep growing for days.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Which post did better at being shared?
    - A) Impossible to say
    - B) They are equal
    - C) 800 views and 40 shares
    - D) 5,000 views and 2 shares
2. When does YouTube count a thumbnail impression?
    - A) Every time a video is uploaded
    - B) Only when clicked
    - C) When the thumbnail is shown for more than a second with at least half of it visible
    - D) When a video is shared
3. Your findings come from 30 posts and the difference is small. How should you treat it?
    - A) Delete the worse posts
    - B) As proof
    - C) Ignore all data
    - D) As directional, and test it again
4. Which number best shows growth from recommendations?
    - A) Posting time
    - B) The share of views from non-followers
    - C) Total likes
    - D) Number of hashtags

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** Instagram's and YouTube's metric definitions, WhatsApp broadcast stats and HubSpot's measurement lesson (about 45 minutes)
- **Action:** add ratios to your 30 challenge posts, compare groups and write 5 findings with decisions. It is done when your proof is saved: your Posting Log with ratio columns, the grouped comparison table and your 5 findings with decisions.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **C.** 50 shares per 1,000 views against 0.4 per 1,000.
2. **C.** That is YouTube's definition, on YouTube surfaces.
3. **D.** Small samples can mislead; re-test before big changes.
4. **B.** Non-follower views show the system is showing you to new people.

sections.title: SMM-M08-L02: Google Analytics 4 and UTM links
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Set up a free Google Analytics 4 property on a simple site, tag your social links with UTM parameters, and read which platform and post sent visitors. **Time:** about 3 hours 30 minutes (45 minutes study, 2 hours 45 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Why bother with Google Analytics

Platform insights tell you what happened **on** the platform. When a post sends people to a website (a business's booking page, a menu, your portfolio), **Google Analytics 4 (GA4)** tells you what happened next: how many arrived, from which platform and campaign, and what they did. GA4 is free; Google's setup guide says it gives insights "at no cost".

### Set up GA4 in four steps (as of October 2026)

1. **Account:** sign in at analytics.google.com and create an account.
2. **Property:** name it ("Anu portfolio"), choose India's time zone and rupees.
3. **Web data stream:** add your site's address; turn on enhanced measurement.
4. **Add the tag:** copy the **Measurement ID** (it starts with "G-") into your site. On **Google Sites**, open Settings → Analytics and enter the ID. Google Sites' help notes that data can take up to 24 hours to show, and that visitors who reject cookies make the numbers lower than real.

Test it: open your site on your phone and check the **Realtime** report.

### A simple site to practise on

If you don't have a site yet, make a one-page **Google Sites** page now, such as "About @kuttiady.diaries" or a menu page for a friendly business. You'll turn it into your portfolio in Module 12.

### UTM links: labels on your links

A UTM link is a normal link with labels added at the end, so GA4 knows where each visitor came from. Google's rules:

- **Always use** `utm_source`, `utm_medium` and `utm_campaign`. Missing ones show up as "(not set)".
- **Optional:** `utm_content` (to tell apart two links in the same place), `utm_term` (paid keywords) and `utm_id`.
- **Values are case-sensitive:** `instagram` and `Instagram` are different, so always use lowercase.

Example:

`https://sites.google.com/view/yourpage?utm_source=instagram&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=bio_link`

Use Google's free **Campaign URL Builder** to make them without typing mistakes. Never put names, phone numbers or other personal details in a UTM.

### Read the results

In GA4, open **Reports → Acquisition → Traffic acquisition**. The **session source / medium** shows "instagram / social", "whatsapp / social" and so on; **session campaign** shows your campaign names; the default channel groups include **Organic Social** and **Paid Social**.

### WhatsApp is different

A WhatsApp click-to-chat link opens a chat, not a website, so GA4 can't see it. Track WhatsApp enquiries with **keywords** in your CTA ("send 'SQUAT'"), **labels** in WhatsApp Business and the question "how did you hear about us?".

## Local example

Peak Fitness made a one-page Google Site with its timetable and fees, connected GA4, and used three UTM links for two weeks:

| Where | utm_source | utm_medium | utm_campaign | Sessions (2 weeks) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Instagram bio | instagram | social | bio_link | 96 |
| WhatsApp Status | whatsapp | social | status_timetable | 41 |
| YouTube description | youtube | social | gym_tour | 18 |

Instagram sent the most visitors, but WhatsApp visitors stayed on the page longer and more of them messaged afterwards. The gym kept the bio link and started posting the timetable on Status every Monday.

(Made-up numbers to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Analytics Help: Set up Analytics for a website and/or app](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/9304153) | Read the four setup steps | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Sites Help: Use Analytics with your site](https://support.google.com/sites/answer/97459) | Read how to connect Analytics to Google Sites | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Sites Help: How to use Google Sites](https://support.google.com/sites/answer/6372878) | Read how to create and publish a Google Site | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Analytics Help: URL builders (collect campaign data with UTM links)](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/10917952) | Read the UTM rules and the example | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Google Analytics demos and tools: Campaign URL Builder](https://ga-dev-tools.web.app/ga4/campaign-url-builder/) | Open the Campaign URL Builder | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Analytics Help: Traffic acquisition report](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/12923437) | Read how to find and read the Traffic acquisition report | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Analytics Help: Analytics Academy on Skillshop (free courses)](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/15440208) | Optional: note the free Analytics Academy courses for later | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 45 minutes).
2. Create a one-page Google Site (or use a page you already have) and publish it.
3. Create a GA4 property and web data stream, and add the Measurement ID to the site. Check Realtime from your phone.
4. Write your UTM naming rules (lowercase, underscores) and make 3 UTM links with the Campaign URL Builder: Instagram bio, WhatsApp Status or Channel, and a YouTube description.
5. Use them for at least 7 days, then read the Traffic acquisition report and note sessions by source and campaign.

**Proof to record:** Your published site link, a screenshot of GA4 Realtime or Traffic acquisition showing your UTM sources, and your UTM tracker sheet.

**Full-time track:** Leave the UTM links running while you continue; read the report after 7 real days.

## Template: UTM naming rules and tracker

```
RULES: lowercase only; underscores, no spaces;
       source = the platform; medium = social / paid_social /
       email / qr; campaign = what or when (bio_link,
       onam_2026, pilot_week1); no personal data
Link name,Destination URL,utm_source,utm_medium,utm_campaign,utm_content,Full UTM link,Where used,Date added
```

## Template: GA4 setup checklist

```
[ ] Account created (analytics.google.com)
[ ] Property: name, India time zone, INR
[ ] Web data stream with the site URL
[ ] Enhanced measurement on
[ ] Measurement ID (G-...) added to the site
[ ] Realtime shows my own visit
[ ] 3 UTM links in use, recorded in the tracker
[ ] After 7 days: Reports > Acquisition > Traffic acquisition
```

## Common mistakes

- **Mixed capitals in UTMs.** "Instagram" and "instagram" become two sources. Use lowercase always.
- **Missing source, medium or campaign.** You'll see "(not set)". Always use all three.
- **Expecting GA4 to track WhatsApp chats.** It can't; use keywords, labels and asking customers.
- **Personal data in links.** Never put names or phone numbers in UTMs.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Which three UTM parameters should you always use?
    - A) None
    - B) utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign
    - C) utm_name, utm_phone, utm_city
    - D) utm_term, utm_id, utm_content
2. Why must UTM values be lowercase every time?
    - A) Capitals are illegal
    - B) It hides them
    - C) They are case-sensitive, so different capitals split your data
    - D) GA4 deletes capitals
3. Where do you see which platform sent visitors in GA4?
    - A) YouTube Studio
    - B) Admin → Property settings
    - C) Reports → Acquisition → Traffic acquisition
    - D) Realtime only
4. How should you measure enquiries from a WhatsApp click-to-chat link?
    - A) You can't measure them at all
    - B) With UTMs inside the chat
    - C) GA4 tracks them automatically
    - D) With CTA keywords, WhatsApp labels and asking customers

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** Google's GA4 setup, Sites, UTM and Traffic acquisition guides (about 45 minutes)
- **Action:** set up GA4 on a simple Google Site, run 3 UTM links for 7 days and read the results. It is done when your proof is saved: your published site link, a screenshot of GA4 Realtime or Traffic acquisition showing your UTM sources, and your UTM tracker sheet.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **B.** Google says to always use these three.
2. **C.** utm_source=google and utm_source=Google are different values.
3. **C.** The report shows session source / medium and campaign.
4. **D.** The link opens a chat, not a website, so GA4 can't see it.

sections.title: SMM-M08-L03: A/B tests and client reports
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Run fair A/B tests with the tools platforms provide, judge results honestly, and write a monthly report that a busy shop owner can understand in two minutes. **Time:** about 3 hours (40 minutes study, 2 hours 20 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Testing on social media is noisy

Every post is different: the topic, the day, the weather, what else was trending. So a "test" between two different posts is never perfectly fair. You can still learn a lot if you:

1. **Write a hypothesis first:** "A question hook will get more 3-second views than a result-first hook on food Reels."
2. **Change one thing** and keep everything else as similar as you can.
3. **Repeat it:** at least 3–4 posts per version, or use a tool that splits the audience for you.
4. **Choose the metric before you start:** the one that matches the hypothesis.
5. **Decide:** keep, drop or test again, and write it in the Experiments tab.

### Tools that split the audience for you (as of October 2026)

- **YouTube Test & compare:** test up to three titles, three thumbnails or combinations on a long video. YouTube shows the versions to different viewers and picks the winner by **watch time**, not clicks, usually within two weeks. It works in YouTube Studio on a computer only, not for Shorts, and needs advanced features turned on. Your old laptop is enough.
- **Instagram trial reels:** show a reel to non-followers first and see how it does after about 24 hours, before deciding whether to share it with followers. Useful for testing a risky idea.
- **Meta Ads A/B tests:** in Ads Manager (Module 9), with a budget.

### How sure can you be?

With small accounts, most results are **directional**. Say "this seemed to work, we'll test it again" rather than "this works". If a difference repeats in two or three tests, act on it.

### The monthly client report

Owners are busy. A good report fits on **one page**, with details after it:

1. **Goal and KPI:** "Goal: more weekday orders. KPI: WhatsApp chats from Instagram. Target: 30 a month."
2. **Headline numbers:** this month against last month and the target, with arrows and plain words.
3. **What worked:** the top 3 posts with one-line reasons.
4. **What didn't,** honestly, and why you think so.
5. **What we tested and learned.**
6. **Next month's plan:** 3 actions.
7. **What I need from you:** photos, offers, approvals.

Write in plain language (Malayalam for owners who prefer it), show screenshots, and never claim results you can't connect to your work. A short **weekly WhatsApp update** ("This week: 4 posts, 2,300 views, 11 chats; best post was ...") keeps clients confident between reports.

## Local example

Anu wrote a practice report for her own page after the challenge (made-up numbers):

> **@kuttiady.diaries, report for 1–30 November**
> **Goal:** become the page local people share. **KPIs:** views per post, shares per 1,000 views, local followers.
> **Headline:** 30 posts (target 30) ✅. Average 7-day views 1,150 (October: 310) ⬆. Shares per 1,000 views 13 (October: 6) ⬆. Followers 1,640 (start 820) ⬆.
> **What worked:** shop stories (19 shares per 1,000), collabs (most follows per view), question hooks (small lead, re-testing).
> **What didn't:** text-heavy updates (3 shares per 1,000) → moving to the WhatsApp Channel.
> **Tested:** posting at 1 pm vs 7:30 pm: similar views, faster replies at 7:30 pm.
> **December plan:** 2 shop stories a week; 1 collab; test 15 vs 30 seconds again.
> **Needs:** permission from 4 more shops for stories.

She also ran a Test & compare on her first long video's thumbnail from the laptop: the version with a face won on watch time.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [YouTube Help: A/B test titles and thumbnails](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/16391400) | Read how Test & compare works, its limits and how the winner is chosen | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [TechCrunch: Instagram trial reels (December 2024)](https://techcrunch.com/2024/12/10/instagram-rolls-out-trial-reels-that-arent-shown-to-a-creators-followers) | Re-read how trial reels work | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Instagram for Creators: Finding success on reels in 2025](https://creators.instagram.com/blog/the-latest-with-instagram) | Re-read the trial reels tip | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Digital Culture Network: boosted posts vs ad campaigns](https://digitalculturenetwork.org.uk/knowledge/whats-the-difference-between-boosted-posts-and-ad-campaigns-on-facebook-and-instagram/) | Read the part on A/B testing in Ads Manager (you'll use it in Module 9) | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [HubSpot Academy: Social Media Certification Course (free)](https://academy.hubspot.com/courses/social-media) | Watch the lesson on reporting and ROI (lesson names may change) | 15 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 35 minutes).
2. Plan one A/B test with the template: a YouTube Test & compare on a long video (on the laptop), a trial reel test, or a two-version test across 3–4 posts each.
3. Run it, and record the result honestly as strong or directional in the Experiments tab.
4. Write a one-page monthly report for your own account using the template, with screenshots.
5. Write a weekly WhatsApp update for a pretend client in Malayalam or English.

**Proof to record:** Your A/B test plan and result, your one-page monthly report and your weekly WhatsApp update.

## Template: A/B test plan

```
HYPOTHESIS: If I ________, then ________ will rise,
            because ________.
ONE CHANGE: version A ________ / version B ________
KEPT THE SAME: topic type, length, time, day, pillar
TOOL: Test & compare / trial reel / 3-4 posts each
METRIC (chosen before): ________
RESULT: A ____ B ____  Confidence: strong / directional
DECISION: keep / drop / test again on ____
```

## Template: monthly report (one page)

```
[BUSINESS or ACCOUNT] - SOCIAL MEDIA REPORT, [MONTH]
GOAL: ______________  KPI: ____________  TARGET: ____
HEADLINE NUMBERS     This month  Last month  Target
  [KPI]              ____        ____        ____
  Posts              ____        ____        ____
  Views/reach        ____        ____
  Enquiries (chats)  ____        ____
WHAT WORKED (top 3 posts): 1. ____ 2. ____ 3. ____
WHAT DIDN'T, AND WHY: ____________________________
WHAT WE TESTED: __________ RESULT: _____________
NEXT MONTH (3 actions): 1. ____ 2. ____ 3. ____
WHAT I NEED FROM YOU: ____________________________
(Screenshots and full numbers on the next pages)
```

## Template: weekly WhatsApp update

```
EN: Hi [name], this week on Instagram: [n] posts,
[n] views, [n] WhatsApp chats. Best post: [link]
([reason]). Next week: [plan]. Can you send [photos/offer]
by [day]?
ML: നമസ്കാരം [പേര്], ഈ ആഴ്ച: [n] പോസ്റ്റുകൾ, [n] വ്യൂസ്,
[n] വാട്സാപ്പ് ചാറ്റുകൾ. മികച്ച പോസ്റ്റ്: [link].
അടുത്ത ആഴ്ച: [പ്ലാൻ]. [ഫോട്ടോ/ഓഫർ] [ദിവസം] മുൻപ് അയക്കാമോ?
```

## Common mistakes

- **Calling one comparison "proof".** Say directional, and re-test.
- **Changing the metric after seeing the results.** Choose it before the test.
- **Ten-page reports nobody reads.** One page first; details after.
- **Taking credit for everything.** Say what you can connect to your work and what you can't.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. How does YouTube's Test & compare decide the winning thumbnail?
    - A) Your choice
    - B) Most likes
    - C) Most clicks
    - D) Highest watch time
2. Which is a well-written hypothesis?
    - A) "Make it viral"
    - B) "Let's see what happens"
    - C) "Post more"
    - D) "If I use a question hook on food Reels, 3-second views will rise, because it creates curiosity"
3. What should come first in a monthly client report?
    - A) Every post's screenshot
    - B) Your hourly rate
    - C) The goal, KPI and headline numbers against last month and the target
    - D) Hashtags used
4. Where can you run YouTube Test & compare?
    - A) On Shorts only
    - B) On the phone app
    - C) In YouTube Studio on a computer, for long videos
    - D) In Instagram

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** YouTube's Test & compare, Instagram trial reels, A/B testing in ads and HubSpot's reporting lesson (about 35 minutes)
- **Action:** run one A/B test, write a one-page monthly report and a weekly WhatsApp update. It is done when your proof is saved: your A/B test plan and result, your one-page monthly report and your weekly WhatsApp update.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **D.** YouTube optimises these tests for watch time.
2. **D.** It names one change, one metric and a reason.
3. **C.** Owners need the result in two minutes; details can follow.
4. **C.** It is computer-only and not available for Shorts.

sections.title: Module 9: Paid ads
sections.summary: Learn to spend small amounts of money wisely: when to boost and when to use Ads Manager, how to choose objectives, audiences and budgets, how to test creatives, retarget and use Click-to-WhatsApp ads, the basics of YouTube and Google ads, and how to tell whether an ad made money.
sections.content:
## Overview

Ads amplify what already works. In three weeks you'll set up an ad account safely, learn from other businesses' ads in Meta's Ad Library, plan audiences and rupee budgets, test creatives, and calculate return on ad spend and profit.

Running a real ad is optional. The module project lets you choose a tiny test of ₹300–₹1,000 or a ₹0 dry run.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Decide between boosting and an Ads Manager campaign
- Choose an objective that matches the result you're paying for
- Plan audiences, budgets and a creative test in rupees
- Plan retargeting and Click-to-WhatsApp ads, and explain YouTube and Google ad formats
- Calculate cost per result, ROAS, profit and ROI

## Time

About 11 hours 30 minutes in total: 10 hours of lessons and 1 hour 30 minutes for the module project. Part-time: weeks 22–24.

## Lessons

1. SMM-M09-L01: Boosting vs Ads Manager: objectives, setup and policies (about 3 hours 30 minutes)
2. SMM-M09-L02: Targeting, small budgets and creative testing (about 3 hours 30 minutes)
3. SMM-M09-L03: Retargeting, Click-to-WhatsApp, YouTube and Google ads, and ROI (about 3 hours)

## Module project: Your ad plan and an optional tiny test ad

1. Choose: run a tiny test (₹300–₹1,000 plus GST, your own money or a business that agrees to pay), or a ₹0 dry run.
2. Tiny test: run your plan from SMM-M09-L02 for 5–7 days on a post that already did well organically, with a spending limit set. Track results daily.
3. Dry run: build the full campaign in Ads Manager and save it as a draft without publishing, then write what you expect to happen and why.
4. Either way, fill in the ROI calculator (with real or expected numbers) and write three lessons.
5. Save screenshots with personal and payment details hidden.

**Proof to record:** Your ad plan, screenshots of the test results or the saved draft, the ROI calculation and your three lessons.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3. If a row is a 1, redo that part first.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Decision | Boosts everything | Knows boost vs Ads Manager | Chooses the right tool and objective for each goal |
| Set-up and rules | No limits, unclear ownership | Account set up | Portfolio, admin access, spending limit, policies and GST checked |
| Targeting and budget | Random | Some plan | A local audience and a rupee budget with a break-even |
| Creative testing | One ad | Two similar ads | 2–3 different creatives with a success rule |
| ROI | Judges by likes | Counts results | Calculates cost per customer, ROAS, profit and ROI |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, when PSC prep or work leaves little time:

- Do the three 5-minute Blueprint lessons and the Ad Library task.
- Write a test plan with two creatives.
- Do the ROI calculation with the Amma's Pickles example numbers.
- Choose the ₹0 dry run.

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, read the front, say the answer, then check. Repeat the ones you missed the next day.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| Boost or Ads Manager for a planned 3-creative test? | Ads Manager. |
| Ads Manager's six objective groups (October 2026)? | Awareness, Traffic, Engagement, Leads, App promotion, Sales. |
| Safety setting before your first ad? | A monthly spending limit. |
| GST on Google Ads purchases in India without a GSTIN? | 18% (check current rules). |
| Biggest lever in a small campaign? | The creative. |
| Cost per result formula? | Total cost (with GST) ÷ results. |
| ROAS formula? | Revenue from the ad ÷ ad spend. |
| When can a skippable YouTube ad be skipped? | After 5 seconds. |
| Customer lists for custom audiences need what? | Consent from the people when their details were collected. |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Spending before the organic content works.** Prove it organically first, then amplify.
- **Hiding results from a client.** Report cost per customer honestly, good or bad.
- **Promising results from ads.** Promise a clear test and honest numbers, not sales.

sections.title: SMM-M09-L01: Boosting vs Ads Manager: objectives, setup and policies
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Decide when an ad is worth paying for, choose between boosting a post and an Ads Manager campaign, pick the right objective, and set up an ad account safely and within the rules. **Time:** about 3 hours 30 minutes (1 hour 15 minutes study, 2 hours 15 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Organic first, then pay to amplify

Ads don't fix weak content; they show it to more people faster. The safest small-budget approach:

1. Post organically and find what works (Modules 6–8).
2. Put money behind a post or offer that already does well, or an offer with a real deadline.
3. Measure the cost of each result (a message, a booking, an order) and compare it with what that result is worth.

### Boosting or Ads Manager?

| | **Boost a post** | **Ads Manager campaign** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Where | From the post, the Instagram or Facebook app, or Meta Business Suite | Ads Manager (in Meta Business Suite, or on a computer) |
| Goals | Basic: engagement, profile visits, website visits, messages | Full range of campaign objectives, including leads and sales |
| Targeting | Simple | Detailed: location, age, interests, custom and lookalike audiences |
| Placements and formats | Limited | Choose placements (Reels, Stories, Feed, Messenger); video, carousel and Stories ads |
| Testing and reports | Basic insights | A/B tests and detailed reports |
| Best for | A quick, small push for one good post | A planned test with a clear goal, running at least a week |

(Based on the Digital Culture Network's comparison, updated September 2026. Boost options change often; check what your app shows.)

### Choosing an objective

Ads Manager asks for your **objective** first, and the system then shows your ad to the people most likely to do that thing. As of October 2026 Ads Manager groups its objectives into six: **Awareness, Traffic, Engagement, Leads, App promotion and Sales** (check the current names in Ads Manager). For a small local business:

- Reach people nearby who haven't heard of you → **Awareness**
- Get people to message you on WhatsApp, Messenger or Instagram → an objective with **messages** as the conversion location (Meta's free Blueprint course "Selecting campaign objectives" explains conversion locations)
- Collect enquiries with a form → **Leads**
- Online sales on a website → **Sales** (needs tracking set up)

Pick the objective that matches the result you will pay for. Asking for "engagement" when you want orders gets you likes, not orders.

### Setting up an ad account safely

The Digital Culture Network's checklist (updated October 2026):

- Use your **real personal Facebook profile**; Meta often disables obviously fake ones.
- Have **admin access** to the Facebook Page and Instagram account you'll advertise.
- Keep the Page, Instagram account and ad account in one **Business Portfolio** in Meta Business Suite.
- Add a payment method and set a **monthly spending limit** as a safety net.
- The **Meta Pixel** (code on a website that tracks what people do after clicking) is optional for beginners; if you add it, the website's privacy policy must mention it.

**Taxes:** ad purchases can attract GST. Google's help page, for example, says Google Asia Pacific charges 18% GST on Google Ads purchases in India unless a valid GSTIN is given. Check the taxes shown on Meta's billing screen before you pay, and budget for them.

### Advertising rules

- Ads must follow Meta's advertising standards. Ads about **social issues, elections or politics** have extra requirements, including authorisation and disclaimers; keep clients' ads away from them unless you know the rules.
- Advertisers must disclose when certain political or social issue ads were digitally created or altered, and Meta labels AI-generated content (as of October 2026).
- Indian law applies to ads too: no misleading claims, no fake urgency, no unqualified health or money promises (SMM-M05-L02, Module 14).
- Use **Meta's Ad Library** to see the ads that other Pages are running; it's the free way to learn what local competitors advertise.

## Local example

Nisha's Oven had two options for Christmas:

- **Boost** her best-performing Reel (a plum cake being sliced, 6,000 organic views) for ₹300 over 3 days to people within about 8 km, goal "messages".
- **Ads Manager campaign:** a 7-day campaign with a messages goal, three different videos, a 10 km radius around Kuttiady, and a spending limit of ₹1,500.

She chose to boost first, because it was quick and her post had already proved itself. It brought 19 WhatsApp chats and 7 orders. Encouraged, she planned an Ads Manager campaign for the next festival, to test which of three videos brought chats most cheaply.

Before either, she checked Meta's Ad Library: two bakeries in town were running Christmas ads, both with discounts and no price. Hers showed the price clearly.

(Made-up example to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Digital Culture Network: boosted posts vs ad campaigns](https://digitalculturenetwork.org.uk/knowledge/whats-the-difference-between-boosted-posts-and-ad-campaigns-on-facebook-and-instagram/) | Read the whole comparison of boosted posts and ad campaigns | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Digital Culture Network: what you need to set up Meta ads](https://digitalculturenetwork.org.uk/knowledge/what-you-need-to-set-up-meta-ads/) | Read what you need to set up Meta ads | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Meta Blueprint: Get started with advertising on Facebook and Instagram](https://www.facebookblueprint.com/student/path/211543-meta-advertising-course) | Free sign-up. Do all three 5-minute lessons | 15 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Meta Blueprint: Selecting campaign objectives in Meta Ads Manager](https://www.facebookblueprint.com/student/path/219699-ad-objectives-course) | Do both lessons on objectives and conversion locations | 16 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Meta Transparency Center: Meta Ad Library tools](https://transparency.meta.com/researchtools/ad-library-tools/) | Open the Ad Library and search for 5 local businesses | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 (page title checked) |
| [Meta Transparency Center: Ads about social issues, elections or politics](https://transparency.meta.com/policies/ad-standards/SIEP-advertising/SIEP) | Note the extra rules for social issue, election and political ads | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 (page title checked) |
| [Google Ads Help: Taxes in your country (India: GST)](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2375370) | Read the India section on GST | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 1 hour 10 minutes).
2. Set up (or check) a Business Portfolio with your Page, Instagram account and an ad account, following the checklist. Set a low monthly spending limit. Don't run an ad yet.
3. For three scenarios (a bakery wanting orders, a homestay wanting bookings, your page wanting local followers), write which you'd use (boost or Ads Manager) and which objective, with one sentence why.
4. Search Meta's Ad Library for 5 businesses in your area or niche. For each, note the creative, the message, the call to action and how long the ad has run.

**Proof to record:** A screenshot of your set-up (with personal details hidden), your three scenario decisions and your Ad Library notes on 5 advertisers.

## Template: ad readiness checklist

```
[ ] The post or offer already works organically
    (or has a real deadline)
[ ] One clear result to pay for (messages / leads /
    sales / reach)
[ ] Real personal profile; admin on Page and Instagram
[ ] Business Portfolio with Page + Instagram + ad account
[ ] Payment method added; monthly spending limit set
[ ] Taxes (GST) included in the budget
[ ] WhatsApp quick replies and labels ready for chats
[ ] Claims checked: no misleading, health or money promises
[ ] Not a social issue, election or political ad
```

## Template: objective chooser

```
I want people to...                   -> choose
  notice us nearby                    -> Awareness
  visit our website                   -> Traffic
  message us (WhatsApp/Messenger/DM)  -> an objective with
                                         messages as the
                                         conversion location
  fill in an enquiry form             -> Leads
  buy on our website                  -> Sales (needs tracking)
  install our app                     -> App promotion
Boost when: one proven post, small budget, quick push.
Ads Manager when: a planned test, several creatives,
  detailed targeting, a week or more.
```

## Common mistakes

- **Boosting a weak post.** If it didn't interest people for free, paying shows it to more people who won't care.
- **The wrong objective.** Paying for engagement when you want orders buys likes.
- **No spending limit.** Set a monthly limit before your first ad.
- **Forgetting GST.** Budget for taxes on top of the ad spend.
- **Fake or dummy profiles.** Meta often disables them, and your ad account with them.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. When is boosting a post a sensible choice?
    - A) For a quick, small push of one post that already performed well
    - B) For political ads
    - C) Never
    - D) For a planned test of three creatives
2. A homestay wants WhatsApp enquiries from an ad. What should it choose?
    - A) App promotion
    - B) An Awareness objective with no CTA
    - C) Nothing, just post more
    - D) An objective with messages as the conversion location
3. What should you set before running your first ad?
    - A) A fake profile
    - B) A monthly spending limit
    - C) Ten hashtags
    - D) A political disclaimer
4. What does Meta's Ad Library let you do?
    - A) Buy cheaper ads
    - B) See competitors' private results
    - C) Remove ads
    - D) See the ads that Pages are running

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** The Digital Culture Network's guides, three free Meta Blueprint courses, the Ad Library and the tax rules (about 1 hour 10 minutes)
- **Action:** set up an ad account safely, choose objectives for three scenarios and study 5 advertisers in the Ad Library. It is done when your proof is saved: a screenshot of your set-up (with personal details hidden), your three scenario decisions and your Ad Library notes on 5 advertisers.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **A.** Boosts are simple; Ads Manager is better for planned tests.
2. **D.** Choose the objective that matches the result you will pay for.
3. **B.** A limit protects you from overspending.
4. **D.** It is a free transparency tool for learning from others' ads.

sections.title: SMM-M09-L02: Targeting, small budgets and creative testing
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Choose a sensible audience for a local business, plan a small test budget in rupees, and test two or three creatives so that the numbers tell you which message works. **Time:** about 3 hours 30 minutes (45 minutes study, 2 hours 45 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Audiences, from broad to narrow

| Audience | What it is | When to use it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Location + age** | People in or near a place, in an age range | Almost every local business: a radius around the shop |
| **Advantage+ audience** | Meta's automated targeting, which looks for the people most likely to get your result | Often a good default when the creative is clear; Meta Blueprint has a short free video on it |
| **Interests** | People Meta thinks are interested in a topic | When your product clearly fits an interest; don't stack many |
| **Custom audiences** | People who already interacted: watched your videos, engaged with your Page or Instagram, visited your website (with the Pixel), or a customer list | Retargeting (SMM-M09-L3). Customer lists only if people agreed when you collected their details |
| **Lookalike audiences** | New people similar to a custom audience | Later, once you have a few hundred engaged people or customers |

For a shop in Kuttiady, start simple: a radius around the shop that matches its real delivery or travel area, sensible ages, and either broad targeting or Advantage+ audience. With small budgets, narrow targeting often just makes ads cost more.

### Small budgets: plan in rupees

You don't need lakhs to learn. A test budget of **₹500–₹1,000 plus GST**, spread over 5–7 days, is enough to compare two or three creatives directionally. Ads Manager shows the minimum it will accept when you set a daily or lifetime budget. Decide in advance:

- **Daily or lifetime budget:** lifetime budgets stop automatically at the total.
- **How long:** at least 5–7 days, so the system has time to find people.
- **The result you're buying** and the most you'll pay for it (your break-even, SMM-M09-L03).

### Creative is the biggest lever

The audience and the budget matter, but the **ad itself** decides most results. Test creatives, not tiny settings:

- **Two or three versions** with different hooks or angles: price-first, result-first, a customer story.
- **Made for the placement:** vertical video for Reels and Stories, with captions. Meta's free Blueprint videos include one on adding Reels placements to campaigns.
- **The first 3 seconds** carry the message, as in organic posts.
- **One offer, one call to action,** and a clear price where possible.
- Ads Manager's **A/B test** feature can split the audience between versions; or put the versions in one ad set and compare cost per result.

### The numbers to watch

- **CPM:** cost per 1,000 impressions (how expensive it is to reach people)
- **CTR:** clicks ÷ impressions (how interesting the ad is)
- **Cost per result:** spend ÷ results (messages, leads, orders); the number that matters
- **Frequency:** how many times each person saw it on average; if it climbs high, people get tired of it

Small tests give **directional** answers. If one creative gets messages at half the cost of the others, that's a useful signal to test again with more budget.

## Local example

Peak Fitness ran a 7-day test with ₹1,050 plus GST (made-up numbers to show the method):

- **Audience:** about 6 km around the gym, ages 20–45, Advantage+ audience
- **Result:** WhatsApp messages
- **Three Reels:** A "First session free" (offer-first), B a trainer fixing a squat (value-first), C a member's 90-day story (shared with her written permission)

| Creative | Spend (₹) | Messages | Cost per message (₹) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A Offer-first | 350 | 9 | 39 |
| B Value-first | 350 | 14 | 25 |
| C Member story | 350 | 6 | 58 |

Eleven of the 29 people who messaged booked a free session and 4 joined (₹1,500 a month each). The value-first Reel won this round; they planned to re-test it against a new member story before spending more.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Meta Blueprint: Create audiences in Meta Ads Manager](https://www.facebookblueprint.com/student/path/211545-ads-manager-audiences) | Do both lessons on audience types and creating audiences | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Meta Blueprint: Browse free courses from the Blueprint catalog](https://www.facebookblueprint.com/student/page/512235-browse-free-courses-from-the-blueprint-catalog) | Watch "Use Advantage+ audience" and "Include Reels placements in your campaigns" | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Digital Culture Network: reaching your audience with Meta ads](https://digitalculturenetwork.org.uk/knowledge/reaching-your-audience-making-your-meta-ads-more-effective/) | Read cold, custom and lookalike audiences and the advice on ad fatigue | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Digital Culture Network: boosted posts vs ad campaigns](https://digitalculturenetwork.org.uk/knowledge/whats-the-difference-between-boosted-posts-and-ad-campaigns-on-facebook-and-instagram/) | Re-read the part on A/B testing | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Google Ads Help: Write compelling, genuine ad copy](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6167101) | Re-read the advice on genuine, benefit-led copy | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 35 minutes).
2. Choose a real scenario: your page (for example, more local followers or "suggest a spot" messages) or a friendly local business.
3. Write an audience plan: location and radius, ages, and broad, Advantage+ or interests, with your reason.
4. Plan a budget in rupees including GST, with duration and the most you'll pay per result.
5. Make 2–3 ad creatives with different hooks, sized for Reels and Stories, with captions and one CTA.
6. Write the test plan. (You'll decide in the module project whether to run it.)

**Proof to record:** Your audience plan, budget plan, 2–3 creatives and the complete test plan.

## Template: ad test plan

```
BUSINESS / PAGE: ______________  DATES: ____ to ____
RESULT I'M BUYING: messages / leads / follows / visits
MOST I'LL PAY PER RESULT: Rs ____ (break-even: Rs ____)
AUDIENCE: radius ___ km around ______; ages ___-___;
          broad / Advantage+ / interests: ________
BUDGET: Rs ____ + GST, lifetime, ___ days
CREATIVES: A ________ B ________ C ________
           (hook, offer, CTA for each)
PLACEMENTS: Reels / Stories / Feed (vertical first)
SUCCESS RULE: if one creative's cost per result is
  below Rs ____ after 5 days, re-test it with Rs ____
```

## Template: budget calculator

```
Ad budget (Rs)                     A = ______
GST (check the rate on the bill)   B = A x ___% = ____
Total cost                         C = A + B = ______
Expected cost per result (guess)   D = ______
Expected results                   E = A / D = ______
Value of one result to the business F = ______
Worth it if                        E x F > C
```

## Common mistakes

- **Very narrow targeting on a tiny budget.** It often raises costs. Start broad or with Advantage+ within your real area.
- **Testing settings instead of creatives.** The ad's message matters most; test hooks and angles.
- **Judging after one day.** Give a test 5–7 days.
- **Customer lists without consent.** Upload lists only if people agreed when you collected their details.
- **Horizontal videos for Reels ads.** Make vertical versions with captions.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. For a small local test, which audience is usually a good start?
    - A) Everyone over 13
    - B) Ten stacked interests across India
    - C) A radius around the shop with broad targeting or Advantage+ audience
    - D) A bought email list
2. Which number matters most when judging a messages campaign?
    - A) Impressions only
    - B) Cost per message (and how many messages became customers)
    - C) Likes
    - D) Followers
3. What is the biggest lever in most small ad campaigns?
    - A) The creative (hook, message, offer)
    - B) The ad account name
    - C) The time zone
    - D) The number of hashtags
4. When can you upload a customer list for a custom audience?
    - A) Only for political ads
    - B) Never
    - C) Only if people agreed when you collected their details
    - D) Always

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** Meta Blueprint's audience courses and videos and the Digital Culture Network's audience guide (about 35 minutes)
- **Action:** plan an audience, a rupee budget and 2–3 creatives in a complete ad test plan. It is done when your proof is saved: your audience plan, budget plan, 2–3 creatives and the complete test plan.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **C.** Simple local targeting gives the system room to find the right people.
2. **B.** You are paying for messages that lead to customers.
3. **A.** Test different creatives, not tiny settings.
4. **C.** Consent is needed, as the Digital Culture Network's guide stresses.

sections.title: SMM-M09-L03: Retargeting, Click-to-WhatsApp, YouTube and Google ads, and ROI
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Plan a retargeting audience and a Click-to-WhatsApp ad, understand YouTube and Google ad formats, and calculate whether an ad made or lost money. **Time:** about 3 hours (40 minutes study, 2 hours 20 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Retargeting: talk to people who already know you

Retargeting means showing ads to people who have already interacted with you: watched your videos, engaged with your Instagram or Facebook, visited your website (tracked with the Meta Pixel) or are on a customer list they agreed to. They are warmer, so the message can be more direct: "Still thinking about that cake? Order by 6 pm." Vary the creative so the same people don't see one ad again and again.

### Click-to-WhatsApp ads

For many Kerala businesses the best ad sends people straight into a WhatsApp chat. WhatsApp's own business pages list **ads that click to WhatsApp** among the app's tools, and you can start them from the WhatsApp Business app or set WhatsApp as the destination in Ads Manager. Before you start:

- quick replies ready for price, delivery and payment
- labels for "From ad", "Ordered", "Not ordered"
- someone available to reply quickly during the ad's hours
- a keyword in the pre-filled message or CTA so you can count chats from the ad

### YouTube and Google ads in one page (as of October 2026)

Google's free **Skillshop** has learning paths and certifications for Search, Display, Video, Shopping and Measurement. The basics:

- **Skippable in-stream video ads:** viewers can skip after 5 seconds. With cost-per-view bidding you pay when someone watches 30 seconds (or the whole ad if shorter) or interacts.
- **Non-skippable in-stream:** up to 60 seconds; paid per thousand impressions.
- **Bumper ads:** non-skippable, about 6 seconds; paid per thousand impressions.
- **In-feed video ads:** a thumbnail and text inviting people to click and watch.
- **Shorts ads:** between Shorts; viewers can swipe past straight away.
- **Search ads** (Google Ads): text ads shown to people searching, for example "mobile display change Kuttiady". They catch people who already want something, which suits local services.

Google charges 18% GST on Google Ads purchases in India unless a valid GSTIN is given (check current rules).

### Did the ad make money?

Work it out every time:

- **Cost per result** = total cost (with GST) ÷ results
- **Conversion rate** = customers ÷ results (for example, orders ÷ chats)
- **Cost per customer** = total cost ÷ customers
- **ROAS** (return on ad spend) = revenue from the ad ÷ ad spend
- **Profit** = (revenue × margin) − total ad cost
- **ROI** = profit ÷ total ad cost × 100

The **break-even cost per customer** is the profit you make on one customer's purchase (or on their first few purchases if they usually come back). If an ad costs more than that per customer, it loses money, however many likes it gets.

## Local example

**Amma's Pickles** ran a Click-to-WhatsApp ad for 6 days (made-up numbers to show the method):

| Item | Number |
| --- | --- |
| Ad spend | ₹800 |
| GST at 18% (as shown on the bill) | ₹144 |
| Total cost | ₹944 |
| WhatsApp chats from the ad (keyword "PICKLE") | 46 |
| Orders | 12 |
| Average order | ₹300 |
| Revenue | ₹3,600 |
| Margin after ingredients, jars and delivery (40%) | ₹1,440 |
| Profit after the ad | ₹1,440 − ₹944 = ₹496 |
| Cost per chat / per customer | ₹21 / ₹79 |
| ROAS | ₹3,600 ÷ ₹800 = 4.5 |

The ad made a small profit on the first orders, and five of the twelve customers re-ordered within a month, so it was worth more than it first looked. They also learned that chats arriving after 9 pm rarely became orders, so they set the ad to run during the day.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [WhatsApp Business: the built-in business tools](https://whatsappbusiness.com/resources/resource-library/small-business-use-whatsapp-business-app/) | Re-read the "ads that click to WhatsApp" part | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Digital Culture Network: reaching your audience with Meta ads](https://digitalculturenetwork.org.uk/knowledge/reaching-your-audience-making-your-meta-ads-more-effective/) | Re-read the retargeting section | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Google Ads Help: About video ad formats](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2375464) | Read the video ad formats and how you pay for each | 15 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Google Skillshop: Free Google Ads training](https://skillshop.withgoogle.com/googleads/) | Browse the free learning paths; note the Video and Search ones for later | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Google Ads Help: Taxes in your country (India: GST)](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2375370) | Re-read the GST rules for India | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 35 minutes).
2. Write a retargeting plan for one business: who (video viewers, engagers, website visitors or customers with consent), what message, and how long.
3. Write a Click-to-WhatsApp ad plan: creative, keyword, quick replies, labels and reply hours.
4. Write one Google search ad idea for a local service: three short headlines and two descriptions, following Google's genuine copy advice.
5. Use the ROI calculator on your Peak Fitness, Amma's Pickles or own test numbers and write whether the ad made money.

**Proof to record:** Your retargeting plan, Click-to-WhatsApp plan, search ad idea and a completed ROI calculation with your conclusion.

## Template: ROI calculator

```
Ad spend (Rs)                     A = ______
GST and other charges (Rs)        B = ______
Total cost                        C = A + B = ______
Results (chats/leads)             R = ______
Customers                         N = ______
Revenue from those customers      V = ______
Margin %                          M = ______
Cost per result                   = C / R = ______
Conversion rate                   = N / R x 100 = ____%
Cost per customer                 = C / N = ______
ROAS                              = V / A = ______
Profit                            = V x M/100 - C = ______
ROI %                             = Profit / C x 100 = ____%
Break-even cost per customer      = profit on one
                                    customer's orders = ____
```

## Template: Click-to-WhatsApp checklist

```
[ ] Destination: WhatsApp (from the WhatsApp Business app
    or Ads Manager)
[ ] Pre-filled message or CTA keyword: "_____"
[ ] Quick replies: price, delivery, payment, order steps
[ ] Labels: From ad / Ordered / Not ordered
[ ] Someone replies within ___ minutes during ad hours
[ ] Ad runs only during hours you can reply
[ ] Count chats and orders daily in a sheet
```

## Common mistakes

- **Counting chats as sales.** Track how many chats became orders.
- **Running WhatsApp ads when nobody can reply.** Slow replies waste the money. Run ads during reply hours.
- **Ignoring GST and costs in ROI.** Use the total cost and the margin, not just revenue.
- **Showing one retargeting ad for weeks.** Change the creative to avoid tiring people.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. When can viewers skip a skippable in-stream YouTube ad?
    - A) Never
    - B) After 5 seconds
    - C) Immediately
    - D) After 30 seconds
2. An ad cost ₹944 in total and brought 12 customers. What was the cost per customer?
    - A) ₹944
    - B) ₹12
    - C) About ₹20
    - D) About ₹79
3. What is ROAS?
    - A) Profit after tax
    - B) Number of chats
    - C) Revenue from the ad divided by ad spend
    - D) Cost per thousand impressions
4. Who is a retargeting audience?
    - A) Competitors
    - B) People who already interacted with you, such as video viewers or website visitors
    - C) Only new customers
    - D) Random people in Kerala

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** WhatsApp's ad tools, retargeting, Google's video ad formats, Skillshop and GST rules (about 35 minutes)
- **Action:** plan a retargeting audience, a Click-to-WhatsApp ad and a search ad, and calculate an ad's ROI. It is done when your proof is saved: your retargeting plan, Click-to-WhatsApp plan, search ad idea and a completed ROI calculation with your conclusion.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **B.** Google's format guide says viewers can skip after 5 seconds.
2. **D.** ₹944 ÷ 12 is about ₹79.
3. **C.** Return on ad spend compares revenue with spend.
4. **B.** Retargeting reaches warmer people with a more direct message.

sections.title: Module 10: Influencer and creator marketing
sections.summary: Work with creators the right way, from both sides: as a marketer hiring local micro-influencers and using customer content, and as a creator who may earn from brand deals, affiliate links and platform programmes.
sections.content:
## Overview

Trusted voices sell better than ads. In two weeks you'll find and vet local creators, write briefs, use user-generated content with permission, and learn the real ways creators earn in India, with the disclosure rules that apply to all of them.

Your 90-day growth sprint begins at the end of this module (SMM-M17-L01), so you'll also plan your sprint in week 26.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Find and vet micro-influencers with real, local audiences
- Write a clear influencer brief with deliverables, claims and usage rights
- Use UGC only with permission and never as fake reviews
- Explain creator income options in India and their prerequisites
- Disclose paid, gifted and affiliate content correctly, and make a rate card

## Time

About 6 hours 30 minutes in total: 5 hours 30 minutes of lessons and 1 hour for the module project. Part-time: weeks 25–26.

## Lessons

1. SMM-M10-L01: Micro-influencers and UGC for local brands (about 3 hours)
2. SMM-M10-L02: Affiliate marketing and creator monetisation (about 2 hours 30 minutes)

## Module project: An influencer brief and your creator money plan

1. Finalise one influencer brief for a real local business, including disclosure instructions and usage rights.
2. Finalise your own creator money plan and rate card v1.
3. Put your disclosure snippets in your template library.
4. If you did a barter collaboration, add its results and what you would change.

**Proof to record:** Your final influencer brief, money plan, rate card and disclosure snippets in 10 Influencers.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3. If a row is a 1, redo that part first.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Finding and vetting | Picks by follower count | Some checks | Checks location, engagement, growth, fit and disclosure habits |
| Briefing | Verbal only | Partial brief | Complete brief with message, claims, deliverables, rights and payment |
| UGC | Reposts without asking | Asks sometimes | Always asks, credits and keeps permission |
| Monetisation | Unclear | Lists options | A money plan with prerequisites and a rate card based on own numbers |
| Disclosure | Hidden or missing | Sometimes labelled | Correct labels for paid, gifted and affiliate content, every time |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, when PSC prep or work leaves little time:

- Vet one creator with the checklist.
- Write a half-page brief.
- Write your money plan with two streams.
- Save the disclosure snippets.

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, read the front, say the answer, then check. Repeat the ones you missed the next day.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| Why micro-influencers for local shops? | Small but engaged, local, trusted audiences give better value. |
| Five vetting checks? | Local audience, real engagement, growth pattern, fit and values, disclosure habits. |
| Four deal types? | Barter, paid fee, commission, discount code. |
| What are usage rights? | Whether and how the brand may reuse the creator's content, for example as ads. |
| ASCI labels for material connections? | Ad, Sponsored, Collaboration, Partnership, Employee, Free gift, Affiliate. |
| Maximum Amazon.in Associates fee? | Up to 10%, varying by category (check current rates). |
| YouTube Shopping affiliate partners in India at launch (Oct 2024)? | Flipkart and Myntra. |
| Which creator income usually comes first? | Local services and sponsorships. |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Treating influencer posts as ads without labels.** Every material connection needs a clear label.
- **Paying before vetting.** Check the audience first; ask for Insights screenshots.
- **Building income on one platform's programme.** Programmes change; keep several streams.

sections.title: SMM-M10-L01: Micro-influencers and UGC for local brands
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Find and vet local creators with real audiences, brief them well, agree fair terms, and make sure every partnership and piece of user-generated content is disclosed and used with permission. **Time:** about 3 hours (50 minutes study, 2 hours 10 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Why micro-influencers suit local businesses

A celebrity reaches millions who will never visit a shop in Kuttiady. A local food page, a college page or a community admin with a few thousand followers reaches the right people, who trust them like a friend's recommendation. For small budgets, **micro-influencers** (creators with small but engaged, often local audiences) usually give better value than big names.

### Finding creators

- Search your area's place names and hashtags on Instagram and YouTube, and note who appears again and again.
- Ask customers which local pages they follow.
- Look at who local businesses already collaborate with (and whether those posts are disclosed).
- **Instagram's Creator Marketplace**, launched in India in February 2024, lets brands find creators through Meta Business Suite; access and features vary (as of October 2026).

### Vetting: is the audience real and right?

Before you offer anything, check:

| Check | How | Red flag |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Local audience** | Ask for screenshots of Insights: top towns and cities, age ranges | Most followers outside Kerala for a local shop |
| **Real engagement** | Read comments on recent posts; compare views with follower count | Comments like "nice 🔥" from random accounts; tiny views for huge followings |
| **Growth pattern** | Ask how they grew; look at older posts | Sudden jumps in followers with no viral post |
| **Fit and values** | Watch 10 recent posts | Content that clashes with the brand, or hateful or risky posts |
| **Disclosure habits** | Look for "Ad", "Collaboration" or Paid partnership labels on past sponsored posts | Obvious sponsored posts with no label |

### Deal types

- **Barter:** a free product, meal or stay in exchange for content
- **Paid fee:** a fixed price for agreed posts
- **Commission:** a percentage of sales through a code or link
- **Discount code:** followers get a discount; you can count the orders

Ask for the creator's rate card and decide from expected results: compare the price with what reaching the same people with ads would cost (Module 9). Start with one small, clear deliverable.

### A good brief

A brief prevents disappointment on both sides: the goal, the key message, must-include details (price, location, timing, disclosure), claims the creator must not make, deliverables (for example 1 Reel and 3 Stories), dates, who approves what, whether the brand may reuse the content in ads (usage rights, often for an extra fee), and payment terms.

### Disclosure is not optional

Under ASCI's guidelines a **material connection** (payment, free products even if unsolicited, discounts, gifts, trips, barters, family or work ties) must be disclosed with a clear label such as **Ad, Sponsored, Collaboration, Partnership, Free gift** or **Affiliate**, placed where the audience can't miss it: at the start of the caption, superimposed on Stories and images without text, and on screen for a set time in videos. Platform tools such as Instagram's **Paid partnership** label are used as well. The government's "Endorsement Know-hows!" guide adds that endorsers shouldn't promote products they haven't personally used or vetted. Module 14 covers the full rules.

### UGC: content made by customers and creators

**User-generated content (UGC)** means content made by customers or creators rather than the brand: a customer's photo of their birthday cake, or a video a creator makes for the brand to use in its own ads.

- **Customers' posts:** ask before you repost, credit them, and keep the permission (a screenshot of their "yes").
- **Creator-made UGC for ads:** agree in writing how and where the brand may use it, for how long, and the fee.
- **UGC is not fake reviews.** Never ask people to pretend to be customers.

## Local example

**Kakkayam Hills Homestay** wanted more monsoon weekend bookings. They shortlisted five travel creators from Kozhikode and vetted three:

| Creator (made up) | Followers | Average Reel views | Top city in Insights | Disclosure habit | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| @malabar.trails | 18,000 | 9,000 | Kozhikode | Labels "Collaboration" | ✅ Invite |
| @kerala.wanderer | 120,000 | 4,000 | Outside Kerala | No labels on obvious ads | ❌ |
| @weekend.kozhikode | 6,500 | 5,500 | Kozhikode | Labels "Free stay" | ✅ Invite |

They offered each a free one-night stay (barter) with a brief: show the balcony mist, the breakfast and the trek path, state the price (₹2,500 a night for two), tag the location, start the caption with "Collaboration (free stay)" and use Instagram's Paid partnership label; no claims like "safest trek in Kerala". The homestay could reshare the Reels on its own page with credit, but not use them as paid ads without asking.

Results over three weeks: 31 WhatsApp enquiries mentioning the creators, 9 bookings.

(Made-up example to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [ASCI: Guidelines for influencer advertising in digital media (PDF)](https://www.ascionline.in/social/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/ASCI-Influencer-Guidelines.pdf) | Read the definitions, the list of labels and the placement rules for each format | 20 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |
| [ASCI: influencer advertising FAQs](https://www.ascionline.in/social/faqs/) | Re-read the FAQs on barters and free products | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |
| [PIB: Endorsement guidelines for celebrities and influencers (January 2023)](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1892527&reg=48&lang=2) | Read the government's summary of the endorsement guide | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |
| [MediaNama: Instagram Creator Marketplace launches in India (February 2024)](https://www.medianama.com/2024/02/223-instagram-creator-marketplace-india-2/) | Read what Instagram's Creator Marketplace offers in India | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Instagram for Creators: Best practices hub](https://creators.instagram.com/best-practices) | In "Monetize", look at Partnership Ads and Creator Marketplace from the creator's side | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 50 minutes).
2. Choose a local business (real or the one you'll pilot in Module 11) and shortlist 5 local creators who could suit it.
3. Vet 3 of them with the checklist, using public posts and, if you contact them, Insights screenshots they choose to share.
4. Write a complete influencer brief for one of them.
5. Write a permission message for reposting a customer's post (UGC), in Malayalam and English.
6. Optional: carry out one small barter collaboration with correct disclosure and log the results.

**Proof to record:** Your shortlist, three vetting sheets, the influencer brief and the UGC permission message (plus the collaboration post link if you did one).

## Template: creator vetting checklist

```
CREATOR: @________  Platform: ______  Date: ____
Followers: ____  Avg views (last 9 posts): ____
Views / followers: ____%
Top towns (Insights screenshot): __________
Age ranges: __________
Comments: real conversations / generic / bots
Follower jumps without a reason? Y / N
Content fit with the brand (1-5): ___
Values or risk concerns: __________
Discloses past sponsorships? Y / N
Decision: invite / maybe / no   Reason: ______
```

## Template: influencer brief

```
BRAND: ______________  CREATOR: @____________
GOAL: ______________ (e.g. weekend booking enquiries)
KEY MESSAGE (one line): __________________________
MUST INCLUDE: price ____ / location tag / timing ____
DISCLOSURE: caption starts "Collaboration" / "Free
  gift" / "Ad"; label on screen in videos; Paid
  partnership tool switched on
DO NOT CLAIM: ___________________________________
DELIVERABLES: __ Reel(s), __ Stories, by ____ (date)
APPROVAL: brand sees the draft ___ days before posting
USAGE RIGHTS: reshare with credit Y/N; use as paid ad
  Y/N (fee: ____, for ___ months)
PAYMENT: barter (what) / fee Rs ____ / commission __%,
  paid within ___ days of posting
CONTACT: ______________
```

## Template: UGC permission message

```
EN: Hi [name]! We loved your photo of [product]. Could we
share it on our page with credit to you? Reply YES if
that's okay. Thank you! 🙏
ML: നമസ്കാരം [പേര്]! [product]-ന്റെ നിങ്ങളുടെ ഫോട്ടോ ഞങ്ങൾക്ക് വളരെ
ഇഷ്ടമായി. നിങ്ങളുടെ പേര് സഹിതം ഞങ്ങളുടെ പേജിൽ ഷെയർ ചെയ്യട്ടെ?
സമ്മതമാണെങ്കിൽ YES എന്ന് മറുപടി തരൂ. നന്ദി! 🙏
(Save a screenshot of their reply.)
```

## Common mistakes

- **Choosing by follower count.** Check views, comments and where the audience lives.
- **No written brief.** Misunderstandings about claims, dates and rights are common. Write it down.
- **Undisclosed barters.** A free stay or meal is a material connection; it must be labelled.
- **Reposting customers without asking.** Ask, credit and keep the permission.
- **Using creator videos as ads without agreement.** Agree usage rights and any fee first.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. Which creator is the best fit for a Kuttiady shop?
    - A) 6,500 followers, mostly Kozhikode, real comments and labelled sponsorships
    - B) A page that never shows its audience
    - C) 120,000 followers, mostly outside Kerala
    - D) Anyone with a blue tick
2. A creator gets a free night at a homestay. What does ASCI expect?
    - A) A label in the bio only
    - B) A label at the end of a long caption
    - C) A clear label such as "Collaboration" or "Free gift" where the audience can't miss it
    - D) No label, since no money changed hands
3. Before reposting a customer's photo, you should:
    - A) Just repost it
    - B) Edit it to look like your own
    - C) Ask permission, credit them and keep their reply
    - D) Remove their name
4. What does "usage rights" in a brief decide?
    - A) The creator's password
    - B) The posting time
    - C) The number of hashtags
    - D) Whether and how the brand may reuse the creator's content, for example in ads

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** ASCI's influencer guidelines and FAQs, the government endorsement guide and Instagram's creator tools (about 50 minutes)
- **Action:** shortlist and vet local creators, write an influencer brief and a UGC permission message. It is done when your proof is saved: your shortlist, three vetting sheets, the influencer brief and the UGC permission message (plus the collaboration post link if you did one).
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **A.** A real, local, engaged audience and good disclosure habits matter most.
2. **C.** Free products and stays are material connections; labels must be upfront.
3. **C.** It is their content.
4. **D.** Reusing content as ads needs agreement and often a fee.
