sections.title: SMM-M12-L02: Portfolio and case studies with before/after numbers
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Write clear, honest case studies with before and after numbers, and publish a simple portfolio site on Google Sites that a shop owner can read on a phone in two minutes. **Time:** about 2 hours 30 minutes (25 minutes study, 2 hours 5 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### What a client wants to see

A shop owner looking at your portfolio asks: "Have you helped someone like me? What changed? How do you work? What will it cost?" Your portfolio answers the first three with **case studies**; Module 15 adds your services and prices.

### The case study structure

| Part | What to write |
| --- | --- |
| **Title with the result** | "Phone shop doubles weekly enquiries in 4 weeks" |
| **Client and context** | Who they are, where, what they sell (with permission, or described generally) |
| **The challenge** | What wasn't working, in their words if possible |
| **Goal and baseline** | The KPI and the "before" number, with dates |
| **What you did** | 4–6 steps, plainly |
| **Results** | A before-and-after table, plus 2–3 screenshots |
| **What you learned** | One or two honest lessons, including what didn't work |
| **Testimonial** | Two lines from the client, with permission |

Keep a **one-page version** for WhatsApp and a longer one for the site.

### Honest numbers only

- Use the real numbers from your logs and screenshots.
- Say what you can connect to your work and what you can't ("enquiries also rose during the festival season").
- Separate paid and organic results.
- Get written permission to use a client's name, numbers and screenshots; if they prefer, describe them generally and blur names.
- Never invent results, round them up or borrow someone else's case study. Clients and employers check, and one fake number ruins your reputation.

### Your three case studies

1. **Your 30-day challenge** (Module 8): your own account, before and after.
2. **The pilot** (Module 11): a real business.
3. **Your 90-day growth project** (Module 17): your account over three months.

### A portfolio site on Google Sites

Google Sites is free with a Google account and easy on the laptop. Keep it simple and mobile-friendly:

- **Home:** your one-line promise, a photo, two headline results, and a WhatsApp button.
- **Case studies:** one card per case study, linking to the full page.
- **Services:** a placeholder until Module 15.
- **About:** your story in five lines, and where you work.
- **Contact:** WhatsApp click-to-chat link, email, LinkedIn.

Connect Google Analytics (SMM-M08-L02) and use UTM links in your bios so you know where visitors come from. Also export a short PDF version in Canva to send on WhatsApp.

## Local example

Anu's case study 1, in short (made-up numbers to show the method):

> **A new local page: 4× views and 2× followers in 30 days**
> **Context:** @kuttiady.diaries, a hyperlocal page started in week 0 of a course.
> **Challenge:** posts reached mostly friends; average 310 views.
> **Goal:** become the page local people share. KPIs: views per post, shares per 1,000 views.
> **What I did:** posted daily for 30 days; tested question hooks, video length and posting time; started a "Shop story" series; one Collab a week.
> **Results:**
>
> | | Before (October) | After (30 days) |
> | --- | --- | --- |
> | Average 7-day views | 310 | 1,150 |
> | Shares per 1,000 views | 6 | 13 |
> | Followers | 820 | 1,640 |
>
> **Learned:** people stories beat text updates (19 vs 3 shares per 1,000); posting time mattered less than replies.

Her site: Home, Case studies (the challenge, plus "Pilot: phone shop, results coming in week 32"), Services (coming soon), About, Contact.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Sites Help: How to use Google Sites](https://support.google.com/sites/answer/6372878) | Read how to create and publish a site | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Sites Help: Use Analytics with your site](https://support.google.com/sites/answer/97459) | Re-read how to connect Analytics | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Canva Design School: Graphic design essentials](https://www.canva.com/design-school/courses/graphic-design-essentials/) | Re-watch the lessons on principles of design for your layout | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Analytics Help: URL builders (collect campaign data with UTM links)](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/10917952) | Re-read the UTM rules for your bio links | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 25 minutes).
2. Rewrite case study 1 (your 30-day challenge) in the template: one-page and long versions.
3. Ask your pilot client for written permission to use their name, numbers and screenshots, and create a placeholder card for case study 2.
4. Build your Google Sites portfolio with Home, Case studies, Services (placeholder), About and Contact. Check it on your phone.
5. Connect GA4, and put UTM-tagged links to the site in your Instagram bio, LinkedIn and WhatsApp profile.

**Proof to record:** Case study 1 (both versions), the permission message to your pilot client, and the link to your published portfolio site.

## Template: case study template

```
TITLE: [result] for [kind of client] in [time]
CLIENT: ______ (named with permission / described)
CHALLENGE: ______________________________
GOAL AND KPI: ___________  BASELINE (date): ______
WHAT I DID:
  1. ______ 2. ______ 3. ______ 4. ______
RESULTS:
  Metric        | Before | After | Change
  ____________  | ____   | ____  | ____
  ____________  | ____   | ____  | ____
  (screenshots 1-3; paid shown separately)
WHAT I LEARNED: ______  WHAT DIDN'T WORK: ______
TESTIMONIAL (with permission): "______" - name, business
CAVEATS: ______ (season, small sample, other factors)
```

## Template: permission to use results (English and Malayalam)

```
EN: Hi [name], thank you for the pilot! May I use the
results (numbers and screenshots) as a case study on my
portfolio and LinkedIn? I can name [business] or just
say "a phone shop in Kozhikode district", whichever you
prefer. Reply YES (named) or YES (unnamed).
ML: നമസ്കാരം [പേര്], പൈലറ്റിന് നന്ദി! ഫലങ്ങൾ (നമ്പറുകളും സ്ക്രീൻഷോട്ടുകളും)
എന്റെ പോർട്ട്‌ഫോളിയോയിലും ലിങ്ക്ഡ്ഇനിലും കേസ് സ്റ്റഡിയായി ഉപയോഗിക്കട്ടെ?
[ബിസിനസ്] പേര് പറയാം, അല്ലെങ്കിൽ "കോഴിക്കോട് ജില്ലയിലെ ഒരു മൊബൈൽ ഷോപ്പ്"
എന്ന് മാത്രം പറയാം. YES (പേരോടെ) / YES (പേരില്ലാതെ) എന്ന് മറുപടി തരൂ.
```

## Template: portfolio site structure

```
HOME: one-line promise / photo / 2 headline results /
      WhatsApp button
CASE STUDIES: cards -> full pages (1, 2, 3)
SERVICES: packages and price sheet (Module 15)
ABOUT: 5 lines: who, where, how you work
CONTACT: WhatsApp click-to-chat, email, LinkedIn
CHECKS: loads on a phone / GA4 connected / UTM links
  in bios / no client data without permission
```

## Common mistakes

- **Results without a baseline.** "10,000 views" means nothing without the before.
- **Mixing paid and organic.** Show them separately.
- **Long, text-heavy pages.** A table, a few screenshots and short paragraphs.
- **Using client data without permission.** Ask in writing, or describe them generally.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. What makes a case study convincing?
    - A) Stock photos
    - B) Lots of hashtags
    - C) Big claims
    - D) A clear baseline, real before-and-after numbers, the steps and honest caveats
2. A pilot client prefers not to be named. What do you do?
    - A) Describe them generally and blur names in screenshots
    - B) Invent a different client
    - C) Drop the case study
    - D) Name them anyway
3. What should your portfolio site's Home page include?
    - A) A long list of tools
    - B) Your promise, two headline results and a WhatsApp button
    - C) Your full life story
    - D) Only your logo

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** Google Sites, Analytics on Sites, Canva's design principles and UTM rules (about 25 minutes)
- **Action:** write case study 1, ask for permission for case study 2 and publish your portfolio site. It is done when your proof is saved: case study 1 (both versions), the permission message to your pilot client, and the link to your published portfolio site.
- **Quiz:** at least 2 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **D.** Specific, checkable evidence persuades.
2. **A.** Respect their wish and keep the evidence honest.
3. **B.** Visitors decide in seconds; make the next step easy.

Action: write case study 1, ask for permission for case study 2 and publish your portfolio site

sections.title: Module 13: AI for social media
sections.summary: Use AI to work faster on ideas, scripts, captions, visuals, editing and analysis, while protecting accuracy, originality, privacy and honesty, and following the labelling rules of YouTube, Meta and India.
sections.content:
## Overview

AI can halve the time a post takes, or flood your account with generic, wrong or misleading content. In two weeks you'll build reusable prompts that carry your strategy and voice, check every AI output, use AI for visuals and editing within clear limits, and learn exactly when AI content must be labelled.

The module project is your AI playbook: the prompts, checks and rules you'll use with clients.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Write prompts that include role, context, task, constraints, examples and an honesty instruction
- Catch made-up facts, awkward Malayalam and generic phrases in AI drafts
- Use AI for images, video editing and analysis without misleading anyone
- Apply YouTube's, Meta's and India's AI labelling rules
- Explain why mass-produced AI content doesn't pay

## Time

About 5 hours 30 minutes in total: 5 hours of lessons and 30 minutes for the module project. Part-time: weeks 33–34.

## Lessons

1. SMM-M13-L01: AI for ideas, research, scripts and captions (about 3 hours)
2. SMM-M13-L02: AI for images, video and analytics: risks and labels (about 2 hours)

## Module project: Your AI playbook

1. Put your 5 prompts, the AI output check, the disclosure decision tree and the risk checklist in one document.
2. Add your time-saved and errors-caught log from SMM-M13-L01.
3. Add 3 AI-assisted posts as examples, with what you changed.
4. Write a short "AI policy for clients": what you use AI for, what you never do, and how you label.

**Proof to record:** Your AI playbook document in 13 AI.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3. If a row is a 1, redo that part first.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Prompts | One-line requests | Some context | Reusable prompts with role, context, constraints, examples and honesty |
| Checking | Posts AI output unedited | Checks some facts | Checks every fact, Malayalam and claim; logs errors |
| Visuals and video | Misleading or misspelled visuals | Some good uses | Realistic, honest visuals with own text; useful edits |
| Labels | Unaware of rules | Knows YouTube's rule | Applies YouTube, Meta and Indian rules with a decision tree |
| Privacy and quality | Pastes private data; template content | Some care | No private data; every piece adds something real |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, when PSC prep or work leaves little time:

- Write 2 prompts (hooks and captions) and use them for 3 posts.
- Do the decision tree for one AI-assisted piece.
- Write a five-line AI policy for clients.

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, read the front, say the answer, then check. Repeat the ones you missed the next day.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| Six parts of a good prompt? | Role, context, task, constraints, examples, honesty instruction. |
| What does AI do worst for local marketing? | Local, current facts such as prices, timings and names. |
| Does YouTube need AI disclosure for script help or beauty filters? | No. |
| What does YouTube need disclosed? | Realistic altered or synthetic content, such as real people saying things they didn't. |
| Meta's label for AI content? | "AI info". |
| Since when are India's 2026 AI-content labelling rules in force? | 20 February 2026. |
| Are routine edits "synthetic content" under India's rules? | No: routine editing, formatting and technical correction are exempt. |
| What does YouTube not monetise (clarified July 2025)? | Inauthentic, mass-produced or repetitive content. |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Using AI to fake proof.** Never generate testimonials, results or product images that aren't real.
- **Relying on one AI tool's answer about rules.** Check the official help page; rules change.
- **Replacing your voice.** AI drafts; you decide and write the final version.

tasks.detail: **Proof to record:** Your AI playbook document in 13 AI.

sections.title: SMM-M13-L01: AI for ideas, research, scripts and captions
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Use free AI assistants to brainstorm, draft, rewrite and summarise faster, with prompts that carry your strategy and voice, while catching made-up facts, generic writing and privacy risks. **Time:** about 3 hours (30 minutes study, 2 hours 30 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### What AI is good and bad at, for social media

| Good at | Bad at |
| --- | --- |
| Brainstorming many angles and hooks in seconds | Facts: it can state wrong things confidently ("hallucinations") |
| First drafts of scripts, captions and outlines | Current platform rules, limits and features |
| Rewriting for a platform, length or tone | Local knowledge: prices, timings, who runs which shop |
| Turning a long piece into several short ones | Natural Malayalam and local expressions (check every line) |
| Summarising 200 comments into themes | Originality: drafts often sound like everyone else's |
| Checklists and report structures | Legal, tax or medical advice |

The free plans of Gemini, ChatGPT and Claude are enough for this work (as of October 2026; limits change, check current rules). The Free AI Generalist Course in this app teaches prompting in depth (Level 1).

### Your strategy goes in; AI drafts come out

AI is a fast assistant, not the strategist. A good workflow:

1. **You decide** the goal, audience, pillar and message (Modules 2 and 5).
2. **AI drafts options:** 20 hooks, 3 script versions, 5 caption variants.
3. **You choose** the best and **add real details**: the owner's words, true prices, your own observations.
4. **You check every fact** against a real source or the business owner.
5. **You edit to your voice** using your voice chart, and read it aloud.

Meta's advice to Facebook creators in July 2025 was to write high-quality captions rather than relying on unedited automated AI captions; the same applies everywhere.

### A prompt pattern that works

Give the assistant what a new team member would need:

- **Role:** "You are a social media copywriter for small businesses in Kerala."
- **Context:** the business, the audience (your persona), your voice chart and language rules.
- **Task:** "Write 10 hooks for a 30-second Reel about ..."
- **Constraints:** length, language, "no hype or superlatives", "at most five hashtags", "no health claims".
- **Examples:** two of your best past captions.
- **Honesty:** "Ask me questions if anything is unclear. Mark any fact you're not sure about with [CHECK]."

### Summarising comments and reviews

Paste comments (with names and numbers removed) and ask: "Group these into themes, count each, and quote one example per theme." It turns an hour of reading into minutes. Check a few by hand to make sure it didn't invent themes.

### Privacy

Never paste customers' phone numbers, private chats, payment details or a client's confidential plans into an AI tool, and check each tool's privacy settings. Remove names before you ask for summaries.

### Avoid "AI sameness"

AI drafts tend to use the same phrases ("Unlock the secret...", "Elevate your..."). Delete them. Your local knowledge, real photos and the owner's own words are what make posts work; AI can't supply those.

## Local example

Anu used a free AI assistant to prepare a "Shop story" Reel about a tailoring shop:

- **Prompt:** her role, the page's voice chart, the persona, "write 15 hooks for a 40-second Reel about a tailor who has worked on the same street for decades; Malayalam and English; no exaggeration; mark facts to check with [CHECK]".
- **Output:** 15 hooks in about 20 seconds. Three were good; one said "since 1950 [CHECK]".
- **Her edit:** the owner told her he started in 1987, so she wrote "Same street, same machine, since 1987". She rewrote the Malayalam hook herself because the AI's version used an unnatural word.
- **Caption:** she asked for "a 3-line caption in my voice chart, first line with 'Kuttiady tailor'", then changed two lines to the tailor's own words.

Time: 25 minutes instead of about an hour. Errors caught: one wrong date, one awkward Malayalam phrase, one cliché ("timeless craftsmanship").

(Made-up example to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Google Gemini plans (has a free plan)](https://gemini.google/subscriptions/) | Check what the free plan includes | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |
| [ChatGPT plans (has a free plan)](https://chatgpt.com/pricing) | Check what the free plan includes | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |
| [Claude plans (has a free plan)](https://claude.com/pricing) | Check what the free plan includes | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |
| [TechCrunch: Meta cracks down on unoriginal Facebook content (July 2025)](https://techcrunch.com/2025/07/14/following-youtube-meta-announces-crackdown-on-unoriginal-facebook-content) | Re-read Meta's advice on authentic storytelling and AI captions | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 20 minutes) and choose one free assistant to use this week.
2. Write 5 reusable prompts with the pattern above: hooks, a short-video script, a caption rewrite for each platform, a comment or review summary, and a repurposing plan.
3. Use them to prepare one week of posts for your sprint or your pilot client.
4. For every AI draft, log the time it took, what you changed and every error you caught (wrong facts, awkward Malayalam, clichés).
5. Publish the posts and note in the Posting Log which ones were AI-assisted.

**Proof to record:** Your 5 prompts, the log of time saved and errors caught, and links to the published AI-assisted posts.

## Template: prompt template

```
ROLE: You are a social media copywriter for small
businesses in Kerala.
CONTEXT: Business: ______ in ______. Audience: ______
(persona). Voice: ______ (paste voice chart).
Language rules: ______.
TASK: Write ______ (e.g. 10 hooks / a 30-second script /
a 3-line caption) about ______.
CONSTRAINTS: max ___ words; English and Malayalam;
no hype or superlatives; no health or money promises;
max 5 hashtags; one call to action: ______.
EXAMPLES OF MY STYLE: "______" / "______"
HONESTY: Ask me questions if unclear. Mark any fact you
are not sure about with [CHECK]. Do not invent prices,
dates, names or reviews.
```

## Template: AI output check

```
[ ] Every fact checked with the owner or a real source
[ ] No invented prices, dates, names, reviews or results
[ ] Malayalam read aloud by me (or a native speaker)
[ ] Clichés removed ("unlock", "elevate", "game-changer")
[ ] Real local details and the owner's own words added
[ ] Fits my voice chart and the platform's format
[ ] No private data was pasted into the tool
[ ] Claims pass the honest persuasion check (SMM-M05-L02)
```

## Common mistakes

- **Posting AI drafts unedited.** They sound generic and may be wrong. Edit every line.
- **Trusting AI on platform rules.** Check official help pages; AI can be out of date.
- **Pasting private customer data.** Remove names and numbers first.
- **Letting AI decide strategy.** You set the goal, audience and message; AI drafts options.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. An AI draft says a shop opened "in 1950". What should you do?
    - A) Remove the shop's name
    - B) Post it
    - C) Ask the AI if it's sure and post anyway
    - D) Check the real date with the owner before posting
2. Which job is AI weakest at?
    - A) Rewriting a caption shorter
    - B) Knowing a local shop's real prices and timings
    - C) Brainstorming 20 hooks
    - D) Grouping comments into themes
3. What should you remove before asking AI to summarise customer comments?
    - A) Nothing
    - B) Emojis
    - C) Positive comments
    - D) Names, phone numbers and other personal details
4. What makes AI-assisted posts stand out from everyone else's?
    - A) More hashtags
    - B) Your real local details, photos and the owner's own words
    - C) Longer captions
    - D) More AI phrases

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** The free AI plans and Meta's advice on authentic captions (about 20 minutes)
- **Action:** write 5 reusable prompts, use them for a week of posts and log time saved and errors caught. It is done when your proof is saved: your 5 prompts, the log of time saved and errors caught, and links to the published AI-assisted posts.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **D.** AI can invent facts; confirm with a real source.
2. **B.** Local, current facts must come from the business or a real source.
3. **D.** Protect customers' privacy.
4. **B.** AI can't supply your local knowledge or proof.

sections.title: SMM-M13-L02: AI for images, video and analytics: risks and labels
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Use AI tools for visuals, editing and analysis without misleading anyone, know when YouTube, Meta and Indian rules require AI content to be labelled, and keep AI-made content worth watching. **Time:** about 2 hours (40 minutes study, 1 hour 20 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Where AI helps with visuals, video and numbers

- **Images:** backgrounds for thumbnails and covers, simple illustrations, mock-ups, removing a distracting object from your own photo. The free Gemini plan lists image generation and editing; ChatGPT's free plan lists limited image creation (as of October 2026).
- **Video:** auto-captions, cutting silences, voice clean-up, reframing for vertical. YouTube's Shorts tools include AI features such as effects and photo-to-video, and YouTube Create has AI editing features in some countries.
- **Analysis:** paste your Posting Log numbers (no personal data) and ask for patterns, then check the maths yourself; draft report wording.

The Free AI Generalist Course covers AI images, video and voice in Level 3.

### Where AI misleads

The line is **realistic content that makes people believe something false**:

- A "product photo" generated by AI that doesn't show the real product
- Adding a waterfall, a bigger room or a crowd that wasn't there
- A real person shown saying or doing something they didn't
- A fake "customer" testimonial video

Routine edits (brightness, removing a stray wire from a photo of the real place) are fine. Inventing what the customer will get is a misleading ad (SMM-M05-L02), whatever tool made it.

### Labels and disclosure (as of October 2026)

- **YouTube** requires creators to disclose content that is **meaningfully altered or synthetically generated and looks realistic**: making a real person appear to say or do something they didn't, altering footage of real events or places, or realistic AI scenes. You don't need to disclose clearly unrealistic content, beauty filters, or using AI for scripts, outlines, thumbnails, titles or captions. You disclose in YouTube Studio (the "AI use" choice when uploading). Creators who repeatedly don't disclose may have a label added and face penalties such as content removal or suspension from the Partner Program.
- **Meta** adds "AI info" labels to images, video and audio when it detects industry AI signals or when people self-disclose, with a more prominent label for high-risk content that could deceive the public.
- **India:** the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2026, in force since 20 February 2026, require AI-generated or altered content that appears real ("synthetically generated information") to be clearly labelled, and social media platforms must ask users to declare such content before it is published. Routine editing, formatting and technical correction are not treated as synthetic content. Deepfakes that misrepresent real people or events, and non-consensual intimate imagery, are prohibited (check current rules).

When in doubt, disclose. A one-line label costs nothing; a deceived audience costs your reputation.

### AI-made content still has to be worth watching

YouTube says videos made with AI can be recommended as broadly as other videos, but its monetisation policies don't pay for **inauthentic content**: mass-produced, template-like or repetitive videos, a policy it clarified in July 2025. Use AI to make your own ideas faster, not to flood platforms with sameness.

### Other risks

- **Text in AI images** is often misspelled, especially Malayalam. Add text yourself in Canva.
- **Music and voices:** check the licence of any AI music or voice tool before using it in a client's ad.
- **Over-automated replies:** customers notice robotic answers. Use templates, but reply as a person.

## Local example

**Kakkayam Hills Homestay** tried three AI uses (made-up example):

| Use | Decision | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Remove a power line from a real sunrise photo taken on the balcony | ✅ Fine | Routine edit; the view is real |
| Generate a "waterfall view" image for the room page | ❌ Dropped | There is no waterfall; it would mislead guests |
| AI voice-over in English for a real room-tour video | ✅ With a note | The footage is real; they added "Voice-over made with AI" in the description and ticked YouTube's AI disclosure because the voice sounded like a real person |

They also asked an assistant to summarise 60 Google reviews (names removed): the top themes were "breakfast", "quiet" and "steep road at night". They added a "how to reach us after dark" Highlight.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [YouTube Help: Disclosing use of altered or synthetic content](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/14328491) | Read what needs disclosure, what doesn't, and how to disclose | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |
| [Meta: Our approach to labeling AI-generated content](https://about.fb.com/news/2024/04/metas-approach-to-labeling-ai-generated-content-and-manipulated-media/) | Read how Meta labels AI content, including the updates | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |
| [Business Today: Government notifies rules on AI-generated content (February 2026)](https://www.businesstoday.in/amp/technology/story/govt-tightens-rules-on-ai-generated-content-mandates-labels-and-faster-takedowns-515505-2026-02-10) | Read what the 2026 rules require for AI content | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |
| [YouTube Help: Channel monetization policies (inauthentic and reused content)](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/1311392) | Read the section on inauthentic and reused content | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |
| [YouTube Creators: Shorts (how to record, add sound, edit and upload)](https://www.youtube.com/creators/create/shorts/) | Look at the AI tools listed for Shorts | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 45 minutes).
2. Make 2 AI-assisted visuals for your sprint or pilot (for example a thumbnail background and an illustration), adding all text yourself in Canva.
3. Do 1 AI-assisted video edit (captions, silence cutting or voice clean-up) and compare the time with editing by hand.
4. For each piece, decide with the decision tree whether a label is needed, and apply it.
5. Write your AI disclosure rules for yourself and your clients.

**Proof to record:** The 3 AI-assisted pieces (links or files), your decision-tree notes for each, and your written AI disclosure rules.

## Template: AI disclosure decision tree

```
1. Does it look realistic (photo, video, audio, voice)?
   NO  -> no AI label needed (e.g. a cartoon)
   YES -> go to 2
2. Is it only routine editing of real content?
   (brightness, colour, cropping, removing a stray wire,
   captions, script help)
   YES -> no label needed
   NO  -> go to 3
3. Could viewers believe something false about a real
   person, place, event or product?
   YES -> don't post it (or remake it with real content)
   NO, but AI made or changed realistic parts
       -> LABEL IT: YouTube "AI use: Yes"; a clear line such
          as "Made with AI" / "AI-ലൂടെ നിർമ്മിച്ചത്"; accept the
          platform's AI label
When unsure: label it.
```

## Template: AI risk checklist

```
[ ] Nothing shows a product, place or result that isn't real
[ ] No real person shown saying or doing something they didn't
[ ] Text in images added by me (no AI spelling errors)
[ ] AI music or voice licence checked for this use
[ ] Labels applied where the decision tree says so
[ ] Not mass-produced: each piece adds something real
[ ] Numbers from AI analysis re-checked by hand
[ ] No personal data pasted into AI tools
```

## Common mistakes

- **AI "product photos".** Customers expect what they see. Use real photos of the real product.
- **Skipping disclosure because it's "just a voice".** A realistic AI voice can need a label. When unsure, label it.
- **Flooding a channel with template videos.** YouTube doesn't monetise inauthentic, mass-produced content.
- **Trusting AI maths.** Check every calculation in your report.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. According to YouTube Help, which of these needs AI disclosure?
    - A) Making a real person appear to say something they didn't
    - B) A beauty filter
    - C) AI-generated captions
    - D) Using AI to write the script
2. Under India's 2026 IT rule amendments, what must happen to AI content that appears real?
    - A) It must be deleted
    - B) It must be clearly labelled as synthetically generated
    - C) Nothing
    - D) It must be in English
3. A homestay wants an AI image of a waterfall near the rooms, but there isn't one. What do you advise?
    - A) Post it with nice music
    - B) Don't post it: it would mislead guests
    - C) Post it only on WhatsApp
    - D) Post it without a label
4. What did YouTube clarify in July 2025?
    - A) AI videos are banned
    - B) Captions are required
    - C) Inauthentic (mass-produced, repetitive) content isn't monetised
    - D) Shorts are paid per view

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** YouTube's AI disclosure rules, Meta's AI labels, India's 2026 IT rules and YouTube's inauthentic content policy (about 45 minutes)
- **Action:** make 3 AI-assisted pieces, decide and apply labels with the decision tree, and write your AI disclosure rules. It is done when your proof is saved: the 3 AI-assisted pieces (links or files), your decision-tree notes for each, and your written AI disclosure rules.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **A.** Realistic altered content about real people needs disclosure.
2. **B.** Synthetic content that appears real must be labelled; routine edits are exempt.
3. **B.** Showing something that isn't real is misleading, whatever the tool.
4. **C.** The "repetitious content" policy was renamed and clarified as inauthentic content.

Action: make 3 AI-assisted pieces, decide and apply labels with the decision tree, and write your AI disclosure rules

sections.title: Module 14: Ethics, law and safety
sections.summary: Work in a way that keeps you, your clients and the public safe: disclosure rules, copyright and music licensing, consent and personal data, honest growth, crisis handling and account security.
sections.content:
## Overview

You've followed the "rules from day 1" all course. Now you learn them properly, the way a professional must before taking paid clients: ASCI's influencer guidelines and India's endorsement rules, copyright and music, consent for photos of people (especially children) and the DPDP Rules, the platform rules against fake engagement and fake reviews, India's ban on dark patterns, and what to do when comments turn negative or an account is attacked.

The module project is your compliance and safety kit, which goes into every client agreement.

## Outcomes

By the end of this module you can:

- Apply ASCI's labels and placement rules and India's endorsement standards
- Use only licensed content and handle copyright claims correctly
- Get and keep consent for filming people and handle personal data carefully
- Explain why fake engagement, fake reviews and dark patterns harm clients, and offer alternatives
- Follow a crisis playbook and secure accounts with two-step verification and roles

## Time

About 10 hours in total: 9 hours of lessons and 1 hour for the module project. Part-time: weeks 34–36.

## Lessons

1. SMM-M14-L01: Disclosure: ASCI influencer guidelines and Indian endorsement rules (about 2 hours)
2. SMM-M14-L02: Copyright, music licensing and consent for photos of people (about 2 hours 30 minutes)
3. SMM-M14-L03: Honest growth: platform rules, fake engagement, fake reviews and dark patterns (about 2 hours)
4. SMM-M14-L04: Negative comments, crises and account security (about 2 hours 30 minutes)

## Module project: Your compliance and safety kit

1. Put in one folder (14 Compliance): the disclosure checklist and placement card, your consent form, your safe sources list, your ethics code and "no, but" replies, the response ladder, the crisis playbook template and the security audit checklist.
2. Write a one-page "how I work safely" summary you can give clients.
3. Confirm that the security audit is done for your accounts and your pilot client's.
4. Fix anything in your own past posts that the kit shows is wrong.

**Proof to record:** The 14 Compliance folder and your one-page "how I work safely" summary.

## Self-assessment rubric

Score yourself honestly after the project. Move on when no row is a 1 and at least half the rows are 3. If a row is a 1, redo that part first.

| Criterion | 1: Not yet | 2: Getting there | 3: Ready |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Disclosure | Labels missing or hidden | Labels used inconsistently | Correct labels and placement for every format, platform tools on |
| Copyright and music | Uses downloaded music and images | Mostly licensed | Only own or licensed content; claims handled correctly |
| Consent and data | Films people without asking | Asks sometimes | Consent saved for everyone; children protected; personal data hidden |
| Honest growth | Uses or would use fakes | Avoids fakes but can't explain why | Explains the rules and offers honest alternatives |
| Crisis and security | No plan; weak security | Some 2FA | Crisis playbook ready; 2FA and roles on every account |

## Short on time?

The minimum version, when PSC prep or work leaves little time:

- Learn the label placement card by heart and check 5 sponsored posts.
- Audit your last 10 posts for music and consent.
- Write your ethics code.
- Turn on two-step verification everywhere and save the backup codes.

## Revision flashcards

Cover the right-hand column, read the front, say the answer, then check. Repeat the ones you missed the next day.

| Front (say the answer aloud) | Back |
| --- | --- |
| ASCI: disclosure needed even if the review is honest? | Yes: "Disclosures are required even if the evaluations are unbiased." |
| ASCI labels? | Advertisement, Ad, Sponsored, Collaboration, Partnership, Employee, Free gift, Affiliate. |
| Label time for a 15-second-to-2-minute video? | At least a third of its length. |
| CCPA maximum fine for a misleading ad, first and repeat? | ₹10 lakh; ₹50 lakh. |
| Is giving credit a valid reason to dispute a Content ID claim? | No. |
| What do the DPDP Rules expect for children's data? | Verifiable consent from a parent or guardian. |
| Four dark patterns banned in 2023? | False urgency, bait and switch, drip pricing, disguised advertisements (13 in all). |
| First step in a crisis? | Pause scheduled posts and get the facts. |
| Hacked Instagram account? | instagram.com/hacked. |
| Cyber fraud helpline? | 1930 (24 hours). |

## Top mistakes in this module

- **Treating rules as optional for small accounts.** The rules apply to everyone, and clients rely on you to know them.
- **Giving legal advice.** Explain the rules simply; for disputes and contracts, point clients to professionals.
- **Assuming rules stay the same.** Check the official sources every few months.

sections.title: SMM-M14-L01: Disclosure: ASCI influencer guidelines and Indian endorsement rules
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Know exactly when a post must be labelled as paid or connected to a brand in India, which labels to use and where to place them in captions, Stories, videos, lives and audio, and what endorsers must check before promoting anything. **Time:** about 2 hours (45 minutes study, 1 hour 15 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Two sets of rules apply (as of October 2026)

1. **ASCI's Guidelines for Influencer Advertising in Digital Media.** The Advertising Standards Council of India is the industry's self-regulatory body. Its guidelines cover influencers, brands and agencies, and it can ask for misleading or undisclosed ads to be changed or withdrawn.
2. **The law:** the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, with the CCPA's Guidelines for Prevention of Misleading Advertisements and Endorsements (June 2022) and the Department of Consumer Affairs' "Endorsement Know-hows!" guide for celebrities, influencers and virtual influencers (January 2023).

As a marketer you are responsible too: build disclosure into every brief, caption check and client agreement.

### When must a post be labelled?

Whenever there is a **material connection** between the advertiser and the person posting: anything that could affect how much weight the audience gives the recommendation. ASCI lists payment, free products (even unsolicited ones), discounts, gifts, contest entries, trips, media barters, awards, and family or employment relationships. ASCI is explicit: **"Disclosures are required even if the evaluations are unbiased."**

No label is needed when someone shares a product they bought themselves with no connection to the brand, or for genuinely editorial content.

### Which labels?

ASCI's guidelines list: **Advertisement, Ad, Sponsored, Collaboration, Partnership, Employee, Free gift** and **Affiliate**, plus the platforms' own tools such as Instagram's **Paid partnership** label and YouTube's **Includes paid promotion**. Use one or more. The government guide adds plain terms such as "advertisement", "sponsored" and "paid promotion". Use the platform tool **as well as** your own label, not instead of it.

### Where and how to place it

| Format | ASCI's rule |
| --- | --- |
| **Captions** | Upfront and prominent, hard to miss; not buried in hashtags or links, not only in the bio, not at the end or behind "more" |
| **Stories and images without text** | The label superimposed on the picture, clearly visible |
| **Videos of 15 seconds or less** | Label on screen for at least 3 seconds |
| **Videos from 15 seconds to 2 minutes** | Label on screen for at least a third of the video |
| **Videos of 2 minutes or more** | Label on screen for the whole section where the brand is mentioned |
| **Live streams** | Announced at the start and the end (and in the caption if the video stays up) |
| **Audio** | Announced at the start and end, and before and after each break |
| **Language** | English or the language of the post, easy for an average viewer to understand |

### Before you endorse anything

- The law expects an endorsement to reflect the endorser's **genuine, reasonably current opinion**, based on **adequate information or real experience** with the product. The government guide says endorsers shouldn't promote what they haven't personally used or properly vetted.
- ASCI advises influencers to check that the advertiser can back up its claims.
- **Health and finance:** ASCI's 2023 addendum requires influencers giving technical advice on health, nutrition, banking, investment or insurance to hold relevant qualifications (for example SEBI registration for investment advice) and to show them prominently.
- **Virtual influencers** must also disclose that people are not interacting with a real human.

### What happens if rules are broken

ASCI can ask for posts to be changed or removed. Under the Consumer Protection Act the CCPA can fine a manufacturer or endorser up to **₹10 lakh** for a false or misleading advertisement, and up to **₹50 lakh** for repeat offences (check current rules). Beyond penalties, hidden ads destroy the trust that makes influencer marketing work.

## Local example

A Vatakara food creator posted a Reel about a new restaurant after a free meal for four. The caption began "Best biryani in Malabar!! 😍 #foodie #vatakara #ad" with "#ad" buried at the end of 15 hashtags, and nothing on screen. The restaurant had asked Anu (as their marketer) to arrange it.

Anu's fixes, agreed with both:

- Caption now starts: "Collaboration (free meal from @restaurant). Honest review below."
- "Free meal | Collaboration" on screen for the first 10 seconds of the 30-second Reel (more than a third).
- Instagram's Paid partnership label switched on, with the restaurant as the partner.
- "Best biryani in Malabar" changed to what the creator actually thought: "The mutton biryani was the highlight; the chicken was average."

She added a disclosure section to her influencer brief so it never happens again.

(Made-up example to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [ASCI: Guidelines for influencer advertising in digital media (PDF)](https://www.ascionline.in/social/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/ASCI-Influencer-Guidelines.pdf) | Read the full guidelines and both addenda (health and finance; disputing a connection) | 25 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |
| [ASCI: influencer advertising FAQs](https://www.ascionline.in/social/faqs/) | Re-read the FAQs on labels and placement | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |
| [PIB: Endorsement guidelines for celebrities and influencers (January 2023)](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1892527&reg=48&lang=2) | Read the government's summary of "Endorsement Know-hows!" | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |
| [PIB: Misleading advertisement guidelines and penalties (February 2023, PDF)](https://consumeraffairs.nic.in/sites/default/files/PIB1897389.pdf) | Re-read the endorser standards and the penalties | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 45 minutes).
2. Find 10 sponsored or gifted posts from Kerala creators or businesses. For each, check: is there a material connection, a correct label, correct placement for the format, and the platform tool?
3. Rewrite 3 of them so they follow the rules, keeping the creator's voice.
4. Write your disclosure checklist and the label placement card for your sales kit, and add a disclosure clause to your influencer brief template.

**Proof to record:** Your check of 10 posts, your 3 rewrites and your disclosure checklist with the placement card.

## Template: disclosure checklist

```
Is there a material connection? (payment, free product
even if unsolicited, discount, gift, trip, barter, contest
entry, award, family or employment tie) -> YES = label it
[ ] Label: Ad / Advertisement / Sponsored / Collaboration /
    Partnership / Employee / Free gift / Affiliate
[ ] Placed upfront: start of the caption, not in hashtags,
    bio, end of caption or behind "more"
[ ] Platform tool on (Paid partnership / Includes paid
    promotion) AS WELL AS the label
[ ] In the post's language, easy to understand
[ ] Claims are the endorser's genuine, current experience
[ ] Advertiser can back up every claim
[ ] Health or finance advice? Endorser has and shows the
    required qualification
[ ] Virtual influencer? Says it isn't a real human
```

## Template: label placement card

```
CAPTION:   label at the start, before "more"
STORY/IMAGE (no text): label superimposed, clearly visible
VIDEO <=15 s:      on screen at least 3 s
VIDEO 15 s-2 min:  on screen at least 1/3 of the length
VIDEO >=2 min:     on screen through the whole brand section
LIVE:      say it at the start and end (+ caption if kept)
AUDIO:     say it at the start, end, and around each break
```

## Common mistakes

- **#ad hidden among hashtags.** Labels must be upfront and hard to miss.
- **"It was free but I was honest, so no label".** ASCI: disclosure is required even if the review is unbiased.
- **Relying only on the platform tool.** Use it as well as your own clear label.
- **Endorsing products you haven't used.** Endorsements must reflect genuine experience.
- **Health or investment tips from unqualified creators.** ASCI requires relevant qualifications for technical advice.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. A creator received a free phone without being asked to post, then posts a review. Does it need a label?
    - A) No, it was unsolicited
    - B) Only if they liked it
    - C) Yes: a free product, even unsolicited, is a material connection
    - D) Only on YouTube
2. For a 90-second sponsored Reel, how long must the label stay on screen under ASCI's guidelines?
    - A) The last frame only
    - B) Only in the caption
    - C) 1 second
    - D) At least a third of the video (30 seconds)
3. Where should a caption label go?
    - A) Upfront, at the start, where it's hard to miss
    - B) In a comment
    - C) At the end, after 20 hashtags
    - D) Only in the bio
4. What must an endorsement reflect under the 2022 guidelines?
    - A) Nothing in particular
    - B) The brand's script
    - C) Whatever gets views
    - D) The endorser's genuine, reasonably current opinion based on adequate information or experience

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** ASCI's influencer guidelines and FAQs, the government endorsement guide and the misleading-ads rules (about 45 minutes)
- **Action:** check 10 sponsored posts against the rules, rewrite 3 and write your disclosure checklist. It is done when your proof is saved: your check of 10 posts, your 3 rewrites and your disclosure checklist with the placement card.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **C.** ASCI includes unsolicited free products.
2. **D.** Videos from 15 seconds to 2 minutes need the label for at least a third of their length.
3. **A.** Labels must not be buried or hidden behind "more".
4. **D.** That is the standard the CCPA guidelines set.

sections.title: SMM-M14-L02: Copyright, music licensing and consent for photos of people
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Use only content you have the right to use, handle copyright claims correctly, get and keep consent before filming people (especially children), and handle customers' personal data the way Indian law expects. **Time:** about 2 hours 30 minutes (45 minutes study, 1 hour 45 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### Copyright in plain words

In India, the Copyright Act, 1957 protects original creative work: photos, videos, music, recordings, writing, designs. The creator (or the person they work for, in some cases) owns it, and using it without permission is infringement. Section 52 of the Act lists the acts that are **not** infringement, such as limited fair dealing for criticism, review or reporting current events, but these exceptions are narrow and don't cover using a popular film song as background music in a shop's Reel.

Three myths to drop:

- **"I gave credit."** Credit is not permission. YouTube's own help page says giving credit isn't a valid reason to dispute a copyright claim.
- **"It was on Google, so it's free."** Almost everything online belongs to someone.
- **"It's only 10 seconds."** There is no safe length.

### How platforms enforce it (as of October 2026)

- **YouTube** uses **Content ID**: a claim can block your video, send its earnings to the owner or track it. A **copyright strike** is more serious: it follows a valid removal request and counts against your channel. Shorts over a minute with an active claim are blocked worldwide. Dispute a claim only if you have all the rights, the use is a genuine exception, or the claim is a mistake; abusing disputes can bring penalties, and a valid removal request leads to the video being removed and a strike.
- **Instagram and Facebook** can mute audio, block or remove content that uses music without a licence. Music added from the app's own library is licensed for use in the app, but business accounts may have a more limited library.

### Safe sources

- Your own photos, videos and voice
- Music and sounds added inside Instagram, Facebook or YouTube from their libraries
- The **YouTube Audio Library**: tracks with a Creative Commons licence need the artist credited in the description; you can filter for "Attribution not required"
- Canva's free media, used within its licence (not in logos or trademarks)
- Work by local musicians, photographers or artists with **written permission**

For clients, also get written permission for their logo, photos and any content they send you, and agree who owns the content you make for them (Module 15).

### Consent before you film or post people

- **Ask first** and save the yes: a consent note, a WhatsApp message or a short recorded "yes" (SMM-M04-L03 has a form).
- **Children:** ask a parent or guardian, and think twice even then. Avoid names, schools and locations of children.
- **Staff and customers in a client's shop:** the business should ask them, and you should check.
- **Sensitive places and moments:** hospitals, funerals, places of worship, accidents: don't film without clear permission, and often not at all.
- **Let people change their minds:** remove a post promptly if someone asks.

### Customers' personal data

Phone numbers, addresses, chats and photos of customers are personal data. India's Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (with obligations phased in over 18 months) expect consent that is clear and informed, a notice saying what the data is for, the right to withdraw consent at any time, and verifiable consent from a parent or guardian for children's data. Penalties for businesses can be very large, up to ₹250 crore for security failures (check current rules). In practice for you:

- Never post screenshots of chats or reviews without hiding names and numbers, unless the customer agreed.
- Use customer lists only for the purpose people agreed to (for example, order updates), and let them stop.
- Don't paste customer data into AI tools or share it with anyone else.

## Local example

Anu's early Short used 40 seconds of a popular Malayalam film song she had downloaded. It got a Content ID claim and the ad money went to the music label. A follower also messaged: "Please remove my daughter from your Onam video."

What she did:

1. Removed the film song in YouTube Studio's editor and replaced it with a track from the YouTube Audio Library ("Attribution not required"). The claim was released.
2. Deleted the Onam video the same day, apologised, and re-posted a version without the child.
3. Audited her last 20 posts: two more had downloaded songs (fixed), one had a customer's phone number visible in a screenshot (blurred).
4. Started using a consent note for every person she films, and a rule: no children unless it's her own family, with a parent's OK.

(Made-up example to show the method.)

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [India Code: The Copyright Act, 1957 (PDF)](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/1367/1/a195714.pdf) | Open the Act and read the arrangement of sections, including the title of section 52 | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |
| [YouTube Help: Dispute a Content ID claim (claims and strikes)](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/2797454) | Read claims vs strikes and when you may dispute | 10 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [YouTube Help: Use music and sound effects from the Audio Library](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/3376882) | Re-read how to use and credit Audio Library tracks | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Instagram Help: Access to the licensed music library](https://help.instagram.com/ipad-app/402084904469945) | Open Instagram's page on the licensed music library | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 (page title checked) |
| [Canva Free Media License](https://www.canva.com/policies/free-media) | Re-read the limits of the free licence | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [PIB: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 explained (PDF)](https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/nov/doc20251117695301.pdf) | Read the summary of consent, withdrawal, children's data and penalties | 15 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 45 minutes).
2. Audit your last 20 posts (and your pilot client's posts) with the rights and consent sheet: music source, images, people shown, consent saved, personal data visible.
3. Fix every problem you find: replace music, remove or blur, ask for missing consent or take the post down.
4. Make your consent form (English and Malayalam) and a list of your safe music and image sources.
5. Write two sentences for clients explaining why you won't use film songs or Google images in their posts.

**Proof to record:** Your completed audit sheet with the fixes made, your consent form and your safe sources list.

## Template: rights and consent audit sheet

```csv
Post link,Date,Music source (own/app library/Audio Library/other),Images (own/Canva free/other),People shown,Consent saved (Y/N/NA),Children shown (Y/N) with parent OK,Personal data visible (Y/N),Problem,Fix done
```

## Template: photo and video consent form (English and Malayalam)

```
CONSENT TO BE FILMED OR PHOTOGRAPHED
I, ______________, agree that ______________ (page or
business) may film or photograph me and post it on
Instagram, YouTube, Facebook and WhatsApp.
[ ] Face shown  [ ] Voice only  [ ] Hands only
I can ask for it to be removed at any time by messaging ____.
For a child: parent or guardian ______________ agrees.
Signature or recorded yes: ________  Date: ________

ചിത്രീകരണത്തിനുള്ള സമ്മതം
______________ (പേജ്/ബിസിനസ്) എന്നെ ചിത്രീകരിച്ച്
ഇൻസ്റ്റഗ്രാം, യൂട്യൂബ്, ഫേസ്ബുക്ക്, വാട്സാപ്പ് എന്നിവയിൽ പോസ്റ്റ്
ചെയ്യുന്നതിന് ഞാൻ ______________ സമ്മതിക്കുന്നു.
എപ്പോൾ വേണമെങ്കിലും ____ ൽ മെസ്സേജ് ചെയ്ത് നീക്കം ചെയ്യാൻ ആവശ്യപ്പെടാം.
കുട്ടിയാണെങ്കിൽ രക്ഷിതാവിന്റെ സമ്മതം: ______________
```

## Template: safe sources list

```
MUSIC: in-app libraries (Instagram, Facebook, YouTube);
  YouTube Audio Library ("Attribution not required" or
  credit added); local musician ____ (written permission)
IMAGES: my own; client's own (written permission); Canva
  free media (not in logos)
NEVER: film songs, songs downloaded from YouTube, Google
  Images, other creators' videos, "no copyright" uploads
  from unknown channels
```

## Common mistakes

- **"Credit to the owner" as a licence.** Credit isn't permission.
- **Disputing claims you know are valid.** Abuse of disputes can bring penalties and strikes.
- **Filming children at events.** Ask a parent, avoid identifying details, or leave them out.
- **Posting chat screenshots with numbers.** Hide names and numbers, or get permission.
- **Keeping posts someone asked you to remove.** Remove them promptly and apologise.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. You used a film song and credited the composer. Is that a valid reason to dispute a Content ID claim?
    - A) No: YouTube says giving credit isn't a valid reason
    - B) Yes
    - C) Only for Shorts
    - D) Only in Malayalam
2. What is the difference between a Content ID claim and a copyright strike?
    - A) None
    - B) Claims delete your channel
    - C) Strikes are good
    - D) A claim attaches to a video; a strike follows a valid removal request and counts against the channel
3. A parent asks you to remove a video showing their child. What do you do?
    - A) Remove it promptly and apologise
    - B) Ask them to pay
    - C) Blur it next month
    - D) Ignore it
4. What do the DPDP Rules, 2025 expect for consent?
    - A) Consent only for adults over 60
    - B) Consent only on paper
    - C) Nothing
    - D) Clear, informed consent with a notice of purpose, and the right to withdraw

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** The Copyright Act, YouTube's claims and Audio Library rules, Instagram's music page, Canva's licence and the DPDP Rules summary (about 45 minutes)
- **Action:** audit 20 posts for rights, consent and personal data, fix every problem and make your consent form. It is done when your proof is saved: your completed audit sheet with the fixes made, your consent form and your safe sources list.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **A.** Credit is not permission.
2. **D.** Strikes are penalties on the channel; claims are about the video.
3. **A.** Consent can be withdrawn, and children need extra care.
4. **D.** That is the summary in the government explainer.

sections.title: SMM-M14-L03: Honest growth: platform rules, fake engagement, fake reviews and dark patterns
sections.summary: **Outcome:** Know the main platform rules that protect your accounts, explain to clients why fake followers, fake reviews, engagement bait and dark patterns are harmful and often against the law, and offer honest alternatives. **Time:** about 2 hours (35 minutes study, 1 hour 25 minutes action).
sections.content:
## Core lesson

### The rules that keep accounts alive (as of October 2026)

| Platform rule | What it covers | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Community Guidelines and Standards | What can't be posted at all | Meta's Community Standards; YouTube's Community Guidelines |
| Recommendation Guidelines | What can stay up but won't be recommended to non-followers | Instagram's Account Status |
| Inauthentic behaviour and spam | Fake accounts, coordinated fakery, misleading pages | Meta's Community Standards |
| Fake engagement | Buying or faking views, likes, subscribers, comments; sub4sub; incentivised engagement | YouTube's fake engagement policy |
| Fake and incentivised reviews | Reviews that aren't genuine experiences; reviews in exchange for benefits | Google Maps content policies |
| Monetisation policies | Inauthentic, mass-produced and reused content doesn't earn | YouTube Partner Program policies |
| Engagement bait | Posts that ask for likes, comments, shares, tags or votes just for reach | Meta's content distribution guidelines |

### Fake followers and fake engagement

Buying followers, likes or views is cheap and tempting. It is also a bad deal:

- **It breaks the rules.** YouTube removes content and can terminate channels for fake engagement; artificial traffic isn't counted. Instagram removes inauthentic likes, follows and comments made through third-party growth apps and warns the accounts using them.
- **It ruins your numbers.** Fake followers never watch, so your views per follower and engagement fall, and recommendations get harder.
- **It deceives clients.** Selling a business "10,000 followers" that will never buy anything is dishonest, and showing inflated numbers to win clients can be a misleading claim.

### Fake reviews

Reviews written by owners, staff, family or paid strangers, or swapped between businesses, break Google's policies and can be removed, with the profile restricted. India's online review standard IS 19000:2022 expects paid reviews to be disclosed and bars reviews bought or written by people employed for that purpose. Fake testimonials in ads can also be misleading advertising under the Consumer Protection Act.

### Engagement bait and fake contests

"Like if you love Kerala", "Comment YES for part 2", "Tag 5 friends to win" ask for empty actions. Meta demotes engagement bait. If a client wants a giveaway, keep it honest: clear written terms, a real prize, a fair way to choose winners, no payment to enter, and no "tag 10 friends" requirement. Check the platform's promotion rules before you run one.

### Dark patterns

In November 2023 India's Central Consumer Protection Authority issued guidelines banning **13 dark patterns**: design and wording tricks that push people into choices they didn't intend. They include **false urgency** (fake countdowns and "only 2 left"), **bait and switch** (advertising one thing and delivering another), **drip pricing** (hiding part of the price until the end) and **disguised advertisements** (ads made to look like normal content). Social media marketers meet these every day; avoid them all (check current rules).

### Your answer to a client who asks for shortcuts

Say no to the shortcut and offer the honest alternative: "Buying followers would hurt your reach and could get the account restricted. Instead, let's run a collab with a local food page and a small, targeted ad to real people within 5 km." Clients respect a marketer who protects their business.

## Local example

Before Onam, the owner of a new textile shop in Kuttiady asked Anu three things (made-up example):

1. "Can you get us 5,000 followers this week? My cousin knows a site."
2. "Write ten 5-star Google reviews from different names."
3. "Put 'Only 3 sarees left!' on every post so people hurry."

Her replies:

1. "Bought followers don't come to the shop, and Instagram removes fake follows from such apps. Let's do a Collab Reel with two local pages and a ₹1,000 ad to women within 8 km."
2. "Fake reviews break Google's rules and can get the profile restricted. Let's put a QR review card at the billing counter and ask every customer this week."
3. "If it isn't true, it's false urgency, which India banned in 2023. We can say 'Onam collection: new stock every Friday', which is true."

The owner agreed to all three alternatives. By Onam the shop had 36 genuine new reviews.

## Free resources

| Resource | What to study | Time | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [YouTube Help: Fake engagement policy](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/3399767) | Re-read the fake engagement policy and its penalties | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [Instagram Help: Avoid apps that offer likes and followers](https://help.instagram.com/263751177667145/) | Open Instagram's page on apps that offer likes and followers | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 (page title checked) |
| [Meta Community Standards: Inauthentic behavior](https://transparency.meta.com/policies/community-standards/inauthentic-behavior/) | Open Meta's inauthentic behaviour standard | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25 (page title checked) |
| [Maps content policy: Fake engagement](https://support.google.com/contributionpolicy/answer/11414422) | Re-read Google's fake engagement policy | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 |
| [PIB: Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023](https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1983994) | Re-read the dark patterns press release | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |
| [Meta Transparency Center: Engagement bait (content distribution guidelines)](https://transparency.meta.com/features/approach-to-ranking/content-distribution-guidelines/engagement-bait/) | Re-open the engagement bait page | 3 min | verified 2026-10-25 (page title checked) |
| [YouTube Help: Channel monetization policies (inauthentic and reused content)](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/1311392) | Re-read the inauthentic and reused content rules | 5 min | verified 2026-10-25; check current rules |

## Action task

1. Study the resources (about 30 minutes).
2. Check your own accounts: Instagram Account Status and YouTube Studio for any warnings or limits. Screenshot them.
3. Write your personal ethics code: at least 8 things you will always do and never do as a marketer.
4. Write "no, but" replies to five unethical requests a client might make (followers, reviews, fake urgency, hidden ads, copied content).
5. Find one example of a dark pattern or engagement bait in a real post or ad, and write how you'd fix it.

**Proof to record:** Your account status screenshots, your ethics code, your five "no, but" replies and your dark pattern fix.

## Template: my ethics code

```
I ALWAYS
1. use real numbers, and say when results are unclear
2. disclose paid, gifted and affiliate content clearly
3. get consent before filming people, and parents' OK
4. use music and images I have the right to use
5. tell clients when an idea breaks rules or law
I NEVER
6. buy followers, likes, views or reviews
7. write or arrange fake reviews or testimonials
8. use false urgency, hidden prices or disguised ads
9. copy other creators' content
10. ask for or keep clients' passwords
```

## Template: "no, but" replies

```
FOLLOWERS: "Bought followers won't buy from you and can
  get the account restricted. Instead: ________."
REVIEWS: "Fake reviews break Google's rules. Instead:
  a QR review card and asking every customer."
URGENCY: "If it isn't true it's false urgency, banned in
  2023. Instead: a real deadline such as ________."
HIDDEN ADS: "The law and ASCI need a clear label. It
  won't hurt: honest labels build trust."
COPYING: "Copied videos get less reach and can bring
  claims. Let's make our own version of the idea."
```

## Common mistakes

- **Thinking small fakery is harmless.** Platforms detect patterns; clients lose trust when they find out.
- **Agreeing to bad requests to keep a client.** Say no with an honest alternative; good clients stay.
- **"Tag 5 friends to win" giveaways.** That is engagement bait. Use clear terms and real entries.
- **Fake countdowns and "only 2 left".** False urgency is a banned dark pattern.

## Quiz

Answer without looking back. The answers are at the bottom of this page.

1. What does YouTube do with artificial traffic?
    - A) Pays for it
    - B) Doesn't count it, and it can lead to strikes
    - C) Ignores it with no effect
    - D) Counts it double
2. Which is a dark pattern banned in India in 2023?
    - A) A real deadline
    - B) False urgency, such as a fake countdown
    - C) Showing the full price upfront
    - D) A clear Ad label
3. A client asks you to write reviews under different names. What do you do?
    - A) Write them carefully
    - B) Refuse and suggest asking real customers with a QR card
    - C) Ask family to write them
    - D) Buy them
4. Why do bought followers hurt an account's reach?
    - A) They change the bio
    - B) They don't
    - C) They post spam
    - D) They never watch, so engagement and views per follower fall

## Progress checklist

Tick these under **Your tasks** at the top of this page:

- **Study:** Platform rules on fake engagement, inauthentic behaviour, reviews, engagement bait and monetisation, and India's dark patterns guidelines (about 30 minutes)
- **Action:** check your account status, write your ethics code and "no, but" replies, and fix a real dark pattern example. It is done when your proof is saved: your account status screenshots, your ethics code, your five "no, but" replies and your dark pattern fix.
- **Quiz:** at least 3 right, or re-read the core lesson and try again.

## Answers

1. **B.** YouTube says artificial traffic isn't counted and can bring strikes.
2. **B.** The CCPA's guidelines list false urgency among 13 dark patterns.
3. **B.** Fake reviews break Google's policies and mislead customers.
4. **D.** The system sees a large audience that ignores the posts.

Action: check your account status, write your ethics code and "no, but" replies, and fix a real dark pattern example
